Precautions_Contraindications: Rx - specialist supervision required; Do not abruptly stop antiviral therapy (causes severe acute hepatitis flare); Renal function and bone density monitoring with Tenofovir; Max paracetamol 2000 mg/24h; Avoid NSAIDs and alcohol
Home_Care_Advice: Complete lifelong adherence to antivirals; Zero alcohol intake; Vaccinate family members/close contacts against Hepatitis B; Do not share razors/needles
Lab_Investigations: HBsAg; HBeAg; HBV DNA Quantitative Real-Time PCR; Liver Function Test; USG Abdomen; FibroScan; Alpha-Fetoprotein (AFP)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Decompensation signs (ascites, jaundice, variceal bleeding, encephalopathy); Acute flare up with severe jaundice and vomiting

Common_Names_Hindi: Hepatitis C; Hepatitis C ka infection
Primary_Symptoms: Often asymptomatic for decades; Chronic fatigue; Myalgia; Arthralgia; Mild RUQ pain
Secondary_Symptoms: Jaundice (late stage); Anorexia; Weight loss; Cirrhosis complications
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Anti-HCV blood test positive aaya hai?; 2. Kabhi blood transfusion ya surgery hui hai?; 3. Thakan rehti hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Sofosbuvir + Velpatasvir (Direct-Acting Antiviral combination)
Supportive_Medicines: Ursodeoxycholic Acid 300 mg BD; Multivitamins
Precautions_Contraindications: Rx - specialist supervision required; Direct-Acting Antivirals cure >95% of cases; Test for HBV co-infection before starting (risk of HBV reactivation); Max paracetamol 2000 mg/24h; Avoid NSAIDs and alcohol
Home_Care_Advice: Strict daily adherence to 12-week course without missing doses; Total alcohol abstinence; Avoid sharing personal care items (razors, toothbrushes)
Lab_Investigations: Anti-HCV Antibody; HCV RNA Quantitative PCR; HCV Genotype; Liver Function Test; USG Abdomen; FibroScan
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Signs of liver decompensation (ascites, jaundice, bleeding, encephalopathy); Suspected hepatocellular carcinoma

Primary_Symptoms: Acute jaundice (scleral icterus & dark urine); Severe anorexia; Nausea; Vomiting; RUQ pain
Secondary_Symptoms: Fever; Malaise; Pruritus; Clay-colored stools; Hepatomegaly
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Peeli aankhein aur kaala/peela peshab hai?; 2. Khana dekhkar ulti aati hai?; 3. Dushit paani ya bahar ka food khaya tha?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Symptomatic supportive treatment - NO SPECIFIC ANTIVIRAL NEEDED
Supportive_Medicines: Ondansetron 4 mg SOS; B-complex vitamins; Hydration (ORS)
Max_Safe_Limit_24h: Max paracetamol dose is 2000 mg/24h in all liver conditions
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; HIGH MORTALITY IN PREGNANT WOMEN (up to 20-25% risk of fulminant hepatic failure in 3rd trimester); Max paracetamol 2000 mg/24h; Avoid NSAIDs and alcohol
Home_Care_Advice: Complete physical bed rest; High carbohydrate, low-fat diet; Drink boiled water; Absolute avoidance of alcohol and hepatotoxic drugs
Lab_Investigations: IgM Anti-HEV Antibody; Liver Function Test (SGOT/SGPT often >1000 U/L, High Bilirubin); PT/INR; USG Abdomen
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Any pregnant woman with Hepatitis E (Urgent admission); Drowsiness/confusion (encephalopathy); Bleeding manifestations; Persistent severe vomiting

Common_Names_Hindi: Dawai se dast; Antibiotic Diarrhea / C. difficile
Primary_Symptoms: Watery loose stools developing during or after antibiotic course; Abdominal cramps
Secondary_Symptoms: Low fever; Nausea; Bloating; Leukocytosis; Mucus in stool
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Koi antibiotic (Cefixime, Augmentin, Clindamycin) chal rahi hai?; 2. Din me kitni baar loose motion ho raha hai?; 3. Pet me marod hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Saccharomyces boulardii OR Oral Vancomycin / Metronidazole (if C. difficile severe)
Supportive_Medicines: Oral Rehydration Salts (ORS); Zinc 20 mg OD; Discontinue offending antibiotic if possible
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; STOP offending broad-spectrum antibiotic if clinically safe; Do NOT give anti-motility agents (Loperamide) in C. difficile colitis (risk of toxic megacolon)
Home_Care_Advice: Aggressive hydration with ORS; Probiotics taken 2 hours apart from antibiotics; Avoid dairy and spicy foods short-term
Lab_Investigations: Stool C. difficile Toxin A & B ELISA; Stool Routine & Microscopy; CBC; Serum Electrolytes
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Severe profuse watery diarrhea (>10/day); High fever; Severe abdominal distension and pain; Blood in stool; Dehydration signs

Primary_Symptoms: Fatigue; Anorexia; Mild jaundice; Palmar erythema; Spider angiomas; Distended abdominal veins
Secondary_Symptoms: Splenomegaly; Mild leg edema; Easy bruising; Weight loss; Parotid enlargement
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Ultrasound me liver cirrhotic/nodular aaya hai?; 2. Sharab ya Hepatitis ki purani history hai?; 3. Pairo me sujan ya thakan rehti hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Ursodeoxycholic Acid + Propranolol (if varices present)
Supportive_Medicines: Spironolactone 100 mg OD (if mild fluid retention); B-complex; Multivitamins; Lactulose syrup
Precautions_Contraindications: Rx - specialist supervision required; Max paracetamol limit is 2000 mg/24h; NSAIDs are STRICTLY CONTRAINDICATED (cause acute renal failure/hepatorenal syndrome); Absolute alcohol cessation
Home_Care_Advice: TOTAL ABSTINENCE FROM ALCOHOL; Low-sodium diet (<2g salt/day); High protein diet (unless encephalopathic); Vaccinate against Hepatitis A, B, and Pneumococcus
Lab_Investigations: Liver Function Test; Serum Albumin; PT/INR; USG Abdomen with Doppler; Upper GI Endoscopy (screen for esophageal varices); FibroScan
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Decompensation flare: Hematemesis/Melena; Ascites (abdominal swelling); Confusion (encephalopathy); Spontaneous Bacterial Peritonitis (fever + pain)

Primary_Symptoms: Hematemesis (bright red blood or coffee-ground vomitus); Melena (black tarry sticky foul stool)
Secondary_Symptoms: Postural dizziness; Syncope; Tachycardia; Hypotension; Severe pallor; Cold clammy skin
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Khoon ki ulti hui hai ya kaala latrine aaya hai?; 2. Chakkar aa rahe hain ya behoshi hui hai?; 3. NSAID painkiller, alcohol, ya liver disease ki history hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: None - emergency hospital referral
Popular_Indian_Brands: Injection Pantoprazole 80 mg bolus; Injection Terlipressin 2 mg IV; Injection Octreotide
Supportive_Medicines: Emergency Upper GI Endoscopy (Banding/Sclerotherapy/Cautery); IV Pantoprazole infusion; Blood transfusion; IV Terlipressin (for varices)
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Life-threatening emergency; Do NOT give home painkillers, NSAIDs, laxatives, or antacids; Strict Nil By Mouth (NPO)
Home_Care_Advice: Keep patient strictly Nil By Mouth (NPO); Absolute bed rest in flat position with legs elevated; Immediate emergency transfer to hospital with ICU and endoscopy facilities
Lab_Investigations: Emergent Upper GI Endoscopy (within 12-24h); Complete Blood Count; PT/INR; Blood Grouping & Cross-matching; RFT/LFT
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Medical emergency - Immediate ER referral; Continuous hematemesis; Hemodynamic instability/Shock; Altered consciousness

Primary_Symptoms: Severe crampy paroxysmal abdominal pain; Complete inability to pass gas or stool (obstipation)
Secondary_Symptoms: Bilious or feculent vomiting; Severe abdominal distension; High-pitched tinkling bowel sounds
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Pet fula hua hai aur gas ya latrine bilkul nahi ho rahi?; 2. Peeli/hali ya saday khane ki ulti ho rahi hai?; 3. Pehle koi pet ki surgery hui thi?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: None - emergency hospital referral
Popular_Indian_Brands: Injection Pantoprazole; IV Fluids (Ringer Lactate); Injection Tramadol
Supportive_Medicines: Nasogastric (NG) tube decompression; IV Fluid resuscitation; Emergency Exploratory Laparotomy / Adhesiolysis
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Life-threatening emergency; Do NOT give home laxatives, purgatives, antacids, or painkillers; Strict Nil By Mouth (NPO)
Home_Care_Advice: Keep patient strictly Nil By Mouth (NPO); Immediate emergency transfer to surgical hospital; Do NOT give oral laxatives or water while reaching hospital
Lab_Investigations: Plain X-ray Abdomen Erect & Supine (Multiple air-fluid levels, dilated bowel loops); Contrast CT Abdomen; CBC; Electrolytes; RFT
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Medical emergency - Immediate ER referral; Strangulated/gangrenous bowel signs (fever, severe peritonitis, shock); Feculent vomiting

Primary_Symptoms: Chronic abdominal pain (RLQ/periumbilical); Alternating diarrhea and constipation; Unexplained weight loss
Secondary_Symptoms: Low-grade evening fever; Night sweats; Anorexia; Abdominal mass; Ascites; Anemia
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Pet me dard aur weight loss mahino se hai?; 2. Shaam ko halka bukhar aur raat me pasiina aata hai?; 3. Aant me sujan ya ganth batayi hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Rx - NTEP regimen under doctor supervision
Duration_Days: 6 months minimum (2 months Intensive HRZE + 4 months Continuation HRE)
Supportive_Medicines: Pyridoxine (Vitamin B6) 10-20 mg daily; High protein nutritional supplements; Antispasmodics
Precautions_Contraindications: Rx - specialist supervision required; Treatment follows national NTEP/DOTS programme under doctor supervision; Do not start self-medication; Hepatotoxicity risk; Max paracetamol 2000 mg/24h; Avoid NSAIDs
Home_Care_Advice: Strict daily compliance with anti-TB drugs without missing doses; High calorie high protein diet; Rest; Hydration
Lab_Investigations: Colonoscopy with ileocecal biopsy (Caseating granulomas, AFB positive); GeneXpert on biopsy tissue; CT Abdomen (ileocecal thickening, necrotic lymph nodes); Mantoux test; ESR
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Acute intestinal obstruction (vomiting, no gas/stool); Intestinal perforation (severe sudden pain, rigidity); Massive GI bleeding; Severe drug-induced jaundice

Primary_Symptoms: Annular erythematous scaly plaques with central clearing; Active advancing scaly border; Severe pruritus
Secondary_Symptoms: Post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation; Mild burning sensation; Erythema; Scaling
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Lal gol daag/chhalla bana hai jiske kinaro par khujli zyada hai?; 2. Kya aapne gharelu steroid cream (Clobetasol/Betnovate) lagai hai?; 3. Kitne din se hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Terbinafine 1% cream OR Clotrimazole 1% cream
Supportive_Medicines: Levocetirizine 5 mg OD at bedtime for itching; Ketoconazole soap
Precautions_Contraindications: Do NOT use steroid or steroid-combination creams (e.g. clobetasol, betamethasone combos) - they worsen fungal infections; Incomplete courses cause recurrence and resistance; Oral antifungals Rx only with liver caution
Home_Care_Advice: Keep skin folds dry and clean; Wear loose cotton clothing; Bathe twice daily; Do not share towels, combs, or bedsheets
Lab_Investigations: Skin scraping for KOH wet mount (fungal hyphae inspection); Fungal culture if refractory
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Rapidly spreading lesion; Widespread secondary bacterial infection with pus; Severe painful swelling

Primary_Symptoms: Pruritic erythematous rash in groin and inner thighs; Sharply demarcated scaly active border
Secondary_Symptoms: Chafing; Burning sensation; Maceration; Dark skin patches
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Jangho aur groin ke paas lal khujli waala daag hai?; 2. Pasiina aane par khujli badhti hai?; 3. Koi combination steroid cream lagai hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Terbinafine 1% cream OR Sertaconazole 2% cream
Supportive_Medicines: Levocetirizine 5 mg OD at bedtime; Clotrimazole dusting powder
Precautions_Contraindications: Do NOT use steroid or steroid-combination creams (e.g. clobetasol, betamethasone combos) - they worsen fungal infections; Incomplete courses cause recurrence and resistance; Avoid applying potent steroids in groin area
Home_Care_Advice: Wear loose-fitting, breathable cotton underwear; Keep groin area completely dry after bath; Use antifungal dusting powder; Avoid tight jeans
Lab_Investigations: Skin scraping for KOH preparation; Blood sugar estimation (rule out diabetes mellitus)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Secondary severe bacterial infection with foul discharge; Spreading to scrotum/penis with pain; Severe erosive skin breakdown

Primary_Symptoms: Interdigital scaling, erythema, and maceration between toes; Intense itching; Malodor
Secondary_Symptoms: Fissuring; Scaling on soles (moccasin distribution); Vesicles; Burning pain
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Pairo ki ungliyo ke beech me khal chhil rahi hai aur khujli hai?; 2. Pairo se badboo aati hai?; 3. Gille joote/moze pehente hain?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Terbinafine 1% cream OR Clotrimazole 1% cream
Supportive_Medicines: Levocetirizine 5 mg OD for itching; Antifungal foot powder
Precautions_Contraindications: Do NOT use steroid or steroid-combination creams (e.g. clobetasol, betamethasone combos) - they worsen fungal infections; Incomplete courses cause recurrence and resistance; Caution in diabetic foot
Home_Care_Advice: Dry feet thoroughly between toes after washing; Wear clean cotton socks daily; Change wet footwear immediately; Use open sandals when possible
Lab_Investigations: Skin scraping for KOH mount; Fasting blood glucose (for diabetic screening)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Spreading cellulitis of leg; Severe painful bullae/blisters; Non-healing painful ulcer in diabetic patient

Primary_Symptoms: Hypopigmented or hyperpigmented fine scaly macules on chest, back, and neck; Mild pruritus
Secondary_Symptoms: Fine branny scaling (fine dust-like scale on scraping); Patchy appearance; Increased visibility after sun exposure
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Chhati ya pitth par safed ya bhure chote-chote daag hain?; 2. Pasiina aane par halki khujli hoti hai?; 3. Dhoop me jaane par daag zyada dikhte hain?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Ketoconazole 2% shampoo / lotion OR Clotrimazole 1% cream
Dosage_Frequency: Apply on wet affected skin, leave for 5-10 mins, rinse off daily
Supportive_Medicines: Fluconazole 150 mg weekly (oral Rx strictly under doctor); Levocetirizine 5 mg SOS
Precautions_Contraindications: Do NOT use steroid or steroid-combination creams - they worsen fungal infections; Incomplete courses cause recurrence; Hypopigmentation may persist for weeks post cure
Home_Care_Advice: Wash affected skin with ketoconazole lotion daily; Wear loose cotton clothes; Avoid heavy oils/cocoa butter on chest and back
Lab_Investigations: KOH mount of skin scrapings (classic 'spaghetti and meatballs' hyphae/spores appearance)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Lesions spreading to face or >50% body surface; Failure to respond after 4 weeks of topical therapy

Common_Names_Hindi: Sir ki daad; Baalo me daad
Primary_Symptoms: Scaly patchy alopecia on scalp; Broken hair stumps ('black dot' pattern); Intense scalp itching
Secondary_Symptoms: Cervical lymphadenopathy; Kerion (boggy inflammatory nodule); Scaling; Favus crusts
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Sir ke baal chhodkar gol chakatta bana hai aur baal toot rahe hain?; 2. Sir me sujan ya mawaad waala fopoola hai?; 3. Paspados me kisi ko hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Griseofulvin OR Terbinafine (Oral systemic therapy mandatory)
Supportive_Medicines: Ketoconazole 2% shampoo 2 times/week; Levocetirizine 5 mg OD for itching
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Oral antifungals require hepatic function monitoring; Topical antifungals alone are INEFFECTIVE for Tinea Capitis; Do NOT use steroids
Home_Care_Advice: Use ketoconazole shampoo twice weekly; Do not share hats, combs, hair clips, or pillows; Disinfect/sterilize hairbrushes and combs
Lab_Investigations: KOH examination of plucked hair shaft; Fungal culture; Wood's lamp examination
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Kerion formation (severe painful boggy swelling with pus); Widespread permanent scarring alopecia; High fever

Common_Names_Hindi: Naakhun me fungus; Naakhun kharab hona
Primary_Symptoms: Distal subungual hyperkeratosis; Yellow-brown discoloration of nail plate; Nail dystrophy; Thickening
Secondary_Symptoms: Onycholysis (nail lifting); Brittle nail edges; Subungual debris; Mild pain
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Naakhun peela/bhoora hokar mota aur khurdura ho gaya hai?; 2. Naakhun toot-toot kar jhad raha hai?; 3. Naakhun me dard hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Amorolfine 5% nail lacquer OR Terbinafine (Oral)
Dosage_Frequency: Apply lacquer once or twice weekly / 1 tab OD
Supportive_Medicines: Oral Terbinafine 250 mg OD (Rx strictly under doctor supervision); Urea 40% cream for nail softening
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Systemic oral antifungals require baseline Liver Function Test; Do NOT use steroid creams; Incomplete courses cause treatment failure
Home_Care_Advice: File down thickened nail plate before applying lacquer; Keep nails clean, short, and trimmed straight; Avoid wet footwear; Keep feet dry
Lab_Investigations: Fungal stain / KOH examination of subungual scrapings; Fungal culture; Periodic Liver Function Test
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Secondary periungual bacterial infection with severe redness/pus; Diabetic patient with dystrophy; Severe pain in nail bed

Common_Names_Hindi: Candida fungal infection; Safed fungus rash
Primary_Symptoms: Bright red erythematous moist rash with satellite pustules/papules in intertriginous folds; Intense itching/burning
Secondary_Symptoms: Maceration; Fissuring; White cheesy exudate; Tenderness
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Chamdi ki silvat (folds) me lal chamakdar rash aur chhote mawaad waale dane hain?; 2. Mawaad/jhalan jaisi khujli hoti hai?; 3. Diabetes hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Clotrimazole 1% cream OR Miconazole 2% cream
Supportive_Medicines: Levocetirizine 5 mg OD at bedtime; Clotrimazole dusting powder; Fasting blood sugar control
Precautions_Contraindications: Do NOT use steroid or steroid-combination creams - they worsen candidal infections; Incomplete courses cause recurrence and resistance; Caution in severe diabetes
Home_Care_Advice: Keep affected skin folds completely dry; Use cotton pads or antifungal powder in skin folds; Change damp clothes immediately; Maintain strict blood sugar control
Lab_Investigations: KOH preparation of skin scraping; Fasting Blood Sugar; HbA1c
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Widespread invasive candidiasis; High fever with shaking chills; Severe painful ulceration in skin folds

Common_Names_Hindi: Ragdne se rash; Sweat rash; Folds ka rash
Primary_Symptoms: Erythematous chafed skin in skin folds (axillae, inframammary, groin); Burning pain; Stinging
Secondary_Symptoms: Maceration; Mild pruritus; Foul odor; Secondary fungal/bacterial infection
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Pasiine aur ragad se skin ke folds (chhati ke niche/jangh) me lalapan aur burning hai?; 2. Skin chhili hui lagti hai?; 3. Pasiina zyada aata hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Zinc Oxide + Calamine cream / Ointment OR Clotrimazole 1% cream
Supportive_Medicines: Levocetirizine 5 mg SOS; Clotrimazole dusting powder; Absorbent barrier pads
Precautions_Contraindications: Do NOT use potent topical steroids on delicate skin folds (causes severe skin atrophy and striae); Do NOT use steroid-antifungal-antibacterial triple combination creams
Home_Care_Advice: Keep skin folds clean and dry; Wear loose, light, breathable cotton clothing; Use barrier creams or dusting powder before physical activity; Lose excess weight
Lab_Investigations: KOH preparation if fungal superinfection suspected; Blood glucose level
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Severe secondary bacterial infection with purulent discharge, warmth, and spreading cellulitis; Foul-smelling deep ulceration

Primary_Symptoms: Severe generalized nocturnal pruritus; Sinuous burrows in web spaces of fingers, wrists, flexors; Papules/vesicles
Secondary_Symptoms: Secondary excoriations; Post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation; Crusting; Secondary impetiginization
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Khujli raat ko sote samay severe badhti hai?; 2. Ungliyo ke beech, kalai aur kamar par chhote dane hain?; 3. Ghar ke doosre logo ko bhi khujli hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Permethrin 5% lotion / cream
Dosage_Frequency: Single overnight application neck-down, wash off after 8-12 hours. Repeat after 7 days
Supportive_Medicines: Levocetirizine 5 mg BD or OD for post-scabietic itch; Calamine lotion; Crotamiton 10% cream
Precautions_Contraindications: CLOSE CONTACTS AND HOUSEHOLD MEMBERS MUST BE TREATED SIMULTANEOUSLY EVEN IF ASYMPTOMATIC; Avoid contact with eyes/mucous membranes; Post-scabietic itch may persist 2-3 weeks post cure
Home_Care_Advice: Apply Permethrin neck-to-toe overnight; Wash ALL bedding, towels, and clothing used in past 4 days in HOT water (>60C) or seal in plastic bag for 7 days; Treat all family members together
Lab_Investigations: Microscopic identification of Sarcoptes scabiei mite, eggs, or scybala from skin scraping
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Norwegian/Crusted Scabies (thick hyperkeratotic crusts over large areas); Widespread secondary bacterial infection with fever and cellulitis

Common_Names_Hindi: Sir ki joo; Joo; Head Lice
Primary_Symptoms: Intense scalp pruritus, especially occipital and postauricular regions; Visible live lice or nits (eggs) attached to hair shafts
Secondary_Symptoms: Excoriations; Secondary impetigo; Cervical lymphadenopathy; Scalp irritability
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Sir me khujli hoti hai aur chhote safed aande (nits) baalo par chipke hain?; 2. Joo chalte hue dikhti hain?; 3. School ya ghar me kisi aur ko bhi joo hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Permethrin 1% lotion / shampoo OR Ivermectin 0.5% lotion
Dosage_Frequency: Apply on damp scalp/hair, leave for 10 minutes, then rinse completely. Repeat after 7 days
Supportive_Medicines: Wet combing with fine-toothed nit comb; Cetirizine 5 mg OD for itching
Precautions_Contraindications: CLOSE CONTACTS AND HOUSEHOLD MEMBERS MUST BE TREATED TOGETHER; Avoid getting lotion into eyes; Repeat treatment at Day 7 is essential to kill newly hatched nits
Home_Care_Advice: Apply Permethrin lotion to scalp/hair for 10 mins; Use fine-toothed nit comb on wet hair daily; Wash combs, brushes, pillowcases, and caps in hot water (>60C)
Lab_Investigations: Visual inspection under bright light or magnifying glass for live lice and nits
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Widespread secondary bacterial infection of scalp with purulent crusting and painful neck glands; Severe allergic dermatitis

Primary_Symptoms: Fragile vesicles/bullae that rupture leaving characteristic honey-colored adherent crusts; Localized pain/itching
Secondary_Symptoms: Erythematous base; Regional lymphadenopathy; Satellite lesions; Mild burning
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Chehre ya naak ke paas fopoole phat kar shahad (honey) jaisi patti banayi hai?; 2. Peela mawaad nikalta hai?; 3. Chhota bachha hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Mupirocin 2% ointment OR Fusidic Acid 2% cream
Supportive_Medicines: Amoxicillin-Clavulanic Acid 625 mg BD (Oral Rx if lesions widespread); Paracetamol 500 mg SOS; Antiseptic wash
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Oral antibiotics required if widespread bullous impetigo; Do NOT pick or scratch crusts to prevent autoinoculation
Home_Care_Advice: Soak and gently remove honey-colored crusts with warm water; Apply Mupirocin ointment gently 3 times daily; Wash hands frequently; Keep child's towels separate
Lab_Investigations: Gram stain and wound swab culture for Staphylococcus aureus and Streptococcus pyogenes
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Widespread bullous impetigo; High fever with lethargy; Ecthyma (deep ulcerative impetigo); Hematuria/edema post infection (Post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis)

Common_Names_Hindi: Baaltor ki sujan; Folliculitis; Hair pore infection
Primary_Symptoms: Small perifollicular pustules surrounded by an erythematous halo; Mild localized pain and pruritus
Secondary_Symptoms: Hair shaft extending through center of pustule; Mild tenderness; Exudate
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Baal ke muuh par chhote peele mawaad waale dane hain?; 2. Khujli ya halka dard hota hai?; 3. Shave karne ya wax karne ke baad hua hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Clindamycin 1% gel OR Mupirocin 2% ointment
Popular_Indian_Brands: Clinka Gel; Cleocin T; T-Bact Ointment
Supportive_Medicines: Cetirizine 10 mg OD for itching; Antiseptic soap (Chlorhexidine wash); Warm compress
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Avoid picking or squeezing pustules; Avoid close shaving over active lesions; Systemic antibiotics if non-responsive
Home_Care_Advice: Apply warm compresses 3-4 times daily; Wash area with antiseptic soap; Avoid tight friction-causing clothing; Use clean razors and shave in direction of hair growth
Lab_Investigations: Pustule swab culture and sensitivity if recurrent or refractory
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Progression to large painful furuncles/carbuncles; Rapidly spreading erythema; Systemic symptoms like fever and chills

Primary_Symptoms: Deep, painful, tender inflammatory nodule centered on a hair follicle; Central purulent core ('head')
Secondary_Symptoms: Erythema; Localized edema; Warmth; Fluctuance; Throbbing pain
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Baal ke paas ek hi bada, lal, aur tez dard waala gummra (boil) bana hai?; 2. Paka hua mawaad ka sar (head) dikhta hai?; 3. Pehle baal toota tha?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Mupirocin 2% ointment (topical) + Cephalexin OR Amoxicillin-Clavulanic Acid (oral)
Dosage_Frequency: TDS (8 hourly for Mupirocin) / BD (12 hourly for Augmentin)
Supportive_Medicines: Warm moist compress; Paracetamol 650 mg SOS for pain; Antiseptic wash
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; NEVER squeeze, pop, or puncture a boil (risk of bacteremia and cavernous sinus thrombosis if on face); Diabetes screening recommended
Home_Care_Advice: Apply warm moist compresses for 15-20 mins 3-4 times daily to facilitate natural drainage; Wash hands thoroughly; Cover draining boil with sterile bandage
Lab_Investigations: Pus culture and antibiotic sensitivity; Fasting blood glucose (for recurrent boils)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Boil located on danger area of face (upper lip, nose, eyelids); High fever with rigors; Multiple coalescing boils (carbuncle); Rapidly spreading erythema

Common_Names_Hindi: Bada baalttor; Carbuncle; Mawaad ki ganth
Primary_Symptoms: Large, painful, deep cluster of interconnected boils with multiple purulent discharge openings; High fever
Secondary_Symptoms: Severe throbbing pain; Erythematous indurated plaque; Malaise; Chills; Regional lymphadenopathy
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Ek hi jagah par kai saare mawaad waale baalttor aapas me mile hue hain?; 2. Bahut saare muuh se pus nikal raha hai?; 3. High fever aur severe pain hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Amoxicillin + Clavulanic Acid OR Cefadroxil (Systemic oral/IV antibiotics)
Supportive_Medicines: Surgical incision and drainage (if fluctuant); Paracetamol 650 mg SOS; Antiseptic dressing
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Requires formal medical evaluation and surgical incision/drainage; Diabetes mellitus screening mandatory
Home_Care_Advice: Warm moist compress; Do not attempt to drain at home; Maintain strict wound hygiene with sterile dressings; Rest; High fluid intake
Lab_Investigations: Pus swab culture and sensitivity; Fasting Blood Sugar & HbA1c; Complete Blood Count (Leukocytosis)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; High fever with chills; Spreading redness/cellulitis; Diabetic or immunocompromised state; Carbuncle on face or neck

Specialty_Category: General Surgery / Infectious Diseases / Emergency Medicine
Primary_Symptoms: Acute, rapidly spreading erythema, warmth, severe pain, and indurated swelling with poorly defined margins
Secondary_Symptoms: High fever with chills/rigors; Lymphangitic streaking; Regional lymphadenopathy; Bullae; Blistering
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Chamdi achanak lal, garam aur severe sooj gayi hai?; 2. Redness dhere-dhere aage phail rahi hai?; 3. Tez bukhar aur kapkapi hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: None - emergency hospital referral
Popular_Indian_Brands: Injection Cefazolin; Injection Ceftriaxone; Injection Piperacillin-Tazobactam
Supportive_Medicines: Elevate affected limb; IV Antibiotics (Ceftriaxone/Cefazolin); IV Fluids; Analgesics (Paracetamol)
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Life-threatening emergency; Do NOT apply local heat or home remedies; Elevate limb while reaching hospital
Home_Care_Advice: Keep affected limb strictly elevated above heart level; Rest motionless; Immediate emergency transfer to hospital for IV antibiotics
Lab_Investigations: CBC (Leukocytosis); Blood cultures x 2; Wound swab culture if open entry site; Serum Creatinine; USG Doppler (rule out DVT)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Medical emergency - Immediate ER referral; Rapidly expanding erythema; Bullae/Skin necrosis (Necrotizing Fasciitis); Hypotension/Shock; High fever with confusion

Primary_Symptoms: Sharply demarcated, raised, bright red, shiny, hot plaque on face or lower leg; High fever with chills
Secondary_Symptoms: Severe burning pain; Localized edema; Vesicles/bullae; Regional lymphadenopathy
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Chehre ya taang par achanak bright red, ubhari hui, shiny soojan aayi hai jiki boundary saaf dikhti hai?; 2. High fever hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Penicillin V OR Amoxicillin OR Cephalexin
Supportive_Medicines: Paracetamol 650 mg SOS for pain/fever; Cold compresses; Elevation of affected leg
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Penicillin hypersensitivity caution; Systemic oral or IV therapy mandatory; Bed rest and limb elevation essential
Home_Care_Advice: Elevate leg if lower extremity involved; Apply cool saline compresses; Rest; Strict hand washing; Complete antibiotic course fully
Lab_Investigations: CBC; Blood culture; Anti-streptolysin O (ASO) titer; Swab culture if portal of entry visible
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; High fever with rigors; Facial erysipelas near eyes; Rapidly spreading skin bullae or black discoloration; Septicemia signs

Primary_Symptoms: Painful erythematous swelling around nail fold (cuticle); Localized tenderness and throbbing pain
Secondary_Symptoms: Purulent collection (abscess) under nail fold; Nail dystrophy; Localized warmth
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Naakhun ke kinare (cuticle) par lalapan, sujan aur mawaad bhara hai?; 2. Tez tis marne waala dard hota hai?; 3. Naakhun chabane ya manicure ke baad hua hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Mupirocin 2% ointment (topical) + Augmentin OR Cephalexin (if oral needed)
Supportive_Medicines: Warm water soaks 3-4 times daily; Paracetamol 650 mg SOS; Simple incision and drainage if pus collection is large
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Do NOT attempt to pierce nail fold with unsterilized needles; Diabetes evaluation if recurrent
Home_Care_Advice: Soak finger in warm water for 15 mins 3-4 times daily; Keep finger clean and dry; Do NOT bite nails or push back cuticles forcefully
Lab_Investigations: Pus culture and sensitivity if refractory or severe
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Pus extending under nail plate (subungual abscess requiring partial nail removal); Spreading tenosynovitis of finger; High fever

Common_Names_Hindi: Mawaad ki ganth; Paka hua boil; Abscess
Primary_Symptoms: Fluctuant, tender, erythematous dermal/subcutaneous mass with purulent collection; Localized warmth
Secondary_Symptoms: Throbbing pain; Erythematous indurated surrounding skin; Fever; Lymphadenopathy
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Chamdi ke niche mawaad ki sooji hui tender ganth (fluctuant mass) hai?; 2. Dabane par andar paani/pus hilta hua lagta hai?; 3. Tez dard hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Incision and Drainage (Primary treatment) + Oral Antibiotics (Augmentin / Cephalexin)
Supportive_Medicines: Warm compress; Paracetamol 650 mg SOS; Sterile wound dressing post drainage
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Primary therapy is surgical Incision and Drainage; Antibiotics alone without drainage will NOT cure a fluctuant abscess
Home_Care_Advice: Apply warm compresses before medical evaluation; After drainage, clean wound with saline and change sterile dressing daily; Rest
Lab_Investigations: Pus swab culture and antibiotic sensitivity; Fasting Blood Sugar
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Abscess on facial danger triangle or perineum; High fever with rigors; Spreading surrounding cellulitis; Multiple recurrent abscesses

Common_Names_Hindi: Hont par fopoole; Cold Sores; Labial Herpes
Primary_Symptoms: Grouped painful small fluid-filled vesicles on an erythematous base on lips/vermilion border; Tingling/burning prodrome
Secondary_Symptoms: Painful shallow ulceration; Crusting; Regional lymphadenopathy; Mild fever
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Hont par chhote paani waale fopoole (vesicles) guchhe me bane hain?; 2. Fopoole nikalne se pehle sunsunahat/jalan hui thi?; 3. Bukhar ke baad nikla hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Acyclovir 5% ointment OR Oral Acyclovir / Valacyclovir
Dosage_Frequency: 5 times daily local application / 400 mg 5 times daily oral
Supportive_Medicines: Paracetamol 500 mg SOS for pain; Calamine lotion or petroleum jelly for crusting
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Antivirals are Rx; Initiate treatment at first prodromal tingling sign for maximum efficacy; Avoid touching eyes post touching lip lesions
Home_Care_Advice: Do NOT pick or pop vesicles; Apply acyclovir ointment with cotton swab; Wash hands frequently; Avoid kissing and sharing utensils during active lesions
Lab_Investigations: Tzanck smear (multinucleated giant cells); HSV-1 PCR or IgM serology
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Lesions spreading near or into eyes (Herpes Simplex Keratitis risk); Immunocompromised patient with severe widespread erosion; Lesions lasting >2 weeks

Primary_Symptoms: Grouped painful vesicles and painful shallow ulcers on genital/perianal mucosa; Dysuria; Inguinal lymphadenopathy
Secondary_Symptoms: Prodromal burning/tingling; Fever; Malaise; Myalgia; Vaginal or urethral discharge
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Guptang (genitals) par dard waale chhote fopoole ya zakhm hain?; 2. Peshab me tez jalan aur inguinal lymph nodes me sujan hai?; 3. Pehle bhi aisa hua hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Acyclovir OR Valacyclovir (Oral antiviral therapy)
Dosage_Frequency: TDS (8 hourly for Acyclovir) / BD (12 hourly for Valacyclovir)
Supportive_Medicines: Paracetamol 650 mg SOS for pain; Lignocaine 2% gel topically for localized pain relief during urination; Salt water hip bath
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Antivirals are Rx; Treat sexual partner if symptomatic; Strict barrier precautions (condoms) during active lesions; Pregnancy caution
Home_Care_Advice: Maintain strict genital hygiene; Take warm Sitz baths to ease dysuria; Wear loose cotton underwear; Avoid sexual activity during active outbreaks
Lab_Investigations: HSV-1 and HSV-2 Type-Specific Serology; Viral Culture / PCR of ulcer swab; Syphilis and HIV screening
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Severe urinary retention due to painful genital lesions; High fever with meningeal irritation (herpetic meningitis); Genital herpes in pregnant women near delivery

Primary_Symptoms: Firm, dome-shaped, shiny, umbilicated papules (central pit) on skin; Asymptomatic or mild pruritus
Secondary_Symptoms: Erythema around papules (molluscum dermatitis); Secondary bacterial infection; Multiple lesions
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Chamdi par shiny, gol, chote dane hain jinke beech me chhota gaddha (umbilication) hai?; 2. Khujli hoti hai?; 3. Bachho me ya guptang par hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Salicylic Acid 16.5% + Lactic Acid lotion OR KOH 10% solution (topical application)
Dosage_Frequency: OD (applied strictly pinpoint on lesion at bedtime)
Supportive_Medicines: Topical Tretinoin 0.025% cream; Cryotherapy or curettage under dermatologist care
Precautions_Contraindications: Avoid applying Salicylic acid/KOH on normal surrounding skin or face; Do NOT squeeze or pick papules to prevent autoinoculation and scarring
Home_Care_Advice: Do not scratch or squeeze lesions; Avoid sharing towels, sponges, or bath toys; Keep lesions covered with clothing or bandage
Lab_Investigations: Clinical diagnosis; Dermoscopy (central pit with white core); Histopathology (Henderson-Paterson bodies)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Widespread giant molluscum (>100 lesions or face involvement in HIV/immunocompromised); Secondary severe bacterial superinfection

Primary_Symptoms: Hyperkeratotic, exophytic, rough papules or plaques with punctate black dots (thrombosed capillaries); Painless or mild pressure pain
Secondary_Symptoms: Koebnerization (spreading along scratch marks); Multiple papules; Fissuring; Tenderness
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Chamdi par khurdura, kadak, ubhara hua massa (wart) bana hai?; 2. Upar chhote kale dot dikhte hain?; 3. Ungliyo ya haath par hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Salicylic Acid 17% + Lactic Acid 17% topical paint
Dosage_Frequency: OD (Apply pinpoint after paring dead skin)
Supportive_Medicines: Cryotherapy with liquid nitrogen or electrocautery (under dermatologist supervision); Retinoic acid gel
Precautions_Contraindications: Do NOT apply salicylic acid paint on facial warts, anogenital warts, or inflamed/broken skin; Avoid pared skin bleeding; Caution in diabetics
Home_Care_Advice: Soak wart in warm water for 5 mins, gently file top dead skin with emery board, apply paint strictly on wart; Protect surrounding skin with petroleum jelly
Lab_Investigations: Clinical diagnosis; Dermoscopy (characteristic red/black capillary dots)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Warts on face, eyelids, or anogenital region; Rapidly spreading warts in immunocompromised patients; Painful bleeding warts

Common_Names_Hindi: Kechua rash; Snake-like rash; Larva Migrans
Primary_Symptoms: Erythematous, intensely pruritic, serpiginous (snake-like) linear creeping eruption; Progresses 1-2 cm/day
Secondary_Symptoms: Vesicles along track; Excoriation; Secondary bacterial infection; Localized edema
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Skin ke niche keda chalne jaisi saamp (snake) jaisi lal khujli waali patti aage badh rahi hai?; 2. Ret/mitti ya samundar ke kinare ghoomne ke baad hua?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Albendazole (Oral) OR Ivermectin (Oral)
Supportive_Medicines: Levocetirizine 5 mg OD for intense itching; Topical 10% Albendazole cream
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Systemic anthelmintics Rx; Avoid in early pregnancy; Antihistamines needed for allergic creeping reaction
Home_Care_Advice: Avoid walking barefoot on moist soil, sand, or beaches contaminated with animal feces; Do not freeze or freeze-spray lesions; Avoid scratching track
Lab_Investigations: Clinical diagnosis based on pathognomonic serpiginous creeping track; CBC (mild eosinophilia)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Widespread tracks (>5 tracks); Secondary severe bacterial cellulitis; Pulmonary symptoms (Loffler syndrome - cough/wheeze)

Common_Names_Hindi: Kusht Rog; Leprosy; Safed sunn daag
Primary_Symptoms: Hypopigmented or erythematous skin patch with DEFINITE LOSS OF SENSATION (touch/pain/temp); Thickened non-tender peripheral nerves
Secondary_Symptoms: Loss of sweating/hair on patch; Muscle weakness/claw hand; Trophic ulcers; Epistaxis; Facial nodular infiltration
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Skin par aisa daag hai jahan sui chobhne ya garam/thanda lagne par dard NAHI hota?; 2. Haath-pairo me sunn-pan hai?; 3. Koni/ghutne ki nas sooji hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Rx - dermatologist supervision required (National NLEP Multi-Drug Therapy - Rifampicin + Dapsone + Clofazimine)
Popular_Indian_Brands: NLEP MDT Blister Packs (PB / MB Adult Packs)
Adult_Strength_Mg: Rifampicin 600 mg monthly + Dapsone 100 mg daily + Clofazimine 300 mg monthly / 50 mg daily
Supportive_Medicines: Prednisolone oral for lepra reactions (Erythema Nodosum Leprosum / Type 1 reaction under specialist supervision); Protective footwear
Precautions_Contraindications: Rx - dermatologist supervision required; Treatment follows National Leprosy Eradication Programme (NLEP) guidelines; Dapsone hypersensitivity syndrome risk; Clofazimine causes reversible reddish-brown skin discoloration
Home_Care_Advice: Take MDT blister pack strictly as prescribed without default; Protect numb hands/feet from heat, cuts, and burns; Wear custom MCR footwear; Perform daily self-inspection of hands/feet
Lab_Investigations: Slit Skin Smear for Acid Fast Bacilli (Bacterial Index); Skin Biopsy; Sensory testing (Semmes-Weinstein monofilaments)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Lepra Reactions (Type 1 or Type 2 ENL: sudden painful red skin nodules, high fever, acute nerve pain/weakness, iridocyclitis)

Primary_Symptoms: Single primary herald patch (2-5 cm oval scaly plaque) followed 1-2 weeks later by Christmas tree distribution of smaller oval lesions
Secondary_Symptoms: Mild to moderate pruritus; Collarette of fine scale inside border of lesion; Mild prodromal fever/malaise
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Pehle ek bada gol daag (herald patch) nikla tha aur uske 1-2 hafte baad pitth/chhati par chhote oval daag nikle hain?; 2. Daag Christmas tree jaise hain?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Symptomatic treatment + Calamine lotion + Levocetirizine
Supportive_Medicines: Topical mild hydrocortisone 1% cream for severe itch; Phototherapy (UVB) if extensive
Precautions_Contraindications: Reassure patient regarding benign self-limiting nature; Avoid aggressive scrubbing or hot water baths; Rule out Secondary Syphilis if palmar/plantar lesions present
Home_Care_Advice: Take lukewarm water baths; Use mild soap-free cleansers; Apply Calamine lotion gently; Wear soft cotton clothing; Avoid vigorous exercise
Lab_Investigations: RPR / VDRL test (to rule out Secondary Syphilis); KOH mount (rule out Tinea corporis)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Severe erythroderma; Lesions involving palms, soles, or mucous membranes; Pruritus unremitting despite oral antihistamines

Common_Names_Hindi: Hont ke kinare katna; Angular Cheilitis
Primary_Symptoms: Painful erythematous fissuring, maceration, and scaling at angles of mouth; Stinging pain on opening mouth
Secondary_Symptoms: Bleeding on wide opening; Cheesy exudate; Burning sensation with acidic food; Maceration
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Hont ke dono kinaro (corners) par chamdi kathi hui aur lal hai?; 2. Muuh kholne par dard hota hai?; 3. Nakli daant (dentures) pehente hain ya B12/Iron ki kami hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Clotrimazole 1% + Mupirocin 2% cream OR Hydrocortisone 1% cream (short term)
Supportive_Medicines: B-Complex with Vitamin B12 and Iron capsules; Zinc supplements; Petroleum jelly barrier
Precautions_Contraindications: Do NOT use potent steroids on facial angle; Avoid lip licking habit (licking worsens maceration); Address underlying denture ill-fit or vitamin deficiency
Home_Care_Advice: Apply petroleum jelly or barrier ointment frequently; Clean and disinfect dentures nightly; Take oral B-complex and iron supplements; Avoid wide mouth opening
Lab_Investigations: Serum Vitamin B12; Serum Ferritin; KOH mount / Swab for Candida and Staph aureus
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Deep non-healing painful ulceration at oral commissures lasting >3 weeks; Spreading facial impetigo

Primary_Symptoms: Evanescent erythematous edematous pruritic wheals (hive-like swelling) lasting <24 hours per individual lesion
Secondary_Symptoms: Severe itching; Dermatographism; Warmth; Angioedema (lip/eyelid swelling); Flushing
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Sharir par lal, ubhare hue, khujli waale chakatte (pitta) nikal rahe hain?; 2. Ek daag 24 ghante me gayab hokar doosri jagah nikalta hai?; 3. Koi nayi dawai ya food khaya tha?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Levocetirizine OR Bilastine OR Fexofenadine
Supportive_Medicines: Calamine lotion topically; Short course oral Prednisolone (only if severe acute refractory episode under doctor supervision)
Max_Safe_Limit_24h: 10 mg Levocetirizine / 40 mg Bilastine / 180 mg Fexofenadine
Precautions_Contraindications: Non-sedating antihistamines first-line; Drowsiness caution with cetirizine/levocetirizine - caution while driving; Do NOT use topical antihistamines or anesthetics (risk of contact dermatitis)
Home_Care_Advice: Avoid identified trigger (NSAIDs, specific food, temperature extremes); Cool water baths; Apply calamine lotion; Wear loose cotton clothes
Lab_Investigations: Complete Blood Count; Absolute Eosinophil Count; CRP; Allergy prick testing not indicated in acute phase
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Signs of Anaphylaxis (difficulty breathing, throat tightness, tongue/lip swelling, dizziness, vomiting, drop in BP)

Primary_Symptoms: Daily or almost daily evanescent pruritic wheals recurring for MORE THAN 6 WEEKS
Secondary_Symptoms: Severe itching; Angioedema (in 40% cases); Sleep disruption; Fatigue; Dermographism
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Chhapaki/pitta pichhle 6 hafte se zyada se roz nikal rahi hai?; 2. Ek chakatta 24 ghante me gayab hota hai?; 3. Dhoop, thand ya pressure se badhta hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Levocetirizine 5 mg OR Fexofenadine 180 mg OR Bilastine 20 mg (Up to 4x standard dose under dermatologist)
Dosage_Frequency: OD initially, can increase up to BD or QID under specialist care
Supportive_Medicines: Omalizumab (anti-IgE biologic injection) / Cyclosporine under specialist care if antihistamine-resistant
Max_Safe_Limit_24h: 20 mg Levocetirizine (4x dose under doctor supervision)
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; High-dose antihistamines require specialist supervision; Avoid long-term continuous oral steroids; Caution with driving
Home_Care_Advice: Identify and avoid physical inducible triggers (pressure, cold, sweat, vibration); Avoid NSAIDs/Aspirin (trigger flares); Maintain symptom diary
Lab_Investigations: CBC; ESR; TSH and Anti-TPO antibodies (autoimmune thyroiditis screening); Autologous Serum Skin Test (ASST)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Concomitant severe angioedema with stridor or dyspnea; Systemic vasculitic urticaria (individual lesions persisting >24h with purpura/pigmentation)

Primary_Symptoms: Sudden severe localized non-pitting edema of deep dermis and subcutaneous tissues (lips, tongue, eyelids, larynx, hands)
Secondary_Symptoms: Stridor; Dyspnea; Hoarseness; Abdominal pain; Urticaria; Absence of itching (in hereditary type)
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Achanak hont, jeebh, aankh ya gala sooj gaya hai?; 2. Saans lene ya nigalne me takleef ho rahi hai?; 3. Koi BP ki dawai (ACE inhibitors) khaate hain?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: None - emergency hospital referral
Popular_Indian_Brands: Injection Adrenaline (Epinephrine) 1:1000 IM; Injection Hydrocortisone; Injection Avil
Dosage_Frequency: Immediate IM Adrenaline 0.5 mg in mid-outer thigh if airway compromised
Supportive_Medicines: Airway management; IM Epinephrine 0.5 mg; IV Antihistamines; IV Corticosteroids; C1-inhibitor concentrate (for HAE)
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Life-threatening emergency; Do NOT delay seeking emergency hospital care; ACE inhibitors strictly contraindicated if drug-induced
Home_Care_Advice: Call emergency services immediately; Keep patient calm in upright sitting position; Administer Auto-injectable Epinephrine (EpiPen) if trained while reaching ER
Lab_Investigations: Complement C4 level; C1-inhibitor quantitative and functional assay; CBC; Electrolytes
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Medical emergency - Immediate ER referral; Laryngeal edema (stridor, barky cough, severe breathlessness); Anaphylactic shock; Tongue swelling obstructing airway

Primary_Symptoms: Pruritic, erythematous, dry scaly papules and plaques with lichenification in flexural folds (elbows/knees)
Secondary_Symptoms: Severe itching (worst at night); Xerosis; Excoriations; Fissuring; Infraorbital fold (Dennie-Morgan line)
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Bachpan se chamdi sookhi aur severe khujli waali hai?; 2. Kohni aur ghutne ke piche lal rash aur chamdi moti hai?; 3. Allergy/Asthma ki history hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Tacrolimus 0.03% / 0.1% ointment OR Fluticasone 0.05% cream (Mild-to-Moderate topical steroid/calcineurin inhibitor)
Supportive_Medicines: Emollient cream (Cetaphil/Venusia) applied liberally 3-4 times daily; Levocetirizine 5 mg OD at bedtime for itch
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Mild/moderate topical steroid duration max 14 days; Do NOT apply potent steroids on face or flexures; Tacrolimus may cause initial burning
Home_Care_Advice: Apply emollient liberally within 3 minutes after bathing ('soak and seal'); Use soap-free liquid cleansers; Wear soft cotton clothing; Avoid wool and synthetic fabrics
Lab_Investigations: Serum Total IgE; Absolute Eosinophil Count; Skin Prick Patch test
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Eczema Herpeticum (sudden widespread painful punch-out vesicles with fever); Widespread secondary bacterial infection with pus crusts

Common_Names_Hindi: Dawai/Gahne se allergy rash; Contact Allergy
Primary_Symptoms: Pruritic erythematous edematous papules, vesicles, and bullae confined strictly to area of contact with allergen
Secondary_Symptoms: Severe itching; Stinging; Oozing and crusting; Lichenification (in chronic cases); Well-demarcated margins
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Kisi cheez (gahne, ghadi, hair dye, cream, leather, cement) ke chhoone ke baad rash hua hai?; 2. Jahan cheez chhui thi wahin lalapan hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Mometasone furoate 0.1% cream OR Fluticasone 0.05% cream (Moderate potency topical steroid)
Supportive_Medicines: Levocetirizine 5 mg OD at bedtime; Calamine lotion; Cold compress; Liquid paraffin emollient
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Moderate/potent topical steroids max 14 days; Do NOT apply on face or genital skin without doctor; Avoid continuous use to prevent striae/atrophy
Home_Care_Advice: Identify and strictly avoid offending allergen (e.g., nickel jewelry, hair dye, rubber, fragrances); Wash area thoroughly after exposure; Apply cold moist compresses
Lab_Investigations: Patch Testing (Finn Chambers) with standard allergen series
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Widespread dermatitis covering >30% body surface; Facial/eyelid involvement with severe edema; Secondary bacterial superinfection

Primary_Symptoms: Erythematous, burning, painful dry scaly fissured skin instantly following chemical/irritant exposure
Secondary_Symptoms: Stinging sensation; Scaling; Glazed/shiny skin appearance; Shallow cracks; Mild itching
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Tej sabun, detergent, acid, ya chemical lagne ke turant baad skin lal aur kathi hai?; 2. Burning aur dard zyada hai khujli se?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Hydrocortisone 1% cream OR Desonide 0.05% cream (Mild topical steroid) + Heavy Barrier Ointment
Supportive_Medicines: Petrolatum jelly / Barrier cream (Zinc oxide); Levocetirizine 5 mg SOS; Emollient soap substitutes
Precautions_Contraindications: Avoid using strong topical steroids on broken skin barrier; Do NOT apply harsh antiseptics (Dettol/Savlon) on raw irritant skin
Home_Care_Advice: Wear protective nitrile/rubber gloves when handling detergents/chemicals; Apply thick barrier cream/petroleum jelly frequently; Wash hands with soap-free cleanser
Lab_Investigations: Clinical diagnosis; Patch testing (to rule out allergic contact component if chronic)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Deep painful fissures with purulent infection; Extensive chemical burn/necrosis; Inability to work due to hand incapacitation

Primary_Symptoms: Erythematous scaly plaques with greasy yellow scales on seborrheic areas (scalp, nasolabial folds, eyebrows, chest)
Secondary_Symptoms: Pruritus; Burning sensation; Follicular papules; Blepharitis; Fine dandruff flakes
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Sir, eyebrows aur naak ke paas lalapan aur peeli chipchipi patti (greasy scales) jamti hai?; 2. Khujli hoti hai?; 3. Thand me badhta hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Ketoconazole 2% + Zinc Pyrithione (ZPTO) shampoo OR Hydrocortisone 1% cream (short term for face)
Popular_Indian_Brands: Nizral Forte; Scalpe Plus; Candid TV
Dosage_Frequency: Use shampoo 2-3 times weekly, leave for 5 mins before rinsing / Cream OD on face
Supportive_Medicines: Sertaconazole 2% cream for face; Coal tar shampoo; Cetirizine 5 mg SOS for itch
Precautions_Contraindications: Do NOT use potent topical steroids on face (causes steroid rosacea, perioral dermatitis, telangiectasia); Ketoconazole treatment is long-term maintenance
Home_Care_Advice: Wash scalp 2-3 times weekly with antifungal shampoo; Avoid heavy hair oils and pomades; Wash face with gentle zinc-containing cleansers
Lab_Investigations: Clinical diagnosis; KOH mount of scales (Malassezia yeast inspection)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Erythroderma (generalized red scaly skin covering whole body); Severe secondary bacterial infection with purulent crusting

Primary_Symptoms: Pruritic, coin-shaped (nummular/discoid) erythematous vesiculopapular scaly plaques on extremities
Secondary_Symptoms: Severe itching; Oozing; Crusting; Lichenification; Dry surrounding skin
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Haath-pairo par sikke (coin) jaise gol lal khujli waale chakatte bane hain?; 2. Dane se paani/oozing nikalta hai?; 3. Skin bohut sookhi rehti hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Clobetasol propionate 0.05% cream OR Betamethasone dipropionate 0.05% cream (Potent topical steroid)
Supportive_Medicines: Liquid paraffin emollient cream; Levocetirizine 5 mg BD for intense itch; Mupirocin ointment if impetiginized
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Potent topical steroid - MAXIMUM 14 DAYS DURATION; Strictly CONTRAINDICATED on face, groin, or axillae; Avoid abrupt cessation
Home_Care_Advice: Apply thick emollients immediately after bathing; Avoid hot showers and harsh soaps; Wear soft loose cotton clothing; Avoid scratching
Lab_Investigations: Skin scraping for KOH mount (rule out Tinea corporis/ringworm); Patch testing if refractory
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Widespread eruption covering large surface area; Severe secondary bacterial infection with honey-colored crusts

Primary_Symptoms: Intensely pruritic, deep-seated 'tapioca-pudding' vesicles on lateral aspects of fingers, palms, and soles
Secondary_Symptoms: Burning pain; Scaling; Desquamation; Painful fissuring; Hyperhidrosis
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Haath ki ungliyo ke kinaro ya hatheli par chhote sabudana (tapioca) jaise paani waale fopoole hain?; 2. Severe khujli/jalan hoti hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Mometasone furoate 0.1% ointment OR Clobetasol 0.05% ointment (Potent topical steroid)
Supportive_Medicines: Levocetirizine 5 mg BD or Atarax 25 mg BT for intense itching; Potassium permanganate (1:10000) soaks for weeping vesicles
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Potent topical steroid - max 14 days; High risk of recurrence; Caution with secondary bacterial infection
Home_Care_Advice: Soak hands in cool water or diluted Potassium Permanganate solution for 15 mins; Apply heavy emollients after soaks; Wear cotton gloves under rubber gloves for wet work
Lab_Investigations: KOH preparation of vesicle fluid/roof (rule out inflammatory tinea pedis/manuum); Patch testing
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Severe painful bullae preventing hand function; Secondary cellulitis/lymphangitis; Unremitting severe disease requiring systemic steroids

Common_Names_Hindi: Pairo ki soojan aur rash; Venous Eczema
Primary_Symptoms: Erythematous, scaly, hyperpigmented (hemosiderin staining) dermatitis on lower legs/ankles; Pitting edema
Secondary_Symptoms: Pruritus; Lipodermatosclerosis ('inverted bowling pin' leg); Venous ulcers; Varicose veins
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Pairo me soojan, naso ka phoolna (varicose veins) aur ankles ke paas bhura/lal rash hai?; 2. Shaam ko pairo me dard badhta hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Mometasone furoate 0.1% cream (short term) + Compression Therapy / Emollients
Supportive_Medicines: Unna boot / Graduated compression stockings (30-40 mmHg); Liquid paraffin emollient; Pentoxifylline 400 mg TDS
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Do NOT use compression therapy if Peripheral Arterial Disease is present (check ABPI first); Potent steroids max 14 days
Home_Care_Advice: Elevate legs above heart level whenever sitting or lying down; Wear graduated compression stockings daily; Walk regularly; Apply thick emollients daily
Lab_Investigations: Venous Doppler Ultrasound of lower limbs; Ankle-Brachial Pressure Index (ABPI); CBC
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Active non-healing painful venous stasis ulcer; Acute deep vein thrombosis (sudden calf swelling/pain); Severe cellulitis

Primary_Symptoms: Sharply demarcated erythematous plaques covered with silvery-white micaceous scales on extensor surfaces (elbows, knees)
Secondary_Symptoms: Auspitz sign (pinpoint bleeding on scraping scale); Pruritus; Nail pitting; Psoriatic arthritis; Koebner phenomenon
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Kohni ya ghutne par lal chakatte hain jinke upar safed chandi (silver) jaisi patti jamti hai?; 2. Patti hatane par khoon ki boond dikhti hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Clobetasol 0.05% + Salicylic Acid 3%/6% ointment OR Calcipatriol 0.005% ointment
Supportive_Medicines: Coal tar 5% ointment; Oral Methotrexate / Acitretin / Cyclosporine (strictly under dermatologist supervision); Phototherapy (NBUVB)
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Potent steroid combo ointment max 28 days then taper; Do NOT abruptly stop systemic steroids (triggers fatal erythrodermic/pustular psoriasis flare)
Home_Care_Advice: Expose lesions to brief daily natural sunlight; Apply thick emollients daily after bath; Avoid skin injury/scratches; Avoid alcohol and smoking
Lab_Investigations: Skin biopsy; Serum Uric Acid; Rheumatoid Factor & Anti-CCP (if joint pain present); Lipid profile
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Erythrodermic Psoriasis (redness >90% body surface); Generalized Pustular Psoriasis (widespread sterile pustules with high fever); Severe joint pain/swelling

Primary_Symptoms: Erythematous plaques with thick silvery-white silvery scales extending beyond hairline on scalp; Severe itching
Secondary_Symptoms: Hair loss (temporary); Tightness; Flaking; Extensor body lesions
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Sir me bahut moti safed/chandi jaisi patti jamti hai jo hair line se bahar aati hai?; 2. Kanga karne par moti patti jhadti hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Clobetasol propionate 0.05% + Salicylic Acid 3% lotion / solution
Dosage_Frequency: Apply on affected scalp at bedtime, wash off in morning
Supportive_Medicines: Coal Tar 4% + Salicylic Acid 3% shampoo 2-3 times weekly; Ketoconazole shampoo if secondary fungal infection
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Potent steroid scalp application max 21 days; Do not apply close to eyes; Taper frequency slowly as lesions clear
Home_Care_Advice: Massage scalp solution gently into scalp; Use coal tar shampoo 2-3 times weekly, leaving on scalp for 10 mins before washing; Avoid aggressive scratching
Lab_Investigations: Clinical diagnosis; Dermoscopy; Skin biopsy if diagnostic doubt
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Hair loss over large area; Severe secondary bacterial infection with purulent discharge and swelling; Psoriatic joint pain

Primary_Symptoms: 5 Ps: Planar, Polygonal, Purplish, Pruritic, Papules/plaques on flexor wrists, ankles, and lumbar spine
Secondary_Symptoms: Wickham striae (fine white lacy lines on surface); Oral lacy white lesions; Nail dystrophy; Koebnerization
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Kalai ya ganth par chamakdar, baagani (purple), chokor, tez khujli waale dane hain?; 2. Muuh ke andar safed jaali (lacy white) bani hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Clobetasol propionate 0.05% cream OR Triamcinolone 0.1% oral paste (for oral mucosal LP)
Popular_Indian_Brands: Tenovate Cream; Kenacort Oral Paste; Clobetamil
Meal_Timing: After Food / After meals for oral paste
Supportive_Medicines: Levocetirizine 5 mg BD or Hydroxyzine 25 mg BT for intense itch; Oral Acitretin / Steroids under dermatologist
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Potent topical steroid max 28 days; Oral Lichen Planus carries a small risk of malignant transformation (regular dental checkups needed)
Home_Care_Advice: Avoid spicy, acidic, and crunchy foods if oral LP present; Do not scratch lesions; Maintain good oral hygiene with alcohol-free mouthwash
Lab_Investigations: Skin biopsy (saw-tooth rete ridges); Hepatitis C virus (HCV) antibody screening (associated with LP)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Severe erosive painful oral or genital Lichen Planus; Rapidly progressive nail destruction (pterygium formation); Ulcerative foot lesions

Common_Names_Hindi: Purani khujli se chamdi moti; LSC
Primary_Symptoms: Thickened, hyperkeratotic, hyperpigmented lichenified plaque with exaggerated skin markings from repetitive scratching
Secondary_Symptoms: Intense paroxysmal itching (worst at rest/night); Excoriations; Well-circumscribed plaque on accessible sites
Typical_Duration: Chronic ongoing until scratch cycle broken
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Ek hi jagah par baar-baar khujlane se chamdi chamde (leather) jaisi moti ho gayi hai?; 2. Khujli itni tez hai ki roke nahi rukti?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Clobetasol propionate 0.05% ointment under occlusive dressing
Supportive_Medicines: Hydroxyzine 25 mg BT for nocturnal itch reduction; Liquid paraffin emollient; Bandaging over lesion
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Potent topical steroid max 21 days; MUST BREAK ITCH-SCRATCH CYCLE to cure condition; Do NOT use on face/groin
Home_Care_Advice: Keep lesion covered with sterile bandage or dressing to physically prevent scratching; Apply heavy emollient multiple times daily; Cut fingernails short
Lab_Investigations: Skin biopsy if atypical or non-responsive
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Severe secondary bacterial cellulitis/abscess; Deep ulceration within lichenified plaque; Failure to respond after 3 weeks

Common_Names_Hindi: Poore sharir me khujli; Generalized Itching
Primary_Symptoms: Widespread intense itching across body without primary skin rash or lesions (only excoriations)
Secondary_Symptoms: Excoriations; Dry skin; Anxiety; Sleep disturbance; Lichenification
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Poore sharir par bina kisi rash/daag ke severe khujli hoti hai?; 2. Diabetes, Kidney, Liver, ya Thyroid ki bimari hai?; 3. Sote samay badhti hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Levocetirizine 5 mg OR Hydroxyzine 25 mg + Emollient lotion
Supportive_Medicines: Calamine lotion with 1% Menthol; Coconut oil / Liquid paraffin emollient baths; Treat underlying systemic cause
Precautions_Contraindications: Sedating antihistamines (Hydroxyzine) caution with driving and operating machinery; Systemic screening mandatory if itching persists without skin lesions
Home_Care_Advice: Take short lukewarm showers; Apply emollients liberally on damp skin immediately after bath; Wear loose cotton clothes; Avoid wool and hot water
Lab_Investigations: CBC; Renal Function Test (Urea/Creatinine); Liver Function Test; Thyroid Function Test (TSH); Fasting Blood Sugar; Stool Occult Blood
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Pruritus accompanied by unexplained weight loss, night sweats, or fever (Lymphoma/Hodgkin's screening); Jaundice; Severe uremic frost

Common_Names_Hindi: Dawai se rash; Drug Allergy Rash
Primary_Symptoms: Symmetrical maculopapular (morbilliform) erythematous rash starting 7-14 days after starting a new drug
Secondary_Symptoms: Mild to moderate pruritus; Low fever; Mild erythema; Absence of mucosal involvement or skin peeling
Typical_Duration: 7 to 14 days after stopping offending drug
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Koi nayi dawai (antibiotic, painkiller, seizure drug) shuru karne ke 1-2 hafte baad rash aaya hai?; 2. Muuh ya aankh ke andar zakhm hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Levocetirizine 5 mg + STOP OFFENDING DRUG IMMEDIATELY
Supportive_Medicines: Calamine lotion topically; Short course oral Prednisolone 20 mg OD for 5 days if widespread (under doctor supervision)
Precautions_Contraindications: IMMEDIATELY STOP SUSPECTED OFFENDING DRUG; Re-exposure to offending drug is STRICTLY CONTRAINDICATED; Monitor closely for red flags of SJS/TEN
Home_Care_Advice: Stop suspected offending medication immediately; Apply Calamine lotion; Drink plenty of fluids; Keep skin cool and hydrated
Lab_Investigations: CBC with Differential (check Eosinophils); LFT; RFT; Skin Biopsy if diagnostic doubt
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Mucosal erosion (mouth/eye/genital ulcers); Skin pain, blistering, or skin peeling (Nikolsky sign - SJS/TEN emergency); High fever; Facial swelling

Common_Names_Hindi: SJS / TEN Emergency; Dawai se chamdi udhedna
Primary_Symptoms: Severe widespread painful dusky-erythematous macules/bullae with extensive epidermal detachment (peeling skin like scald); Severe mucosal necrosis
Secondary_Symptoms: High fever; Hemorrhagic crusting of lips/mouth; Purulent conjunctivitis; Genital erosions; Prostration; Nikolsky sign positive
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Dawai lene ke baad skin chhil kar udhed rahi hai (peeling like hot water burn)?; 2. Muuh, aankh aur guptang me mawaad/zakhm hai?; 3. High fever hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: None - emergency hospital referral
Popular_Indian_Brands: Injection Dexamethasone / Methylprednisolone; IVIG (Intravenous Immunoglobulin); Cyclosporine
Dosage_Frequency: Immediate IV emergency administration in ICU
Supportive_Medicines: Emergency Burn ICU admission; Fluid and electrolyte resuscitation; Sterile non-adherent wound dressing; Ophthalmic care to prevent blindness
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Life-threatening emergency; STOP ALL NON-ESSENTIAL MEDICATIONS IMMEDIATELY; Do NOT attempt home care
Home_Care_Advice: Immediate emergency transfer to a tertiary hospital Burn ICU or Dermatology ICU; Keep patient wrapped in clean sterile sheet; Do NOT rub skin while transporting
Lab_Investigations: CBC; RFT; LFT; Electrolytes; Skin Biopsy; Blood and wound cultures; Chest X-ray
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Medical emergency - Immediate ER referral; Epidermal detachment; Mucosal erosions; High fever with hemodynamic instability; Ocular involvement

Common_Names_Hindi: Keede ke katne ka rash; Insect Bite
Primary_Symptoms: Localized edematous erythematous papule or wheal with central punctum; Intense localized itching and pain
Secondary_Symptoms: Excoriation; Bulla formation (in hypersensitive individuals); Localized warmth; Secondary infection
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Keede (machhar, chikna, keeda) katne ke baad lal gummra aur khujli hui hai?; 2. Central katne ka nishan (punctum) dikhta hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Calamine lotion + Levocetirizine 5 mg OR Hydrocortisone 1% cream
Supportive_Medicines: Hydrocortisone 1% cream applied topically BD; Ice pack compress; Mupirocin ointment if scratched and infected
Precautions_Contraindications: Do not scratch bite area to prevent secondary bacterial impetigo/cellulitis; Mild topical steroid max 7 days; Caution in young infants
Home_Care_Advice: Apply ice pack over bite area for 10 mins; Apply Calamine lotion; Use insect repellents (DEET/Picaridin); Keep surroundings clean
Lab_Investigations: Clinical diagnosis
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Anaphylactic reaction (breathing difficulty, facial swelling, collapse post bee/wasp sting); Rapidly spreading red cellulitis from bite site

Primary_Symptoms: Pruritic erythematous papules in a linear array ('breakfast, lunch, and dinner' pattern) on exposed skin
Secondary_Symptoms: Severe itching; Central punctum; Excoriations; Bullous reactions; Post-inflammatory macules
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Line me 3-4 lal khujli waale dane ('breakfast, lunch, dinner' pattern) hain?; 2. Raat ko sote me kate hain?; 3. Bedding me chhota keeda hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Levocetirizine 5 mg + Hydrocortisone 1% cream / Calamine lotion
Supportive_Medicines: Hydroxyzine 25 mg BT for severe nocturnal itch; Mupirocin ointment for secondary excoriated lesions
Precautions_Contraindications: Medications only relieve symptoms; COMPLETE PEST EXTERMINATION OF LIVING SPACE IS MANDATORY; Do not scratch papules
Home_Care_Advice: Wash all bedsheets, mattress covers, and blankets in hot water (>60C); Vacuum mattress and bed frame thoroughly; Hire professional pest control for bedbugs
Lab_Investigations: Clinical diagnosis based on characteristic linear papular grouping
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Secondary widespread bacterial impetiginization; Severe allergic bullous eruption; Severe sleep deprivation and anxiety

Primary_Symptoms: Multiple tiny erythematous pruritic papules and vesicles on covered skin (neck, chest, upper back) with intense stinging/prickling
Secondary_Symptoms: Sweating-induced burning/prickling sensation; Excoriations; Mild scaling; Anhidrosis
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Garmi/pasiine me chhote-chhote lal dane nikle hain jinme sui chobhne jaisi (prickling) khujli hoti hai?; 2. Pasiina aane par badhta hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Calamine lotion with 1% Menthol OR Zinc Oxide dusting powder
Supportive_Medicines: Levocetirizine 5 mg SOS for itch; Cool water baths; Mild topical hydrocortisone 1% if severely inflamed
Precautions_Contraindications: Do NOT use heavy oil-based ointments or thick creams (they further block eccrine sweat ducts); Avoid excessive scrubbing with harsh soaps
Home_Care_Advice: Stay in a cool, air-conditioned or well-ventilated room; Take cool water showers twice daily; Wear loose, light cotton clothes; Avoid heavy physical exertion in heat
Lab_Investigations: Clinical diagnosis
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Miliaria Profunda with heat exhaustion signs (dizziness, fever, absence of sweating, confusion); Secondary bacterial pustules (Miliaria Pustulosa)

Primary_Symptoms: Erythematous, painful, hot skin developing 2-6 hours post sun exposure; Edema; Tenderness
Secondary_Symptoms: Blistering/bullae (in 2nd degree sunburn); Desquamation (peeling skin); Chills; Fever; Nausea
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Dhoop me lambe samay tak rehne ke baad skin lal, garam aur dard waali ho gayi hai?; 2. Chamdi chhil rahi hai ya fopoole bane hain?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Aloe Vera Gel 99% + Calamine lotion + Paracetamol 650 mg / Ibuprofen 400 mg
Popular_Indian_Brands: Aloe Vera Gel; Calamine; Dolo 650; Brufen 400
Supportive_Medicines: Hydrocortisone 1% cream topically for mild sunburn; Heavy cool emollients; High fluid hydration
Precautions_Contraindications: Do NOT pop blisters; Avoid further sun exposure until completely healed; Do NOT apply ice directly on sunburned skin (causes tissue injury)
Home_Care_Advice: Apply cool compresses or cool water baths; Apply pure Aloe Vera gel liberally 3-4 times daily; Drink plenty of water; Wear wide-brimmed hats and protective clothing
Lab_Investigations: Clinical diagnosis
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Sunburn covering >20% body surface with large blisters; High fever, confusion, or dizziness (Sunstroke / Heat Illness); Severe unbearable skin pain

Primary_Symptoms: Pruritic erythematous papules, vesicles, or plaques appearing 30 min to several hours post sun exposure on sun-exposed skin
Secondary_Symptoms: Severe itching; Burning pain; Hardening/tolerance later in summer; Erythema; Edema
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Dhoop me nikalne ke kuch ghante baad khule me rehne waale hisse (haath, gale) par lal khujli waale dane nikalte hain?; 2. Thand me normal rehta hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Broad-Spectrum Sunscreen SPF 50+ (PA+++) + Levocetirizine 5 mg + Hydrocortisone 1% cream
Popular_Indian_Brands: Bello Photostable SPF 50; La Shield; Lvocet 5
Supportive_Medicines: Mometasone 0.1% cream for severe flares; Short course oral Prednisolone 20 mg OD under dermatologist for severe acute PMLE
Precautions_Contraindications: Medications manage symptoms; STRICT SUN PROTECTION IS MANDATORY; Reapply sunscreen every 2 hours outdoors; Topical steroids max 14 days
Home_Care_Advice: Apply broad-spectrum sunscreen SPF 50+ liberally 20 mins BEFORE going outdoors; Reapply every 2 hours; Wear full-sleeved cotton clothes, sunglasses, and use umbrella
Lab_Investigations: Phototesting (UVA/UVB sensitivity testing); ANA testing (rule out Cutaneous Lupus Erythematosus)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Lesions accompanied by joint pain, oral ulcers, or butterfly facial rash (rule out Systemic Lupus Erythematosus); Erythroderma

Primary_Symptoms: Pruritic, painful, violaceous/erythematous edematous inflammatory nodules on toes/fingers after cold exposure
Secondary_Symptoms: Burning pain; Blistering; Fissuring; Ulceration; Coldness of digits
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Thand ke mausam me pairo aur haath ki ungliya lal-neeli, sooji hui aur khujli/dard waali ho jati hain?; 2. Garam hone par jalan badhti hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Nifedipine (Oral vasodilator) OR Topical Nitroglycerin 0.2% ointment + Warmth
Supportive_Medicines: Calamine lotion topically; Levocetirizine 5 mg OD for itching; High Potency Topical Steroid (Clobetasol short term)
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Nifedipine caution in hypotension and cardiac heart failure; Do NOT apply direct intense heat (hot water/fire) to cold digits
Home_Care_Advice: REWARM DIGITS GRADUALLY at room temperature; Wear thick woollen socks and insulated gloves before stepping into cold; Avoid smoking (nicotine causes vasoconstriction)
Lab_Investigations: ANA test; Antiphospholipid Antibodies; Serum Cryoglobulins; CBC (rule out Raynaud's secondary to connective tissue disease)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Severe digital ulceration or necrosis/gangrene (blackening of digit tip); Persistent symptoms in summer season; Severe unremitting resting pain

Primary_Symptoms: Multiple tiny 1-3 mm monomorphic pruritic wheals surrounded by large erythematous flares triggered by sweating/heat/exercise
Secondary_Symptoms: Intense pinpoint stinging/burning; Flushing; Salivation; Syncope (in severe cases); Wheezing
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Kasrat karne, pasiina aane, ya garam paani se nahane ke turant baad chhote-chhote pinpoint pitta/dane nikalte hain jinme sui jaisi khujli hoti hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Hydroxyzine 25 mg OR Cetirizine 10 mg / Levocetirizine 5 mg
Dosage_Frequency: OD (30-60 min BEFORE exercise/exposure or BD)
Supportive_Medicines: Fexofenadine 180 mg OD; Montelukast 10 mg OD at bedtime; Cool water shower
Precautions_Contraindications: Drowsiness caution with Hydroxyzine/Cetirizine - caution while driving; Take antihistamine 30-60 mins BEFORE planned exercise or hot exposure
Home_Care_Advice: Take cool showers after exercise; Avoid sudden extreme physical exertion in hot humid weather; Wear breathable light cotton gym clothes
Lab_Investigations: Methacholine skin intradermal test; Exercise challenge test under medical supervision
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Cholinergic Anaphylaxis (exercise-induced dyspnea, stridor, hypotension, dizziness, or abdominal cramps)

Primary_Symptoms: Comedones (blackheads/whiteheads) with a few small non-inflammatory or inflammatory papules/pustules on face
Secondary_Symptoms: Mild facial oiliness; Mild localized soreness; Minimal scarring; Absence of deep nodules
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Chehre par chhote kile (blackheads/whiteheads) aur 2-4 chhote red pimples hain?; 2. Mawaad waale bade gummde to nahi hain?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Benzoyl Peroxide 2.5% gel OR Adapalene 0.1% gel
Popular_Indian_Brands: Persol AC 2.5; Galderma Deriva-CMS; Benzac AC
Dosage_Frequency: OD (Applied thin layer strictly over affected areas)
Supportive_Medicines: Salicylic acid 2% face wash; Clindamycin 1% topical gel for active pustules
Precautions_Contraindications: Benzoyl peroxide can bleach colored clothing and hair; Adapalene causes initial mild dryness, redness, and peeling; MUST USE SUNSCREEN daily; OTC options available
Home_Care_Advice: Wash face twice daily with gentle salicylic acid cleanser; Apply thin layer of gel at night; Do NOT squeeze, pop, or pick pimples; Avoid oily heavy cosmetics
Lab_Investigations: Clinical evaluation; Hormonal evaluation (Serum Free Testosterone, DHEAS, USG pelvis) if female with irregular periods/hirsutism
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Sudden flare into severe nodulocystic lesions; Progressive scarring; Severe psychological distress

Primary_Symptoms: Multiple inflammatory papules and pustules with moderate number of comedones on face, chest, and upper back
Secondary_Symptoms: Facial oiliness; Erythema; Localized tenderness; Early superficial scarring; Hyperpigmentation
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Chehre par bahut saare peele mawaad waale aur lal dard waale pimples hain?; 2. Peeth aur chhati par bhi hai?; 3. Pimple hatne par daag chhodta hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Adapalene 0.1% + Benzoyl Peroxide 2.5% gel (topical) + Oral Doxycycline / Limecycline
Meal_Timing: After Food (Doxycycline with full glass of water)
Supportive_Medicines: Clindamycin 1% + Nicotinamide gel for day use; Non-comedogenic sunscreen SPF 30+; Salicylic face wash
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Oral antibiotics Rx only; Doxycycline contraindicated in pregnancy and children <8 years; Take Doxycycline sitting upright with plenty of water to prevent pill esophagitis
Home_Care_Advice: Wash face twice daily with non-comedogenic cleanser; Apply sunscreen daily; Complete full antibiotic course; Do not pop pimples
Lab_Investigations: Routine Blood Count; Liver Function Test (if long-term oral antibiotics used)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Progression to deep painful cysts; Development of permanent pitted scars; Severe drug rash from oral antibiotics
