Lab_Investigations: Ultrasound Thyroid & Neck (TI-RADS scoring); FNAC (Fine Needle Aspiration Cytology - Bethesda system); Serum TSH & Free T4; Anti-TPO
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Rapidly enlarging hard fixed nodule; Stridor or dyspnea; Hoarseness of voice (recurrent laryngeal nerve palsy); FNAC showing Bethesda V/VI (Malignancy)

Primary_Symptoms: Extreme, life-threatening hypermetabolic state: High fever (>103-105F), severe tachycardia (>140 bpm), delirium, agitation
Secondary_Symptoms: Profuse diaphoresis; Vomiting; Diarrhea; Jaundice; Cardiac arrhythmias (AFib); Hypotension/Shock; Coma
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Thyroid patient ko high fever (>103F), tez dhadkan (>140), aur behoshi/uljhan achanak hui hai?; 2. Ulti/dast ho rahe hain?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: None - emergency hospital referral
Popular_Indian_Brands: Injection Propylthiouracil / Carbimazole; Injection Hydrocortisone; Injection Propranolol; Lugol's Iodine
Dosage_Frequency: Immediate IV/NG ICU protocol: PTU first, followed by Iodine 1h later, IV Hydrocortisone, and Propranolol
Supportive_Medicines: ICU Admission; High-dose Antithyroid drugs (PTU/Carbimazole via NG tube); Oral Lugol's Iodine (1h post-PTU); IV Hydrocortisone 100 mg; IV Propranolol; Cooling blankets
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Life-threatening emergency with 10-30% mortality; NEVER GIVE ASPIRIN FOR FEVER IN THYROID STORM (aspirin displaces T4 from binding proteins, worsening storm); Use Paracetamol and physical cooling
Home_Care_Advice: Immediate emergency transfer to tertiary hospital ICU; Physical cooling with ice packs / cool blankets; Do NOT give Aspirin; Do NOT give oral fluids if confused
Lab_Investigations: Serum Free T3, Free T4, TSH (Burch-Wartofsky Point Scale >45 diagnostic); Complete Blood Count; LFT; Electrolytes; ECG; Blood Cultures
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Medical emergency - Immediate ER referral; Any suspected Thyroid Storm; High fever with extreme tachycardia and delirium in hyperthyroid patient

Common_Names_Hindi: Gout Flare; Rikht/Uric Acid ka dard
Primary_Symptoms: Sudden, excruciating, monoarticular joint pain, swelling, erythema, and severe warmth (Podagra - 1st metatarsophalangeal joint in 70%)
Secondary_Symptoms: Inability to bear weight or touch joint (even bedsheet hurts); Fever; Chills; Tophi (in chronic gout); Olecranon bursitis
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Pair ke angoothe (big toe) ya ghutne me achanak tez dard, sujan aur lalapan hua hai?; 2. Kapda chhoone par bhi dard hota hai?; 3. Uric acid bada hua hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Colchicine OR Indomethacin / Naproxen (Gout Flare Dose under Doctor)
Dosage_Frequency: Colchicine: 1 mg at onset, then 0.5 mg 1 hour later (max 1.5 mg total for flare) / Indomethacin TDS
Supportive_Medicines: Pantoprazole 40 mg OD; Ice pack application; Prednisolone oral 30 mg OD (if NSAIDs/Colchicine contraindicated)
Max_Safe_Limit_24h: 1.5 mg Colchicine total per acute flare / 1000 mg Naproxen
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Painkillers like NSAIDs or Colchicine are Rx/doctor-guided; NSAIDs STRICTLY AVOIDED in CKD, peptic ulcers, and Heart Failure; ASPIRIN STRICTLY AVOIDED (aspirin alters uric acid renal excretion and worsens gout); DO NOT START OR STOP ALLOPURINOL/FEBUXOSTAT DURING AN ACUTE FLARE (altering urate levels prolongs flare)
Home_Care_Advice: Apply ice pack wrapped in towel for 15 mins to inflamed joint; Rest and elevate joint; Drink 3 Liters of water daily; Strict low-purine diet (avoid red meat, organ meat, seafood, beer, and high-fructose corn syrup)
Lab_Investigations: Serum Uric Acid (may paradoxically be normal during acute flare); Joint Aspiration & Polarized Microscopy (monosodium urate crystals - negatively birefringent); CBC; X-ray joint; Serum Creatinine
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Polyarticular severe gout flare; High fever with suspected septic arthritis (joint infection rule out); Severe CKD patient with gout flare

Common_Names_Hindi: Purana Uric Acid; High Uric Acid
Primary_Symptoms: Asymptomatic elevated serum uric acid (>6.8-7.0 mg/dL) OR Recurrent gouty flares with Tophi / Urate Nephrolithiasis
Secondary_Symptoms: Polyarticular joint damage; Subcutaneous tophi on ears/joints; Chronic gouty arthropathy; Renal stones
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Uric acid kitne saal se 7.0 se upar bada hai?; 2. Baar-baar gout ka dard ya pathri (kidney stone) hoti hai?; 3. Koni/kaan par gummde (tophi) bane hain?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Febuxostat OR Allopurinol (Urate-Lowering Therapy strictly initiated AFTER acute flare resolves)
Supportive_Medicines: Low-dose Colchicine 0.5 mg OD for first 3-6 months (prophylaxis against urate mobilization flares); Hydration
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Never stop or change dose on your own; ALLOPURINOL OR FEBUXOSTAT MUST NOT BE STARTED DURING AN ACUTE GOUT FLARE (wait 2 weeks post flare); Allopurinol carries risk of severe SJS/TEN reaction (HLA-B*5801 screening in high risk); Febuxostat cardiovascular risk caution
Home_Care_Advice: Maintain high daily fluid intake (2.5-3 Liters/day); Strict low-purine diet (avoid alcohol/beer, red meat, organ meats, shellfish, sweet sodas); Lose weight gradually
Lab_Investigations: Serum Uric Acid (Target <6.0 mg/dL, or <5.0 mg/dL if tophi present); Serum Creatinine & eGFR; LFT; HLA-B*5801 allele (before Allopurinol); Renal USG
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Allopurinol reaction: skin rash, fever, mucosal lesions (STOP drug immediately - SJS risk); Sudden severe flank pain (renal colic); Acute gout flare trigger

Primary_Symptoms: Cluster of 3 or more: Abdominal Obesity (Waist >90 cm in Indian men, >80 cm in women), High BP (≥130/85), High Fasting Glucose (≥100)
Secondary_Symptoms: High Triglycerides (≥150 mg/dL); Low HDL (<40 mg/dL men, <50 women); Acanthosis nigricans; Fatty liver (NAFLD)
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Pet ki charbi (waist size), BP, aur Sugar teeno bade hue hain?; 2. Triglycerides high aur HDL low hai?; 3. Fatty liver report me aaya hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Metformin + Telmisartan + Atorvastatin (Targeted Drug Therapy per component) + Lifestyle Modification
Supportive_Medicines: Saroglitazar 4 mg OD (if NAFLD/mixed dyslipidemia); Fiber supplements; Weight loss program
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Primary management is intensive multi-component lifestyle modification; Drugs target individual risk components (HTN, Diabetes, Dyslipidemia); Monitor renal/liver function
Home_Care_Advice: Aim for 7-10% body weight loss; 150-300 mins/week moderate exercise; Strict Mediterranean/low-GI diet; Eliminate refined sugars, trans-fats, and alcohol; Stop smoking
Lab_Investigations: Fasting Blood Glucose & HbA1c; Fasting Lipid Profile; Waist Circumference; Blood Pressure Log; LFT & USG Abdomen (fatty liver grade); Serum Creatinine
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Progression to frank Type 2 Diabetes; Hypertensive crisis; Symptoms of CAD (chest pain) or Cerebrovascular disease

Primary_Symptoms: Body Mass Index (BMI) 23.0 to 24.9 kg/m² (Asian Indian Criteria); Increased abdominal fat; Fatigue on exertion
Secondary_Symptoms: Mild breathlessness on climbing stairs; Joint stiffness; Early insulin resistance; Snoring
Clarifying_Questions: 1. BMI 23-25 ke beech hai?; 2. Pet par charbi badh rahi hai?; 3. Daily physical activity kitni hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Lifestyle & Dietary Modification First-Line (No Weight-Loss Drugs for Overweight)
Supportive_Medicines: High fiber diet; Daily step tracking (8,000-10,000 steps); Behavior therapy
Precautions_Contraindications: Weight-loss drugs (Orlistat, Semaglutide) are NOT indicated for simple overweight without comorbidities; Primary intervention is calorie restriction and exercise
Home_Care_Advice: 500 kcal daily deficit diet; 150 mins/week moderate aerobic exercise; Eliminate liquid calories (sodas, juices, sweetened tea/coffee); Avoid late-night snacking
Lab_Investigations: BMI Calculation; Waist Circumference; Fasting Blood Glucose; Fasting Lipid Profile; Thyroid Function Test (TSH)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Progression of BMI ≥25 kg/m² (Obesity); Development of comorbidities (Hypertension, Prediabetes, Sleep Apnea)

Primary_Symptoms: BMI ≥25.0 kg/m² (Asian Indian Grade 1: 25-29.9, Grade 2: ≥30 kg/m²); Excessive body fat accumulation; Severe exertional dyspnea
Secondary_Symptoms: Obstructive Sleep Apnea; Osteoarthritis of knees; NAFLD; Acanthosis; Hypertension; Type 2 Diabetes; GERD
Clarifying_Questions: 1. BMI 25 se zyada (25-30 ya >30) hai?; 2. Motaape ke sath BP, Sugar ya Ghutne me dard hai?; 3. Snoring/neend me saans rukti hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Lifestyle First-Line OR Orlistat / Semaglutide (GLP-1 RA under Specialist for BMI ≥27 with comorbidities)
Dosage_Frequency: TDS (Orlistat 120 mg within 1 hour of fat-containing major meals) / OD (Semaglutide empty stomach)
Supportive_Medicines: Multivitamins (fat-soluble A, D, E, K taken 2h apart from Orlistat); Bariatric Surgery evaluation (if BMI >35)
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; WEIGHT-LOSS DRUGS (ORLISTAT, SEMAGLUTIDE) ARE RX AND MUST NOT BE GIVEN WITHOUT A DOCTOR; Orlistat causes oily spotting, flatus with discharge, and fat-soluble vitamin malabsorption; Semaglutide contraindicated in Medullary Thyroid Carcinoma history and Pancreatitis
Home_Care_Advice: Structured calorie-restricted diet (500-1000 kcal deficit); 200-300 mins/week physical activity; Behavioral counseling; Take fat-soluble multivitamins 2 hours before/after Orlistat
Lab_Investigations: BMI & Waist-to-Hip Ratio; Fasting Glucose & HbA1c; Lipid Profile; LFT & USG Abdomen; Serum Creatinine; TSH; Polysomnography
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Acute epigastric pain radiating to back (Pancreatitis risk on GLP-1 RA); Severe depression/mood changes; Gallstone colic symptoms

Primary_Symptoms: Triad (Rotterdam Criteria - at least 2): Oligo/Amenorrhea (irregular/delayed periods), Hyperandrogenism (hirsutism/acne), Polycystic ovaries on USG
Secondary_Symptoms: Infertility; Acanthosis nigricans; Central weight gain; Scalp hair thinning; Mood swings; Anxiety
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Periods mahino late ya irregular aate hain?; 2. Chehre par baal (hirsutism) ya acne hai?; 3. Ultrasound me PCOD ovaries aayi hain?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Combined Oral Contraceptive Pills (Ethinyl Estradiol + Cyproterone / Drospirenone) OR Metformin
Adult_Strength_Mg: 0.035 mg EE / 2 mg Cyproterone / 500 mg Metformin
Dosage_Frequency: OD (OCP daily for 21 days, 7 days gap) / BD (Metformin)
Supportive_Medicines: Myo-Inositol 2g + D-Chiro-Inositol 50 mg BD; Spironolactone 50 mg OD (anti-androgen); Clomiphene / Letrozole (for ovulation induction if conceiving)
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Oral Contraceptive Pills strictly CONTRAINDICATED in active smokers >35 years, thromboembolism history, severe hypertension, and migraine with aura; Metformin requires B12 monitoring
Home_Care_Advice: Weight reduction (5-10% weight loss restores regular ovulation); Low-GI diet; Daily exercise 30-45 mins; Manage stress
Lab_Investigations: USG Pelvis (transvaginal/abdominal - string of pearls polycystic ovaries); LH/FSH ratio (>2:1); Total & Free Testosterone; Fasting Insulin & OGTT; TSH & Prolactin
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Severe heavy prolonged uterine bleeding (dysfunctional uterine bleeding); Sudden severe pelvic pain (ovarian cyst torsion/rupture); Pregnancy test positive

Primary_Symptoms: Cessation of menses (>12 months); Vasomotor symptoms: Hot flashes, Night sweats; Vaginal dryness
Secondary_Symptoms: Insomnia; Mood swings; Irritability; Osteoporosis acceleration; Dyspareunia; Urinary frequency
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Periods 1 saal se zyada se aana band ho gaye hain?; 2. Achanak garmi lagna (hot flashes) aur raat ko pasiina aata hai?; 3. Mood swings hain?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Isoflavones / Phytoestrogens OR Hormone Replacement Therapy (HRT - Conjugated Estrogen + Medroxyprogesterone under Specialist)
Supportive_Medicines: Calcium Carbonate 500 mg + Vitamin D3 600 IU daily; Vaginal Estrogen Cream 0.01% (for local atrophy); SSRIs (Paroxetine for hot flashes if HRT contraindicated)
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Systemic Hormone Replacement Therapy (HRT) strictly CONTRAINDICATED in unexplained vaginal bleeding, breast/endometrial cancer history, active DVT/PE, arterial thromboembolism, and severe liver disease
Home_Care_Advice: Dress in layers; Avoid hot beverages, spicy foods, caffeine, and alcohol triggers; Use water-based vaginal lubricants for dryness; Weight-bearing exercises for bone health
Lab_Investigations: Dual-Energy X-ray Absorptiometry (DEXA Scan - Bone Mineral Density); Mammography; Pelvic Ultrasound (endometrial thickness <4-5 mm); Lipid Profile; TSH
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Any postmenopausal vaginal bleeding (MANDATORY evaluation to rule out Endometrial Carcinoma); Severe depression; Pathological fractures

Primary_Symptoms: Elevated Serum Prolactin (>25 ng/mL in women, >20 in men); Amenorrhea / Oligomenorrhea; Galactorrhea (breast milk discharge)
Secondary_Symptoms: Infertility; Erectile dysfunction & loss of libido in men; Headaches; Bitemporal hemianopia (if pituitary macroadenoma)
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Breast se bina pregnancy ke doodh (galactorrhea) nikalta hai?; 2. Periods band hain ya mard me sexual desire kam hui hai?; 3. Prolactin level kitna hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Cabergoline OR Bromocriptine
Supportive_Medicines: Vitamin D3 & Calcium; Review medication history (Antipsychotics, Metoclopramide, PPIs cause drug-induced hyperprolactinemia)
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; High-dose long-term Cabergoline requires Echocardiography monitoring for cardiac valvulopathy risk; Rule out drug-induced hyperprolactinemia and primary hypothyroidism first
Home_Care_Advice: Take Cabergoline with food/at bedtime to minimize nausea and dizziness; Avoid breast nipple stimulation; Regular follow-up with endocrinologist
Lab_Investigations: Serum Prolactin (fasting morning sample, avoid stress/breast exam prior); TSH (rule out hypothyroidism); Contrast-Enhanced MRI Pituitary / Brain; Serum Pregnancy Test
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Sudden onset severe thunderclap headache with visual field defects / double vision (Pituitary Apoplexy emergency); Severe galactorrhea

Primary_Symptoms: Hypercortisolism symptoms: Moon face, Buffalo hump (dorsocervical fat pad), Central obesity with thin extremities, Broad purple striae (>1 cm)
Secondary_Symptoms: Proximal muscle weakness; Hypertension; Osteoporosis; Impaired glucose tolerance; Hirsutism; Easy bruising
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Chehre par sujan (moon face), gardan ke piche fat (buffalo hump), aur pet par kaali/bagani phatne ke nishan (purple striae) hain?; 2. Steroid dawai pehle li thi?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Rx - specialist supervision required (Ketoconazole / Metyrapone / Surgical Pituitary or Adrenalectomy)
Supportive_Medicines: Calcium + Vitamin D3; Antihypertensives; Insulin/Oral anti-diabetics; Bone protection
Precautions_Contraindications: Rx - specialist supervision required; Most common cause is EXOGENOUS STEROID OVERUSE (AYUSH/unlicensed painkiller powders containing steroids) - do NOT stop steroids abruptly (causes fatal Adrenal Crisis); Ketoconazole hepatotoxicity risk
Home_Care_Advice: Do NOT stop prescribed oral/topical steroids abruptly; Avoid self-medicating with unlicensed painkiller powders; Low-sodium high-protein diet
Lab_Investigations: 24-hour Urinary Free Cortisol; Overnight 1 mg Dexamethasone Suppression Test (DST); Late-night Salivary Cortisol; Plasma ACTH; MRI Pituitary / CT Adrenals
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Medical emergency referral; Adrenal Crisis signs (hypotension, severe vomiting, abdominal pain, high fever post steroid withdrawal); Pathological fractures

Primary_Symptoms: Glucocorticoid/Mineralocorticoid deficiency: Profound fatigue, Weight loss, Hyperpigmentation (skin creases, palmar creases, buccal mucosa), Hypotension
Secondary_Symptoms: Postural dizziness; Salt craving; Nausea; Vomiting; Abdominal pain; Hypoglycemia; Vitiligo association
Typical_Duration: Chronic lifelong condition (Risk of Acute Crisis)
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Chamdi, hont aur hatheliyo par kaala-pan (pigmentation) aaya hai?; 2. BP bohut low rehta hai aur namak Khane ka man karta hai?; 3. Steroid dawai achanak band ki thi?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Rx - specialist supervision required (Hydrocortisone / Prednisolone + Fludrocortisone Replacement)
Adult_Strength_Mg: 15 to 25 mg Hydrocortisone total daily (split 2/3 morning, 1/3 afternoon) + 0.1 mg Fludrocortisone
Supportive_Medicines: Steroid Emergency Medical ID Card/Bracelet; Hydrocortisone 100 mg IM Emergency Self-Injection kit for sick days
Precautions_Contraindications: Rx - specialist supervision required; NEVER MISS OR STOP STEROID REPLACEMENT (stopping causes fatal Acute Adrenal Crisis); Mandatory 'Sick Day Rules': DOUBLE STEROID DOSE DURING FEVER, INFECTION, OR SURGERY
Home_Care_Advice: Wear a Medical Alert ID bracelet 'Adrenal Insufficiency - Steroid Dependent'; Double oral steroid dose during febrile illness/infection; Carry emergency IM Hydrocortisone injection always
Lab_Investigations: Short Synacthen / Cosyntropin Stimulation Test (Gold standard); Plasma ACTH; Morning Serum Cortisol (<3 mcg/dL diagnostic); Serum Electrolytes (Hyponatremia + Hyperkalemia); Anti-Adrenal Antibodies
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Acute Adrenal Crisis emergency: severe vomiting, severe abdominal pain, profound hypotension/shock, high fever, confusion (Requires immediate 100 mg IV Hydrocortisone + IV Saline)

Primary_Symptoms: Hypercalcemia Triad: 'Bones, Stones, Abdominal Groans, and Psychiatric Overtones' (Bone pain, Renal calculi, Constipation/Nausea, Depression)
Secondary_Symptoms: Osteopenia/Fractures; Polyuria; Polydipsia; Fatigue; Muscle weakness; Cardiac QT shortening
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Serum Calcium bada hua aaya hai (>10.5 mg/dL)?; 2. Baar-baar Kidney stone, haddi me dard, aur kabz rehti hai?; 3. Parathyroid Hormone (PTH) report kitni hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Rx - specialist supervision required (Cinacalcet OR Parathyroidectomy surgery)
Supportive_Medicines: Aggressive Oral Hydration (2.5-3 L/day); Bisphosphonates (Zoledronic acid for severe hypercalcemia); Vitamin D correction under specialist
Precautions_Contraindications: Rx - specialist supervision required; Severe Hypercalcemia (>12-14 mg/dL) is a medical emergency requiring IV saline and bisphosphonates; Cinacalcet requires frequent serum calcium monitoring (hypocalcemia risk)
Home_Care_Advice: Maintain high daily fluid intake (3 Liters/day) to prevent kidney stones and hypercalcemic crisis; Avoid thiazide diuretics and calcium supplements; Gentle weight-bearing exercise
Lab_Investigations: Serum Intact PTH (iPTH); Serum Calcium (total and ionized); Serum Phosphate (low); 24-hour Urinary Calcium; Sestamibi Parathyroid Scan; DEXA Scan
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Hypercalcemic Crisis: severe confusion, delirium, intractable vomiting, polyuria, cardiac arrhythmias, or Serum Calcium >14 mg/dL

Primary_Symptoms: Low Serum Sodium (<135 mEq/L; Severe <120 mEq/L); Mild: Nausea, headache, lethargy, gait unsteadiness, muscle cramps
Secondary_Symptoms: Severe: Confusion, disorientation, seizures, cerebral edema, coma, respiratory arrest
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Blood report me Sodium 135 se kam aaya hai?; 2. Sujan ki dawai (diuretic) chal rahi hai?; 3. Uljhan, chakkar ya ulti hui hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Treat Underlying Cause + Fluid Restriction (if SIADH) OR Oral Salt Tablets / 3% Hypertonic Saline IV (if severe in ER)
Popular_Indian_Brands: Tab Sodium Chloride 1g; 3% Hypertonic Saline IV
Supportive_Medicines: Tolvaptan 15 mg OD (Vasopressin receptor antagonist for SIADH under specialist); Normal Saline 0.9% IV (if hypovolemic)
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; NEVER OVER-CORRECT SERUM SODIUM TOO RAPIDLY (>8-10 mEq/L in 24 hours) due to risk of fatal Central Pontine Myelinolysis (Osmotic Demyelination Syndrome); Loop diuretics caution
Home_Care_Advice: If SIADH/hypervolemic hyponatremia: restrict fluid intake to <800-1000 mL/day as advised; Do not drink excess water blindly; Take prescribed salt tablets
Lab_Investigations: Serum Electrolytes (Sodium, Potassium); Serum & Urine Osmolality; Urinary Sodium Concentration; Thyroid Profile; Morning Cortisol
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Severe Hyponatremia (<120 mEq/L); Seizures; Confusion/Disorientation; Coma; Gait instability causing falls

Primary_Symptoms: Low Serum Potassium (<3.5 mEq/L; Severe <2.5 mEq/L); Generalized muscle weakness, leg cramps, fatigue, constipation
Secondary_Symptoms: Paralytic ileus; Cardiac arrhythmias (flattened T waves, U waves, ST depression); Muscle fasciculations; Flaccid paralysis
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Potassium report 3.5 se kam aayi hai?; 2. Pairo me achanak kamzori ya kramps hue hain?; 3. Dast, ulti ya paani ki dawai (diuretic) chal rahi hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Potassium Chloride (Oral Syrup / Sustained Release Tablets) OR IV KCl (if severe in ICU)
Adult_Strength_Mg: 15 to 30 mL (Potassium Chloride syrup - 20 mEq/15 mL)
Dosage_Frequency: BD or TDS (Diluted in a full glass of water)
Supportive_Medicines: Spironolactone / Amiloride (potassium-sparing diuretics); Magnesium supplementation (hypomagnesemia refractory hypokalemia)
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Oral Potassium Chloride liquid MUST BE DILUTED in a full glass of water/juice to prevent severe GI mucosal ulceration; IV Potassium KCl MUST NEVER BE GIVEN AS AN IV PUSHOVER/BOLUS (causes fatal cardiac arrest)
Home_Care_Advice: Take potassium syrup diluted in water/juice immediately after meals; Do not take on empty stomach; Avoid loop diuretics without potassium monitoring
Lab_Investigations: Serum Electrolytes (Potassium, Sodium, Magnesium); Serum Creatinine; ECG (U waves, ST depression, ventricular arrhythmias); ABG
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Severe Hypokalemia (<2.5 mEq/L); Flaccid muscle paralysis / inability to move limbs; Cardiac arrhythmias; Breathlessness (respiratory muscle paralysis)

Specialty_Category: Nephrology / Cardiology / Critical Care / Emergency Medicine
Primary_Symptoms: High Serum Potassium (>5.5 mEq/L; Severe >6.5 mEq/L); Often asymptomatic; Severe muscle weakness, flaccid paralysis
Secondary_Symptoms: Paresthesias; Cardiac Arrhythmias (tall peaked T waves, QRS widening, sine wave pattern); Bradycardia; Cardiac arrest
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Blood report me Potassium 5.5 se upar aaya hai?; 2. Kidney ki bimari (CKD) hai ya ACEi/ARB dawai chal rahi hai?; 3. Heart beat dheemi hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: None - emergency hospital referral
Popular_Indian_Brands: Injection Calcium Gluconate 10%; Injection Glucose 25% + Regular Insulin; Tab Calcium Polystyrene Sulfonate
Dosage_Frequency: Immediate IV emergency administration in ICU / ER
Supportive_Medicines: Emergency Cardiac Membrane Stabilization: IV Calcium Gluconate 10% 10 mL; Shift K+ into cells: IV Glucose 50g + 10 U Regular Insulin + Nebulized Salbutamol; K+ Excretion: Oral Calcium Polystyrene Sulfonate (K-Bind) 15g TDS; Emergency Hemodialysis
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Life-threatening emergency; High risk of sudden fatal cardiac arrest / ventricular fibrillation; STOP ALL POTASSIUM SUPPLEMENTS, ACEi/ARBs, SPIRONOLACTONE IMMEDIATELY
Home_Care_Advice: Immediate emergency transfer to hospital ER/ICU; Stop all potassium supplements, salt substitutes, ACEi/ARBs, and NSAIDs immediately; Do NOT drink fruit juices
Lab_Investigations: 12-lead ECG (immediate - check peaked T waves, prolonged PR, wide QRS); Serum Electrolytes (Potassium repeat); Serum Creatinine; ABG
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Medical emergency - Immediate ER referral; Serum Potassium >6.0 mEq/L; ECG changes of hyperkalemia; Severe muscle weakness; Bradycardia

Common_Names_Hindi: Kidney ki shuruaati bimari; CKD Stage 1-2
Primary_Symptoms: Kidney damage with normal or mildly reduced eGFR (≥60-90 mL/min/1.73m²); Persistent Microalbuminuria/Proteinuria; Asymptomatic
Secondary_Symptoms: Mild hypertension; Microscopic hematuria; Early nocturia; Normal serum creatinine or mild elevation
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Urine me protein (albumin) aaya hai?; 2. eGFR 60 se upar hai par kidney damaged hai?; 3. High BP ya Diabetes ki purani history hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Telmisartan OR Ramipril + Dapagliflozin (SGLT2 inhibitor for renal protection)
Supportive_Medicines: Metformin (dose adjusted for eGFR); Lipid lowering therapy (Atorvastatin); Low-salt diet
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Never stop or change dose on your own; ACEi/ARBs require baseline and periodic K+ and creatinine checks; AVOID ALL NSAID PAINKILLERS STRICTLY (Ibuprofen, Diclofenac cause acute renal decline - use Paracetamol for pain)
Home_Care_Advice: Strict BP control (<130/80) and Glucose control; Low-salt diet (<2g/day); Complete cessation of smoking; Avoid all OTC NSAID painkillers and unknown AYUSH powders
Lab_Investigations: Serum Creatinine & eGFR (CKD-EPI formula); Urinary Albumin-to-Creatinine Ratio (UACR); Serum Electrolytes; Fasting Glucose & HbA1c; Renal Ultrasound
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Rapid rise in serum creatinine (>30% from baseline); Onset of pedal edema or facial puffiness; Uncontrolled hypertension; Hematuria

Primary_Symptoms: Moderate to severe decline in eGFR (<60 mL/min; Stage 5 eGFR <15); Bilateral pedal edema; Anemia; Anorexia; Nausea
Secondary_Symptoms: Uremic pruritus; Metallic taste; Foamy urine; Oliguria; Bone pain; Muscle cramps; Pericarditis; Encephalopathy
Clarifying_Questions: 1. eGFR 60 se kam hai ya Creatinine bada hua hai?; 2. Pairo par sujan, khoon ki kami, aur ulti jaisa lagta hai?; 3. Dialysis ki baat hui hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Rx - specialist supervision required (Nephrologist-guided GDMT + Anemia & Mineral Bone Disease Management)
Supportive_Medicines: Injection Recombinant Human Erythropoietin (Alfa/Beta) SC weekly; Oral Iron; Alpha-Ketoanalogues (Ketosteril); Sodium Bicarbonate; Renal Replacement Therapy (Hemodialysis / Peritoneal Dialysis / Kidney Transplant)
Precautions_Contraindications: Rx - specialist supervision required; AVOID ALL NSAIDs, AMINOGLYCOSIDES, AND CONTRAST DYES STRICTLY; Adjust doses of all renal-cleared drugs based on eGFR; Monitor for Hyperkalemia; Avoid high-potassium foods
Home_Care_Advice: Strict Low-Protein (0.6g/kg/day), Low-Sodium (<2g/day), Low-Potassium, and Low-Phosphorus diet; Strict fluid restriction as advised by nephrologist; Daily weight tracking
Lab_Investigations: Serum Creatinine & eGFR; Serum Electrolytes (Potassium, Sodium, Bicarbonate); Serum Calcium & Phosphate; Intact PTH; Complete Blood Count (Hb); Renal USG
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Medical emergency / Urgent Dialysis referral; Uremic signs: pericardial rub, uremic encephalopathy/confusion, intractable vomiting, refractory hyperkalemia (>6.5), acute pulmonary edema, or Anuria

Primary_Symptoms: Early marker of kidney damage and vascular disease; Urinary Albumin 30-300 mg/day (UACR 30-300 mg/g); Asymptomatic
Secondary_Symptoms: Mild hypertension; Early diabetic nephropathy stage; Absence of overt nephrotic syndrome
Typical_Duration: Chronic reversible state with early treatment
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Peshab ki janch me Microalbumin (30-300 mg/g) aaya hai?; 2. Diabetes ya High BP hai?; 3. Pairo me sujan hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Telmisartan OR Ramipril + Dapagliflozin / Empagliflozin
Supportive_Medicines: Low-salt diet; Strict glycemic control; Statin therapy
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Never stop or change dose on your own; ACEi/ARBs slow progression to overt proteinuria; Monitor baseline serum creatinine and potassium; Avoid NSAIDs strictly
Home_Care_Advice: Maintain strict glycemic control (HbA1c <7.0%) and BP control (<130/80 mm Hg); Low-salt diet; Avoid OTC NSAID painkillers; Stop smoking
Lab_Investigations: Urinary Albumin-to-Creatinine Ratio (UACR - spot morning sample); Serum Creatinine & eGFR; Serum Electrolytes; Fasting Blood Glucose & HbA1c
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Progression to Macroalbuminuria (UACR >300 mg/g); Rise in serum creatinine; Onset of generalized edema

Primary_Symptoms: Sudden rapid decline in kidney function (hours to days): Oliguria (<400 mL/day) or Anuria; Rapid rise in Serum Creatinine
Secondary_Symptoms: Fluid retention; Bilateral pedal edema; Nausea; Vomiting; Confusion; Asterixis; Hyperkalemia; Uremic breath odor
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Peshab ki matra achanak kam (oliguria) hui hai?; 2. Creatinine report achanak badh gayi hai?; 3. Severe dast, ulti, infection, ya painkiller li thi?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: None - emergency hospital referral
Popular_Indian_Brands: Injection Furosemide; IV Normal Saline (if prerenal); Injection Calcium Gluconate (if hyperkalemic)
Dosage_Frequency: Immediate IV emergency protocol in ICU
Supportive_Medicines: ICU Admission; Treat underlying cause (IV fluids for prerenal dehydration; Remove nephrotoxins; Relief of urinary obstruction); Emergency Hemodialysis if uremic/hyperkalemic
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Life-threatening emergency; STOP ALL NEPHROTOXIC DRUGS IMMEDIATELY (NSAIDs, ACEi/ARBs, Aminoglycosides); Immediate hospital admission required
Home_Care_Advice: Immediate emergency transfer to hospital nephrology ICU; Stop all NSAIDs, ACEi/ARBs, and diuretics immediately; Do NOT drink excessive water if anuric
Lab_Investigations: Serum Creatinine & Blood Urea (serial daily checks); Serum Electrolytes (Potassium monitoring); Renal Ultrasound (rule out post-renal obstruction); ABG; Urine Routine & Fractions
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Medical emergency - Immediate ER referral; Anuria (>12 hours no urine); Severe Hyperkalemia (>6.5 mEq/L); Acute pulmonary edema; Uremic encephalopathy

Common_Names_Hindi: Gurde ki pathri ka dard; Renal Colic
Primary_Symptoms: Sudden onset excruciating, writhing flank pain radiating to groin/labia/scrotum; Hematuria (pink/red urine)
Secondary_Symptoms: Nausea; Repeated vomiting; Dysuria; Urinary frequency; Restlessness (inability to find comfortable position); Low fever
Typical_Duration: Acute episode (hours to days until stone passes or treated)
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Kamar/kakh (flank) me achanak tez marod waala dard hua hai jo aage guptang tak ja raha hai?; 2. Peshab me lalapan ya jalan hai?; 3. Ulti ho rahi hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Tamsulosin + Diclofenac / Tramadol (for Acute Colic & Stone Expulsion Therapy)
Supportive_Medicines: Disodium Hydrogen Citrate syrup (alkalinizer) 10 mL TDS in water; Drotaverine 80 mg TDS for spasm; Hydration
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; SEVERE RENAL COLIC REQUIRES DOCTOR EVALUATION; NSAIDs (Diclofenac) STRICTLY AVOIDED in patients with pre-existing kidney impairment (CKD/elevated creatinine); Tamsulosin causes orthostatic dizziness; Avoid NSAIDs if solitary kidney
Home_Care_Advice: Drink 2.5 to 3 Liters of water daily (UNLESS ANURIC OR SEVERELY OBSTRUCTED); Strain urine through cloth/mesh to catch passed stone for analysis; Jump and hydration therapy for small stones (<5 mm)
Lab_Investigations: Ultrasound KUB (detect hydronephrosis/stone size); Non-Contrast CT KUB (NCCT - Gold standard); Urine Routine & Microscopy (RBCs, crystals, infection); Serum Creatinine & Uric Acid
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; High fever with rigors and cloudy urine (Infected Hydronephrosis - Urological Emergency); Complete inability to pass urine (Anuria); Unremitting vomiting

Primary_Symptoms: Heavy Proteinuria (>3.5g/24h or UPCR >2); Severe Hypoalbuminemia (<3.0 g/dL); Generalized Edema (Anasarca: facial puffiness, leg edema, ascites)
Secondary_Symptoms: Hyperlipidemia (High Total Cholesterol/LDL); Frothy urine; Hypercoagulability (DVT/Renal vein thrombosis risk); Infections
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Peshab me bahut zyada jhaag (froth) aata hai?; 2. Subah aankho ke paas aur pairo par severe sujan (anasarca) rehti hai?; 3. Albumin kam aur Cholesterol bada hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Rx - specialist supervision required (High-dose Systemic Corticosteroids - Prednisolone / Cyclophosphamide / Tacrolimus)
Supportive_Medicines: Loop Diuretics (Furosemide + Spironolactone); ACEi/ARBs (to reduce proteinuria); Statins; Prophylactic Anticoagulation (if Albumin <2.0)
Precautions_Contraindications: Rx - specialist supervision required; High infection risk due to urinary loss of immunoglobulins; High-dose steroids require close monitoring of blood sugar, BP, growth (in children), and bone density; Pneumococcal vaccination recommended
Home_Care_Advice: Strict Low-Sodium diet (<1.5-2g/day); Fluid restriction as advised by nephrologist; Normal-protein balanced diet (do NOT eat excessive protein as it worsens renal lesion); Daily weight check
Lab_Investigations: 24-hour Urinary Protein quantification / UPCR; Serum Albumin; Serum Lipid Profile; Serum Creatinine & eGFR; Renal Biopsy (Light, DIF, Electron Microscopy); Antinuclear Antibodies (ANA)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Sudden severe flank pain with gross hematuria (Renal Vein Thrombosis); Severe acute dyspnea (pulmonary embolism or pleural effusion); High fever with abdominal pain (Spontaneous Bacterial Peritonitis)

Primary_Symptoms: Lower Urinary Tract Symptoms (LUTS) in aging men: Weak urinary stream, Hesitancy, Frequency, Nocturia (waking >2 times to void)
Secondary_Symptoms: Urgency; Feeling of incomplete bladder emptying; Post-void dribbling; Acute Urinary Retention risk
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Umar 50+ hai aur peshab ki dhaar patli ya ruk-ruk kar aati hai?; 2. Raat ko baar-baar peshab ke liye uthna padta hai?; 3. Peshab bilkul ruka hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Tamsulosin OR Tamsulosin + Dutasteride
Dosage_Frequency: OD (At Bedtime 30 min after same meal)
Supportive_Medicines: Finasteride 5 mg OD (for large prostates >40g); Plant extracts (Saw Palmetto)
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Never stop or change dose on your own; Tamsulosin causes Intraoperative Floppy Iris Syndrome (IFIS) during cataract surgery (inform eye surgeon) and orthostatic dizziness; Dutasteride lowers PSA by 50% (adjust PSA interpretation); Contraindicated in women
Home_Care_Advice: Limit fluid intake 2 hours before bedtime; Avoid caffeine and alcohol in evening; Double voiding technique (wait 1 min and try voiding again); Do not delay urination when urge occurs
Lab_Investigations: Serum Prostate-Specific Antigen (PSA - rule out prostate cancer); Digital Rectal Examination (DRE); Ultrasound KUB with Post-Void Residual (PVR) volume; Uroflowmetry
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Acute Urinary Retention (complete inability to void with severe painful lower abdominal distension - emergency catheterization needed); Gross hematuria; High fever with rigors (Acute Prostatitis)

Primary_Symptoms: Perineal, pelvic, ejaculatory, or suprapubic pain/discomfort lasting >3 months; Lower Urinary Tract Symptoms (LUTS)
Secondary_Symptoms: Dysuria; Urinary frequency; Pain at tip of penis; Pain after ejaculation; Low back pain; Sexual dysfunction
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Naabhi ke niche, perineum (gutti ke paas) ya ejaculation ke baad dard hota hai?; 2. Peshab me jalan aur baar-baar aana hai?; 3. Reports me infection aata hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Tamsulosin + Ciprofloxacin / Levofloxacin (if Bacterial) OR NSAIDs + Phytotherapy
Duration_Days: 14 to 28 days (Antibiotics 4-6 weeks for Chronic Bacterial Prostatitis)
Supportive_Medicines: Sitz bath; Quercetin / Cernilton; Anti-inflammatory agents; Pelvic floor physical therapy
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Fluoroquinolones (Ciprofloxacin/Levofloxacin) carry tendonitis/tendon rupture warnings; Prolonged antibiotic courses (4-6 weeks) required for bacterial prostatitis to penetrate prostate tissue
Home_Care_Advice: Warm Sitz bath for 15 mins 2-3 times daily; Avoid prolonged sitting on hard surfaces (use donut cushion); Avoid cycling, alcohol, spicy foods, and caffeine
Lab_Investigations: Meares-Stamey 4-Glass Test / 2-Glass Pre- and Post-Prostate Massage Urine Culture; Serum PSA; Urine Routine & Microscopy; Pelvic USG
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; High fever with rigors, severe dysuria, and acute retention (Acute Bacterial Prostatitis - emergency hospital care); Prostatic abscess signs

Common_Names_Hindi: Overactive Bladder; Peshab na rukna; OAB
Primary_Symptoms: Urinary Urgency (sudden compelling desire to void that is difficult to defer); Frequency (≥8 times/day); Nocturia
Secondary_Symptoms: Urge Urinary Incontinence (involuntary leakage accompanied by urgency); Absence of UTI or structural pathology; Stress
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Peshab aane par bilkul roka nahi jata (urgency)?; 2. Din me 8-10 baar aur raat me baar-baar jana padta hai?; 3. Peshab raste me leak ho jata hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Mirabegron OR Solifenacin / Tolterodine
Supportive_Medicines: Pelvic floor muscle training (Kegel exercises); Bladder training therapy
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Solifenacin / Tolterodine (Anticholinergics) STRICTLY CONTRAINDICATED in narrow-angle glaucoma, severe urinary retention, and gastric retention; Mirabegron caution in severe uncontrolled HTN (monitor BP)
Home_Care_Advice: Bladder training (timed voiding, gradually increasing interval between voids); Kegel pelvic floor exercises; Avoid caffeine, sodas, artificial sweeteners, and alcohol; Reduce evening fluid intake
Lab_Investigations: Urine Routine & Microscopy (rule out UTI/hematuria); Post-Void Residual (PVR) volume ultrasound; Frequency-Volume Bladder Diary (3 days); Urodynamic Study
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Gross hematuria (blood in urine); Acute urinary retention; High fever with flank pain (Pyelonephritis); Persistent symptoms non-responsive to oral therapy

Primary_Symptoms: Involuntary leakage of urine; Types: Stress (leakage on coughing/sneezing/laughing), Urge (leakage with urgency), or Mixed
Secondary_Symptoms: Frequency; Urgency; Perianal skin excoriation; Embarrassment; Disturbed sleep; Social isolation
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Khaansne, chinkne, ya wazan uthane par peshab leak hota hai (Stress Incontinence)?; 2. Ya tez bladder bharne par rok nahi paate (Urge Incontinence)?; 3. Delivery ki history hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Pelvic Floor Muscle Training First-Line + Duloxetine (for Stress UI) OR Solifenacin / Mirabegron (for Urge UI)
Supportive_Medicines: Incontinence pads; Pessary insertion (for pelvic organ prolapse); Surgical Tension-Free Vaginal Tape (TVT/TOT under Urogynaecologist)
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Primary therapy for Stress UI is non-pharmacological Pelvic Floor Muscle Training (Kegels); Anticholinergics (Solifenacin) contraindicated in glaucoma and retention; Duloxetine caution in liver disease
Home_Care_Advice: Perform Kegel pelvic floor exercises 3 times daily (10 repetitions holding for 5-10 sec); Maintain ideal weight; Avoid constipation; Avoid caffeine/alcohol; Use absorbent pads
Lab_Investigations: Urine Routine & Culture; Post-Void Residual (PVR) Ultrasound; Stress Cough Test; Urodynamic Testing (UCM/Pad test)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Overflow incontinence (continuous dribbling with distended painless bladder); Hematuria; Pelvic organ prolapse protruding outside vagina; Recurrent UTIs

Primary_Symptoms: Persistent inability to attain or maintain a penile erection sufficient for satisfactory sexual performance (>3 months)
Secondary_Symptoms: Loss of morning erections; Decreased libido; Premature ejaculation association; Performance anxiety; Fatigue
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Sambhog (sex) ke liye ling me kadak-pan (erection) nahi aata ya tikta nahi?; 2. Morning me erection aata hai?; 3. BP, Diabetes, ya Heart ki dawai khaate hain?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Sildenafil OR Tadalafil (PDE5 Inhibitors)
Dosage_Frequency: SOS 30-60 min before sexual activity (Sildenafil) OR 10-20 mg SOS / 5 mg OD daily (Tadalafil)
Meal_Timing: Empty Stomach or Light Meal (Sildenafil) / Before or After Food (Tadalafil)
Supportive_Medicines: Psychosexual counseling; Testosterone replacement (ONLY if documented hypogonadism); Vacuum Erection Device
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; PDE5 INHIBITORS (SILDENAFIL, TADALAFIL) ARE STRICTLY CONTRAINDICATED WITH NITRATES (ISOSORBIDE, NITROGLYCERIN SPRAY/TABS) AND NICORANDIL DUE TO FATAL HYPOTENSIVE SHOCK; STRICTLY CONTRAINDICATED IN RECENT HEART ATTACK (<6 WEEKS), UNSTABLE ANGINA, AND SEVERE STROKE; Caution with Alpha-blockers (Tamsulosin)
Home_Care_Advice: Take tablet as prescribed (Sildenafil works best on empty stomach); Limit alcohol intake (alcohol reduces erection quality); Exercise regularly; Manage stress; Treat underlying Diabetes/HTN
Lab_Investigations: Serum Total Testosterone (8-10 AM sample); Fasting Blood Glucose & HbA1c; Lipid Profile; Thyroid Profile; Penile Doppler Ultrasound
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Priapism (painful prolonged erection lasting >4 hours - Urological Emergency requiring aspiration to prevent permanent impotence); Chest pain during sexual intercourse

Primary_Symptoms: Persistent or recurrent ejaculation occurring within ~1 minute of vaginal penetration (Lifelong PE) or significant reduction to <3 min (Acquired PE)
Secondary_Symptoms: Inability to delay ejaculation; Severe personal distress; Frustration; Avoidance of sexual intimacy; Anxiety
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Sambhog ke waqt 1 minute ke andar ejaculation (virya nikalna) ho jata hai?; 2. Ejaculation par control nahi rehta?; 3. Partner aur aapko distress hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Dapoxetine (Short-acting Selective Serotonin Reuptake Inhibitor)
Dosage_Frequency: SOS 1 to 3 hours BEFORE intended sexual activity
Meal_Timing: Before or After Food with full glass of water
Supportive_Medicines: Topical Lignocaine/Prilocaine spray/cream applied 15 min before sex; Behavioral therapy ('Squeeze' and 'Stop-Start' techniques); Counseling
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Dapoxetine is Rx; Contraindicated with MAOIs, SSRIs, and potent CYP3A4 inhibitors; Caution for orthostatic syncope/dizziness (always take with a full glass of water); Do NOT take daily, use SOS only
Home_Care_Advice: Perform 'Stop-Start' and 'Squeeze' behavioral control techniques during intercourse; Take tablet 1-3 hours before sex with a full glass of water; Reduce performance anxiety; Avoid excess alcohol
Lab_Investigations: Clinical diagnostic evaluation (IELT - Intravaginal Ejaculatory Latency Time assessment); Urine Routine; Fasting Blood Glucose; Thyroid Profile (rule out Hyperthyroidism)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Syncope or severe dizziness post medication; Severe clinical depression; Co-existing severe Erectile Dysfunction needing combination therapy

Primary_Symptoms: Documented Serum Total Testosterone <300 ng/dL (morning sample) with symptoms: Low libido, Erectile Dysfunction, Fatigue, Muscle mass loss
Secondary_Symptoms: Increased body fat; Gynecocomastia; Osteoporosis; Mood swings; Irritability; Hot flashes (in severe deficiency); Anemia
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Blood report me Total Testosterone 300 ng/dL se kam aaya hai?; 2. Sexual Desire (libido) kam hui hai, thakan aur muscle kam hui hai?; 3. Subah 8-10 baje test hua tha?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Rx - specialist supervision required (Testosterone Replacement Therapy - TRT Injection / Gel under Specialist)
Adult_Strength_Mg: 250 mg IM Injection (Testosterone Enanthate) / 5g gel packet (50 mg Testosterone)
Dosage_Frequency: Deep IM injection every 2 to 3 weeks OR Gel applied once daily on clean shoulders/abdomen in morning
Supportive_Medicines: Calcium + Vitamin D3; Weight training exercises; Annual Prostate screening
Precautions_Contraindications: Rx - specialist supervision required; TESTOSTERONE THERAPY IS RX AND SPECIALIST-LED; DO NOT SUGGEST SELF-MEDICATION OR OTC SUPPLEMENTS; Strictly CONTRAINDICATED in Prostate Cancer, Breast Cancer in men, Hematocrit >50-54%, Severe untreated BPH, and uncontrolled Heart Failure; Infertility risk (suppresses spermatogenesis)
Home_Care_Advice: Apply Testosterone gel strictly in morning on clean dry skin of upper arms/shoulders; Wash hands with soap immediately after gel application; Do NOT let female partner or children touch application site; Weight training
Lab_Investigations: Serum Total Testosterone (fasting 8-10 AM sample, repeat to confirm); Serum Free Testosterone; LH & FSH; Serum PSA & DRE (mandatory before and during TRT); CBC (Hematocrit/Hb); LFT & Lipid Profile
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Hematocrit >54% (polycythemia); PSA elevation (>4.0 ng/dL or rapid rise); Prostate nodule on DRE; Severe obstructive sleep apnea flare

Primary_Symptoms: Profound, unexplained, debilitating fatigue lasting >6 months NOT relieved by rest and worsened by exertion (Post-Exertional Malaise - PEM)
Secondary_Symptoms: Unrefreshing sleep; Brain fog/cognitive impairment; Orthostatic intolerance; Myalgia; Arthralgia; Sore throat; Tender lymph nodes
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Thakan 6 mahine se zyada se hai aur aaram karne par bhi teek nahi hoti?; 2. Thoda sa kaam karne par fatigue agle din severe badhta hai (PEM)?; 3. Neend khulne par fresh nahi lagta?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Symptomatic & Pacing Management First-Line (No Drug Cures CFS; Meds for co-symptoms)
Supportive_Medicines: Low-dose Coenzyme Q10 / L-Carnitine; Melatonin 3 mg at bedtime (for sleep); Pregabalin / Duloxetine (if co-existing fibromyalgic pain under doctor)
Precautions_Contraindications: NO DRUG CURES CHRONIC FATIGUE SYNDROME; Primary therapy is Activity Pacing and Energy Envelope Management; Avoid Graded Exercise Therapy if it triggers Post-Exertional Malaise (PEM); Do NOT rely on sedatives or self-medication
Home_Care_Advice: Practice strict Activity Pacing (break activities into small rest periods, do not push through fatigue); Maintain strict sleep hygiene; Balanced nutrition; Hydrate well
Lab_Investigations: Exclusionary Workup: Complete Blood Count; TSH; Serum Ferritin; Vitamin D3 & B12; ESR/CRP; Electrolytes; Liver & Kidney Function; ANA (All must be normal/ruled out)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Appearance of new organic red flags (unexplained weight loss, persistent fever, night sweats, lymphadenopathy, severe neurological deficits)

Primary_Symptoms: Widespread musculoskeletal pain lasting >3 months across multiple body quadrants with tender points; Severe fatigue
Secondary_Symptoms: Unrefreshing sleep; Brain fog (fibro-fog); Morning stiffness; Irritable Bowel Syndrome co-existence; Anxiety; Headaches
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Poore sharir aur manspeshiyo me 3 mahine se zyada se dard rehta hai?; 2. Chhoone par jagah-jagah meetha/tez dard hota hai?; 3. Neend poori nahi hoti aur fatigue rehta hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Pregabalin OR Duloxetine OR Amitriptyline (No Drug Cures; First-Line is Lifestyle + Doctor-Guided Therapy)
Dosage_Frequency: OD or BD (Pregabalin) / OD in morning (Duloxetine) / OD at bedtime (Amitriptyline)
Supportive_Medicines: Gentle low-impact aerobic exercise (hydrotherapy, walking, cycling); Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT); Heat therapy
Max_Safe_Limit_24h: 150 mg Pregabalin / 60 mg Duloxetine / 50 mg Amitriptyline
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; NO DRUG CURES FIBROMYALGIA; Medications manage centralized pain transmission; Do NOT list opioids or strong sedatives (opioids are ineffective and harmful in fibromyalgia); Pregabalin/Amitriptyline caution for drowsiness
Home_Care_Advice: Engage in regular gentle low-impact exercise (swimming, walking, warm water exercise); Maintain consistent sleep schedule; Heat compresses for sore muscles; Stress reduction (mindfulness/yoga)
Lab_Investigations: Exclusionary Panel: ESR & CRP (typically normal in Fibromyalgia); Serum Vitamin D3 & B12; Thyroid Profile (TSH); Complete Blood Count; Rheumatoid Factor & Anti-CCP
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Severe clinical depression with suicidal ideation; Sudden localized joint swelling or hot red joint (rule out inflammatory arthritis); Muscle weakness

Common_Names_Hindi: Cigarette / Bidi ki aadat; Nicotine Addiction
Primary_Symptoms: Compulsive use of tobacco products (cigarettes, bidi, gutka, paan masala); Craving; Irritability/anxiety on withdrawal
Secondary_Symptoms: Inability to quit despite harm; Tolerance; Morning nicotine urge; Cough; Reduced stamina
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Bidi, Cigarette, Gutka ya Khaini kitne saal se use kar rahe hain?; 2. Chhodne par ghabraahat, chidchidapan aur craving hoti hai?; 3. Subah uthte hi urge hoti hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Nicotine Replacement Therapy (NRT - Nicotine Polacrilex Gum / Patch OTC) OR Varenicline / Bupropion (Rx under Doctor)
Dosage_Frequency: Gum: 1 piece every 1-2 hours SOS when craving occurs (Max 24 pieces/day) / Bupropion OD then BD
Supportive_Medicines: Behavioral cessation counseling; Nicotine transdermal patch (7, 14, 21 mg); Deep breathing exercises
Max_Safe_Limit_24h: 24 pieces of 2 mg Nicotine Gum daily
Precautions_Contraindications: NICOTINE GUM/PATCHES ARE OTC; VARENICLINE AND BUPROPION ARE RX; Nicotine gum caution in acute MI (<2 weeks), severe arrhythmias, and pregnancy; Bupropion strictly CONTRAINDICATED in seizure disorders and eating disorders
Home_Care_Advice: Use 'Chew and Park' technique for Nicotine gum (chew slowly until tingle, then park between cheek and gum for 30 mins); Avoid acidic drinks (coffee/soda) 15 mins before chewing; Identify smoking triggers
Lab_Investigations: Fagestrom Test for Nicotine Dependence (FTND score); Carbon Monoxide (CO) breath monitoring; Spirometry; Chest X-ray
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Severe withdrawal depression or suicidal ideation on quitting; Seizures on Bupropion; Chest pain or arrhythmia while using NRT

Primary_Symptoms: Compulsive alcohol consumption despite social/occupational/health harm; Tolerance; Craving; Inability to cut down
Secondary_Symptoms: Loss of control; Neglect of responsibilities; Withdrawal symptoms on cessation; Liver dysfunction; Memory blackouts
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Sharab ki waja se ghar/kaam me pareshani ho rahi hai?; 2. Sharab kam karne ki koshish ki par nahi hua?; 3. Daily kitni sharab peete hain?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Rx - specialist supervision required (Anti-craving Therapy - Acamprosate / Naltrexone / Disulfiram under Specialist)
Duration_Days: Rx - specialist supervision required (6 to 12 months)
Supportive_Medicines: Thiamine (Vitamin B1) 100 mg TDS; B-complex; De-addiction Psychotherapy / Alcoholics Anonymous (AA) support groups
Precautions_Contraindications: Rx - specialist supervision required; TREATMENT IS UNDER MEDICAL SUPERVISION ONLY; Disulfiram strictly CONTRAINDICATED without patient's explicit consent (causes severe acetaldehyde reaction with alcohol: flushing, vomiting, shock); Naltrexone contraindicated in acute hepatitis/liver failure and opioid users
Home_Care_Advice: Join Alcoholics Anonymous (AA) support groups; Complete family counseling; Total lifestyle shift away from alcohol-centric social circles; Nutritious diet rich in B-vitamins
Lab_Investigations: Liver Function Test (AST/ALT ratio, Gamma-GT); Complete Blood Count (MCV); Ultrasound Abdomen; Serum Electrolytes; Carbohydrate-Deficient Transferrin (CDT)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Signs of severe Alcohol Withdrawal (Delirium Tremens): severe tremors, visual/auditory hallucinations, seizures, high fever, extreme confusion

Common_Names_Hindi: Sharab chhodne par daure; Alcohol Withdrawal
Primary_Symptoms: Autonomic hyperactivity 6-48 hours post alcohol cessation: Tremors ('shakes'), Diaphoresis, Tachycardia, HTN, Anxiety
Secondary_Symptoms: Delirium Tremens (DTs - 48-96h): Severe confusion, vivid hallucinations, agitation, fever; Withdrawal Seizures (rum fits)
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Sharab band karne ke 1-2 din baad haath me tez kapaahat, pasiina, aur ghabraahat hui hai?; 2. Awaazein/khatmal dikhte hain (hallucinations)?; 3. Daure (seizures) pade hain?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: None - emergency hospital referral (Rx - supervised hospital detox using Benzodiazepines)
Popular_Indian_Brands: Injection Lorazepam; Tab Diazepam 10; Tab Chlordiazepoxide 25; Inj Thiamine
Dosage_Frequency: Tapering regimen over 5-7 days under hospital supervision
Supportive_Medicines: High-dose IV Thiamine (Vitamin B1 500 mg IV TDS to prevent Wernicke's Encephalopathy); IV Fluids; Magnesium Sulfate; Potassium correction
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Life-threatening emergency; TREATMENT IS UNDER MEDICAL SUPERVISION ONLY; DO NOT SUGGEST ABRUPTLY STOPPING ALCOHOL AT HOME FOR HEAVY DRINKERS WITHOUT MEDICAL COVERAGE; Do not give benzodiazepine doses for home self-use; Write 'Rx - supervised hospital detox'
Home_Care_Advice: Immediate emergency hospital admission for supervised medical detoxification; Keep patient in quiet, low-stimulation, well-lit room; Do NOT give home sedatives blindly
Lab_Investigations: CIWA-Ar Scale (Clinical Institute Withdrawal Assessment for Alcohol); Complete Blood Count; LFT; Serum Electrolytes (K+, Mg2+, Phosphate); Blood Glucose; CT Brain (if first seizure)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Medical emergency - Immediate ER referral; Delirium Tremens (DTs); Withdrawal Seizures; High fever with extreme agitation and visual hallucinations; Wernicke's Encephalopathy signs (ataxia, confusion, ophthalmoplegia)

Primary_Symptoms: Severe Polyuria (hypotonic urine >3-20 Liters/day) and Intense Polydipsia (unquenchable thirst for cold water); Nocturia
Secondary_Symptoms: Dehydration; Hypernatremia; Dry mouth; Fatigue; Constipation; Normal blood glucose levels
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Din me 5-10 Liter se zyada peshab aata hai aur thanda paani peene ki tivra pyas lagti hai?; 2. Blood Sugar report normal hai?; 3. Head injury ya pituitary surgery hui thi?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Rx - specialist supervision required (Desmopressin - DDAVP for Central DI)
Adult_Strength_Mg: 60 to 120 mcg (Desmopressin oral melt / nasal spray)
Dosage_Frequency: BD or TDS (Sublingual melt or Nasal spray under Specialist)
Duration_Days: Rx - specialist supervision required (Lifelong for Central DI)
Supportive_Medicines: Thiazide diuretics + Amiloride (for Nephrogenic DI); Unlimited access to drinking water
Precautions_Contraindications: Rx - specialist supervision required; Risk of severe Hyponatremia and Water Intoxication if Desmopressin taken without monitoring fluid intake; Differentiate Central DI from Nephrogenic DI and Primary Polydipsia
Home_Care_Advice: Unrestricted access to drinking water at all times; Take Desmopressin strictly as prescribed; Wear Medical Alert ID 'Diabetes Insipidus'; Monitor daily fluid intake and output
Lab_Investigations: Water Deprivation Test / Desmopressin Stimulation Test (Gold standard); Urine Specific Gravity (<1.005) & Urine Osmolality (<300 mOsm/kg); Serum Sodium & Serum Osmolality; Contrast MRI Pituitary/Brain
Emergency_Red_Flags: Needs in-person doctor evaluation; Severe Dehydration signs (sunken eyes, confusion, hypotension, extreme lethargy); Severe Hyponatremia (headache, seizures, confusion post desmopressin)

Primary_Symptoms: Neck stiffness and pain worsening with movement; Radiation to upper back; Suboccipital headache
Secondary_Symptoms: Mild shoulder aching; Reduced neck mobility; Muscle spasms in trapezius; Crepitus on neck rotation
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Dard gardan tak hi hai ya haath me ja raha hai?; 2. Haath me sunn-pan ya kamzori hai?; 3. Computer/Mobile par lambe samay tak kaam karte hain?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Paracetamol OR Aceclofenac
Supportive_Medicines: Thiocolchicoside 4 mg BD (if muscle spasm present); Pantoprazole 40 mg OD
Precautions_Contraindications: Oral NSAIDs: max 7 days course. Contraindicated in peptic ulcer/GI bleed, kidney disease, severe heart failure, uncontrolled HTN, asthma, and 3rd trimester pregnancy. Never combine two NSAIDs. Muscle relaxants Rx only (drowsiness caution, contraindicated in pregnancy/lactation)
Home_Care_Advice: Maintain proper ergonomic neck posture; Avoid prolonged forward head posture; Perform gentle neck isometric exercises once acute pain subsides; Use a thin firm cervical pillow; Avoid sudden neck twisting
Lab_Investigations: X-ray Cervical Spine (AP and Lateral views); MRI Cervical Spine (if neurological deficit present)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Loss of bowel/bladder control; Progressive weakness or loss of dexterity in hands; Unsteady gait/frequent falls; Sudden severe trauma

Common_Names_Hindi: Gardan se haath me dard; Cervical Radiculopathy
Primary_Symptoms: Sharp shooting electric-shock pain radiating from neck down the arm/forearm into fingers in a dermatomal pattern
Secondary_Symptoms: Numbness; Paresthesias (pins and needles); Weakness in specific arm/hand muscles; Reduced deep tendon reflexes
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Dard gardan se chal kar haath ki ungliyo tak jata hai?; 2. Haath me suiya chubhna ya sunn-pan hai?; 3. Samaan pakadne me haath se chhoot-ta hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Pregabalin OR Gabapentin + Paracetamol
Supportive_Medicines: Methylcobalamin 1500 mcg OD; Pantoprazole 40 mg OD; Cervical collar short-term
Precautions_Contraindications: Pregabalin/Gabapentin are Rx only. Drowsiness, dizziness, and dependence caution; never stop abruptly. Oral NSAIDs caution in ulcers/renal disease. Doctor-administered cervical epidural steroid injections Rx only (limit injections, caution in diabetics)
Home_Care_Advice: Avoid heavy lifting and overhead activity; Use soft cervical collar for short periods during acute pain flares; Avoid traction or forceful neck manipulation; Sleep with proper neck support
Lab_Investigations: MRI Cervical Spine (Gold standard); Electromyography (EMG) and Nerve Conduction Studies (NCS)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Progressive motor weakness in arm/hand (e.g., wrist drop, inability to grip); Sudden bowel or bladder dysfunction; Severe unremitting nocturnal pain

Common_Names_Hindi: Gardan me khichav; Postural Neck Pain
Primary_Symptoms: Aching stiffness and dull sore pain in back of neck and upper shoulders after prolonged desk/screen time
Secondary_Symptoms: Tension headaches; Upper back tightness; Muscle fatigue; Tenderness along trapezius
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Mobile/Laptop use karne ke baad gardan me dard badhta hai?; 2. Haath me koi sunn-pan ya dard to nahi jata?; 3. Aaram karne par teek hota hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Paracetamol OR Topical Diclofenac Gel
Dosage_Frequency: TDS SOS (Paracetamol) / Local application 3-4 times daily
Supportive_Medicines: Hot/Cold compress; Ergonomic adjustments
Precautions_Contraindications: Topical diclofenac gel and paracetamol are first-line OTC choices for mild pain. Stop and see a doctor if pain lasts beyond 7 days. Avoid prolonged use of systemic NSAIDs without prescription
Home_Care_Advice: Take 5-minute movement breaks every 30 minutes of screen use; Elevate phone/screen to eye level; Perform hourly neck retractions (chin tucks) and shoulder rolls; Apply warm compresses for 15 minutes twice daily
Lab_Investigations: Clinical evaluation; No routine X-rays required unless red flags present
Emergency_Red_Flags: Fever with neck stiffness; Inability to touch chin to chest; Progressive arm weakness or numbness; Pain following high-velocity trauma

Primary_Symptoms: Sudden severe painful spasm of sternocleidomastoid muscle causing head to tilt to one side and rotate to opposite side
Secondary_Symptoms: Markedly restricted and painful neck rotation; Local tenderness; Muscle tightness; Mild headache
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Subah uthte hi achanak gardan ek taraf tedhi aur locked ho gayi hai?; 2. Gardan modne par severe painful spasm hota hai?; 3. Bukhar ya chot to nahi lagi?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Paracetamol + Thiocolchicoside OR Aceclofenac + Thiocolchicoside
Supportive_Medicines: Topical Diclofenac gel; Warm compresses; Soft cervical collar
Precautions_Contraindications: Muscle relaxants (Thiocolchicoside) are Rx only, max 5-7 days duration. Drowsiness and driving caution; STRICTLY CONTRAINDICATED IN PREGNANCY AND BREASTFEEDING. Oral NSAIDs caution in peptic ulcer, renal disease, and asthma
Home_Care_Advice: Apply gentle moist heat compress to affected side for 15 minutes 3-4 times daily; Sleep on a supportive firm pillow; Avoid forced manual stretching or cracking of neck; Wear soft cervical collar temporarily for support
Lab_Investigations: Clinical evaluation; X-ray Cervical Spine (if history of trauma or persistent >1 week)
Emergency_Red_Flags: High fever with severe headache and neck stiffness (meningism); Dysphagia or difficulty breathing; History of neck trauma; Neurological deficits

Primary_Symptoms: Neck pain and stiffness developing within 24-48 hours after acceleration-deceleration injury (e.g., sudden motor vehicle impact)
Secondary_Symptoms: Headache (occipital); Decreased neck range of motion; Paresthesias in shoulders; Dizziness; Fatigue; Interscapular pain
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Gadi ke jhatke ya chot ke baad gardan me dard shuru hua hai?; 2. Haath me sunn-pan ya kamzori hai?; 3. Chakkar ya ulti aayi hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Paracetamol OR Aceclofenac
Supportive_Medicines: Pantoprazole 40 mg OD; Soft cervical collar (short-term strictly <48h); Topical Diclofenac gel
Precautions_Contraindications: Oral NSAIDs max 5-7 days, take after food. Contraindicated in peptic ulcer, renal failure, heart failure, and pregnancy. Stop and see doctor if pain lasts beyond 7 days
Home_Care_Advice: Apply ice pack wrapped in cloth for first 48 hours (15 mins 3 times daily); Maintain gentle gentle active movement as pain allows after 48h; Avoid prolonged rigid immobilization (delays recovery)
Lab_Investigations: X-ray Cervical Spine (rule out fracture/dislocation); MRI Cervical Spine (if severe pain, ligamentous injury suspected, or neurological signs)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Loss of consciousness at time of injury; Progressive arm/leg weakness; Loss of bowel/bladder control; Severe vomiting or memory loss

Primary_Symptoms: Chronic lower back aching stiffness worsening after standing or prolonged bending; Local lumbar tenderness
Secondary_Symptoms: Morning back stiffness (<30 mins); Pain radiating to buttocks; Reduced spinal flexibility; Muscle fatigue
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Kamar ka dard kitne hafte se hai?; 2. Khade rehne ya jhukne par badhta hai?; 3. Pair me sunn-pan ya peshab ka control to nahi khoya?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Paracetamol OR Aceclofenac
Supportive_Medicines: Pantoprazole 40 mg OD; Muscle relaxant (Thiocolchicoside 4 mg BD if muscle spasm present); Core strengthening exercises
Precautions_Contraindications: Oral NSAIDs short course (3-7 days), take after food. Contraindicated in peptic ulcer, CKD, heart failure, uncontrolled HTN, and pregnancy. Never combine two oral NSAIDs. Topical NSAIDs/Paracetamol first-line OTC choices
Home_Care_Advice: Red flags for back pain: loss of bladder/bowel control, saddle numbness, progressive leg weakness, fever, trauma, unexplained weight loss, history of cancer. Maintain core muscle strengthening; Use lumbar support belt short-term during flares; Avoid lifting heavy loads with bent back
Lab_Investigations: X-ray Lumbar Spine (AP and Lateral views); MRI Lumbar Spine (if nerve compression or persistent pain >6 weeks)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Bladder or bowel incontinence/retention; Saddle anesthesia (numbness in groin/buttocks); Progressive foot drop or leg weakness; Fever with back pain; History of cancer with new back pain

Common_Names_Hindi: Kamar ka achanak khichav; Lumbar Sprain
Primary_Symptoms: Sudden sharp lower back pain immediately following heavy lifting, twisting, or sudden bending; Severe local muscle spasm
Secondary_Symptoms: Markedly restricted back movements; Difficulty standing straight; Antalgic tilt; Localized paraspinal tenderness
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Wazan uthane ya achanak jhukne ke baad dard shuru hua?; 2. Kamar ki manspeshiya tight aur kadi lagti hain?; 3. Dard pair me niche to nahi ja raha?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Aceclofenac + Thiocolchicoside OR Paracetamol + Chlorzoxazone
Supportive_Medicines: Pantoprazole 40 mg OD; Topical Diclofenac gel
Precautions_Contraindications: Muscle relaxants Rx only, max 5-7 days. Drowsiness and driving caution; Thiocolchicoside contraindicated in pregnancy and lactation. Oral NSAIDs short course after food, avoid in peptic ulcer/CKD
Home_Care_Advice: First 48h: ice wrapped in cloth for 15 mins 3-4 times daily; After 48h: warm compress; Rest on firm mattress in comfortable position with knees flexed; Early gentle walking as pain permits; Avoid heavy bending/lifting
Lab_Investigations: Clinical evaluation; X-ray Lumbar Spine only if severe trauma, red flags, or non-resolving after 2 weeks
Emergency_Red_Flags: Loss of bladder/bowel control; Saddle numbness; Progressive leg weakness; High fever; Severe unremitting rest pain

Primary_Symptoms: Persistent or recurrent lower back pain lasting >12 weeks without a definitive structural/systemic cause identified
Secondary_Symptoms: General lumbar aching; Reduced functional capacity; Mild stiffness after inactivity; Associated anxiety or sleep disruption
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Kamar dard 3 mahine se zyada se hai?; 2. Koi chot, bukhar ya pair me sunn-pan to nahi hai?; 3. Daily kaam-kaaj par kitna asar pad raha hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Paracetamol OR Naproxen (Short course during flares) + Exercise Therapy
Supportive_Medicines: Duloxetine 30 mg OD (if chronic neuropathic/nociplastic pain under doctor); Core stability exercises; CBT
Precautions_Contraindications: Paracetamol and topical NSAIDs first-line OTC. Oral NSAIDs short course (3-7 days) after food; avoid continuous long-term daily NSAID use due to renal, gastric, and cardiovascular risks. PPI cover doctor-guided
Home_Care_Advice: Red flags: bladder/bowel incontinence, saddle anesthesia, leg weakness, fever, weight loss, cancer history. Stay active; avoid prolonged bed rest; Perform daily core strengthening and hamstring stretching exercises; Maintain healthy body weight
Lab_Investigations: X-ray Lumbar Spine; MRI Lumbar Spine (only to exclude specific spinal pathology if non-responsive); ESR/CRP
Emergency_Red_Flags: Bladder/bowel dysfunction; Saddle numbness; Unexplained weight loss; Progressive motor deficit in legs; Severe nocturnal pain

Primary_Symptoms: Sharp shooting back pain with nerve radiation into buttock, thigh, calf, or foot (Sciatica); Increased by coughing/sneezing
Secondary_Symptoms: Positive Straight Leg Raise (SLR) test; Dermatomal paresthesias; Focal muscle weakness (e.g., extensor hallucis longus); Absent ankle jerk
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Kamar ka dard khansne ya chinkne par pair me niche jhatke se jata hai?; 2. Pair ya ungliyo me sunn-pan hai?; 3. Peshab karne me koi takleef hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Pregabalin OR Gabapentin + Aceclofenac
Supportive_Medicines: Methylcobalamin 1500 mcg OD; Pantoprazole 40 mg OD; Lumbo-sacral belt short-term
Precautions_Contraindications: Pregabalin/Gabapentin are Rx only, drowsiness/dependence caution; do not stop abruptly. Oral NSAIDs short course after food; contraindicated in peptic ulcer, CKD, heart failure. Doctor-administered epidural steroid injection Rx only
Home_Care_Advice: Avoid forward bending, twisting, and lifting heavy weights; Maintain short periods of walking; Use firm mattress; Apply heat packs; Wear LS belt while walking short distances
Lab_Investigations: MRI Lumbar Spine (Gold standard for disc herniation and nerve root compression); X-ray Lumbar Spine
Emergency_Red_Flags: Cauda Equina Syndrome: sudden loss of bowel/bladder control, saddle numbness, bilateral severe leg weakness/foot drop (EMERGENCY SURGERY NEEDED)

Common_Names_Hindi: Sciatica; Pair me nass ka dard
Primary_Symptoms: Burning, shooting, or electric-shock pain originating in lower back/buttock and traveling down back/side of leg to foot
Secondary_Symptoms: Leg numbness; Tingling sensation; Muscle weakness in foot/ankle; Pain exacerbated by sitting or coughing
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Dard kulhe (buttock) se hokar pair ke piche se aedi/ungliyo tak jata hai?; 2. Pair me sunn-pan ya chiintiya kat ti hain?; 3. Chhalne me pair kamzor lagta hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Pregabalin OR Gabapentin + Paracetamol
Supportive_Medicines: Methylcobalamin 1500 mcg OD; Pantoprazole 40 mg OD; Physiotherapy (nerve glides)
Precautions_Contraindications: Pregabalin and Gabapentin are Rx only; cause drowsiness, dizziness, and risk of dependence; never stop abruptly. NSAIDs short course after food. Oral steroids/epidural injections Rx only under specialist supervision
Home_Care_Advice: Red flags: bladder/bowel issues, saddle numbness, progressive leg weakness, fever, trauma, weight loss, cancer history. Avoid prolonged sitting (>30 mins); Perform gentle neural mobilization/stretching exercises under guidance; Sleep with pillow between knees
Lab_Investigations: MRI Lumbosacral Spine; Electromyography (EMG) and Nerve Conduction Studies (NCS)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Sudden bowel or bladder incontinence/retention; Saddle area numbness; Rapidly progressive leg weakness (e.g., foot drop); Severe unremitting rest pain

Primary_Symptoms: Lower back pain worsened by spinal extension (standing tall/bending backward) and relieved by sitting or forward flexion
Secondary_Symptoms: Hamstring tightness; Step-off palpation on lumbar spinous processes; Buttock aching; Neurogenic claudication if canal narrowed
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Kamar piche jhukane ya lambe samay tak khade rehne par dard badhta hai?; 2. Baithne par aaram milta hai?; 3. X-ray me haddi khisaki hui batayi hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Aceclofenac OR Paracetamol + Core Rehabilitation
Supportive_Medicines: Pantoprazole 40 mg OD; Rigid Lumbo-sacral corset belt for activity; Physiotherapy
Precautions_Contraindications: Oral NSAIDs short course (3-7 days) after food. Contraindicated in peptic ulcer, CKD, heart failure, pregnancy. Paracetamol and topical NSAIDs first-line OTC choices. Avoid hyperextension exercises
Home_Care_Advice: Perform flexion-based core strengthening exercises (Williams flexion exercises); Avoid heavy weightlifting, backward bending, and high-impact jumping; Wear supportive LS belt during physical tasks
Lab_Investigations: X-ray Lumbar Spine (Flexion and Extension dynamic lateral views); MRI Lumbar Spine (assess spinal canal and neural foramina)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Loss of bowel/bladder control; Saddle numbness; Progressive neurological deficits in legs; Grade progression with severe unstable pain

Common_Names_Hindi: Kamar ki nali sikudna; Canal Stenosis
Primary_Symptoms: Neurogenic Claudication: bilateral leg pain, heaviness, numbness, or cramping appearing after walking a specific distance and RELIEVED BY SITTING/FORWARD BENDING
Secondary_Symptoms: Back pain; Relieved by leaning forward ('shopping cart sign'); Normal peripheral arterial pulses; Bilateral leg weakness on walking
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Kuch door chalne par dono pairo me dard, sunn-pan, aur bhari-pan aata hai?; 2. Aage jhuk kar chalne ya baithne par 2 min me aaram milta hai?; 3. Pairo ki nasein (pulses) normal hain?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Rx - specialist supervision required (Pregabalin / Gabapentin + Physiotherapy / Epidural Steroid Injections / Surgical Decompression)
Supportive_Medicines: Methylcobalamin 1500 mcg OD; Lumbar flexion physical therapy; Lumbar epidural steroid injection (specialist-administered)
Precautions_Contraindications: Rx - specialist supervision required. Pregabalin/Gabapentin Rx only; cause sedating effects. Differentiate neurogenic claudication (relieved by bending forward) from vascular claudication (relieved by standing still). Avoid spinal hyperextension
Home_Care_Advice: Walk with slight forward tilt or use a walking frame; Stationary cycling is well-tolerated; Avoid prolonged standing or walking upright; Maintain healthy weight
Lab_Investigations: MRI Lumbar Spine (Gold standard - cross-sectional canal area measurement); Plain Dynamic X-rays; Vascular Doppler (rule out PAD)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Cauda Equina Syndrome (bowel/bladder incontinence, saddle anesthesia); Progressive foot drop or leg weakness causing frequent falls

Primary_Symptoms: Inflammatory back pain in young adults (<45y): insidious onset, duration >3 months, MORNING STIFFNESS >30 MINS, IMPROVES WITH EXERCISE, WORSSENS WITH REST
Secondary_Symptoms: Alternating buttock pain; Enthesitis (Achilles tendon/plantar fascia pain); Uveitis (red painful eye); Reduced chest expansion; Bamboo spine
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Umar 45 se kam hai aur kamar me subah uthte hi 30 min se zyada aedan rehti hai?; 2. Kasrat karne par dard kam aur aaram karne par badhta hai?; 3. HLA-B27 test hua hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Rx - specialist supervision required (First-line NSAIDs - Indomethacin / Etoricoxib; Biologics - TNF/IL-17 Inhibitors under Rheumatologist)
Supportive_Medicines: Sulfasalazine 500 mg BD (for peripheral joint involvement under rheumatologist); Pantoprazole 40 mg OD; Daily posture exercises
Precautions_Contraindications: Rx - specialist supervision required. Long-term NSAIDs require strict monitoring for peptic ulcer, CKD, HTN, and cardiovascular events. Avoid prolonged spinal immobilization. Biologics require screening for latent TB and hepatitis B
Home_Care_Advice: Perform daily lifelong posture, spinal extension, and deep breathing exercises; Sleep flat on a firm mattress with a thin pillow; Complete smoking cessation (smoking accelerates spinal fusion)
Lab_Investigations: HLA-B27 gene test; MRI Sacroiliac Joints (detects early bone marrow edema/sacroiliitis); ESR and CRP (elevated); X-ray Pelvis with SI Joints
Emergency_Red_Flags: Sudden severe red painful eye with photophobia (Acute Anterior Uveitis - urgent eye referral); Spinal trauma with severe new neurological deficits (fracture of fused spine risk)

Primary_Symptoms: Unilateral or bilateral deep buttock pain originating from sacroiliac joint; Exacerbated by sitting, climbing stairs, or weight-bearing
Secondary_Symptoms: Pain radiating down posterior thigh (above knee); Local tenderness over SI joint sulcus; Positive Patrick/FABER test; Stiffness
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Kulhe (buttock) me andar tak tez dard hai?; 2. Ek pair par wazan daalne ya siidhiya chadne par badhta hai?; 3. Baithne par dard hota hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Aceclofenac OR Naproxen
Supportive_Medicines: Pantoprazole 40 mg OD; Sacroiliac joint belt; Targeted SI joint steroid/local anesthetic injection (specialist-administered)
Precautions_Contraindications: Oral NSAIDs short course (3-7 days) after food. Contraindicated in peptic ulcer, CKD, heart failure, HTN, pregnancy. PPI cover doctor-guided. Steroid injections Rx and doctor-administered only
Home_Care_Advice: Avoid uneven weight-bearing, single-leg standing, and wide-stride lunges; Apply ice pack for 15 mins during acute pain; Wear SI supportive belt during standing/walking
Lab_Investigations: MRI Sacroiliac Joints (Gold standard); X-ray Pelvis with SI Joints; ESR/CRP; HLA-B27 testing
Emergency_Red_Flags: High fever with severe unilateral buttock pain (Septic Sacroiliitis suspicion); Neurological deficits in leg; Bowel/bladder dysfunction

Primary_Symptoms: Localized severe pain and tenderness at coccyx (tailbone); Exacerbated by prolonged sitting, sitting leaning back, or rising from a chair
Secondary_Symptoms: Pain on defecation or sexual intercourse; Local palpation tenderness over coccyx; Relieved by leaning forward while sitting
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Kamar ke sabse piche niche (tailbone) par baithne par tez dard hota hai?; 2. Kurse se uthte waqt ya piche tek lagane par badhta hai?; 3. Girne ya chot ki history hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Paracetamol OR Etodolac / Aceclofenac
Supportive_Medicines: Cushion support (Coccyx wedge / Donut cushion); Pantoprazole 40 mg OD; Stool softeners (Syp Lactulose)
Precautions_Contraindications: Oral NSAIDs short course after food. Contraindicated in peptic ulcer, renal disease, heart failure. Topical NSAIDs/Paracetamol first-line OTC choices. Local corticosteroid/anesthetic injection Rx and doctor-administered only
Home_Care_Advice: Use a specialized donut-shaped or wedge-shaped coccyx cushion while sitting; Lean slightly forward while sitting to remove weight from tailbone; Apply ice packs for 15 mins 3 times daily; Use stool softeners to prevent straining during defecation
Lab_Investigations: X-ray Coccyx (Sitting and Standing dynamic views to check hypermobility/subluxation); MRI Coccyx (if persistent non-responsive pain)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Fever with local redness/swelling/pus discharge (Pilonidal abscess or bone infection); Rectal bleeding; Unexplained weight loss

Primary_Symptoms: Sudden involuntary, painful contraction and tightness of lumbar paraspinal muscles; Locked or rigid low back posture
Secondary_Symptoms: Severe local tenderness; Inability to bend or straighten back comfortably; Dull aching residual pain after acute spasm subsides
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Kamar ki manspeshi achanak kadi aur tez dard waali ho gayi hai?; 2. Jhukne ya hilne me takleef hai?; 3. Pain pair me to nahi ja raha?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Paracetamol + Thiocolchicoside OR Aceclofenac + Thiocolchicoside
Supportive_Medicines: Topical Diclofenac gel; Warm compresses; Pantoprazole 40 mg OD
Precautions_Contraindications: Muscle relaxants (Thiocolchicoside) Rx only, max 5-7 days. Drowsiness and driving caution; STRICTLY CONTRAINDICATED IN PREGNANCY AND BREASTFEEDING. NSAIDs short course after food
Home_Care_Advice: Apply cold pack for first 24 hours, followed by warm compresses for 15 minutes 3-4 times daily; Gentle active walking as tolerated; Avoid absolute bed rest beyond 1 day; Avoid heavy lifting
Lab_Investigations: Red flags for back pain: loss of bladder/bowel control, saddle numbness, progressive leg weakness, fever, trauma, weight loss, cancer history. Clinical evaluation; Imaging usually not required for simple uncomplicated spasm
Emergency_Red_Flags: Loss of bowel or bladder control; Saddle numbness; Severe shooting leg pain with numbness; High fever

Primary_Symptoms: Mid-back aching pain and muscle tightness between shoulder blades; Worsened by prolonged slouched sitting or desk work
