Common_Names_Hindi: Groin Strain; Jangh ke andar ka khichav
Primary_Symptoms: Sharp pain in inner thigh/groin region (adductor longus) during side-to-side movements, kicking, or sprinting; Local adductor tenderness
Secondary_Symptoms: Pain worsened by resisted hip adduction (squeezing knees together) or passive hip abduction; Localized swelling; Limping
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Jangh ke andar ki taraf (groin) me jhatka/khujli jaisa dard hua hai?; 2. Dono ghutno ke beech ball dabane ya side me le jane par dard badhta hai?; 3. Kicking karte hain?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Paracetamol OR Aceclofenac + RICE Protocol
Supportive_Medicines: Topical Diclofenac gel; Groin spica wrap; Adductor strengthening exercises
Precautions_Contraindications: First-line: RICE protocol and early gentle movement as pain allows; avoid heat and massage in first 48 hours. Oral NSAIDs short course after food. Differentiate from Inguinal Hernia, Sports Hernia (Athletic Pubalgia), and Hip joint pathology
Home_Care_Advice: Follow RICE protocol: Rest from sports, Ice pack wrapped in towel for 15 mins 3 times daily for 48h, Compression groin wrap; Perform gentle adductor squeezes once acute pain subsides; Avoid wide straddle stretches initially
Lab_Investigations: Ultrasound Groin (evaluates adductor longus origin tear); MRI Pelvis/Groin (rules out athletic pubalgia / osteitis pubis); X-ray Pelvis
Emergency_Red_Flags: Palpable bulge in groin worsening with coughing (Inguinal Hernia); Inability to bear weight; High fever with testicular pain

Common_Names_Hindi: Shin Splints; Pindali ke aage ka dard
Primary_Symptoms: Dull aching pain localized along posteromedial border of middle-to-distal tibia (shin bone) appearing during/after running or jumping
Secondary_Symptoms: Diffuse tenderness over lower 1/3 of posteromedial tibia (spanning >5 cm); Mild localized edema; Pain worsened by ankle plantarflexion
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Pair ki aage ki haddi (shin bone) ke andar ki patti par running ke baad dard hota hai?; 2. Choone par 4-5 cm lamba dard ka hissa hai?; 3. Naye joote ya hard surface par running shuru ki?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Paracetamol OR Aceclofenac + Rest Protocol
Supportive_Medicines: Topical Diclofenac gel; Shock-absorbing shoe insoles; Shin stretching and calf strengthening exercises
Precautions_Contraindications: Oral NSAIDs short course after food. Contraindicated in peptic ulcer, CKD, heart failure, HTN, pregnancy. Topical NSAIDs/Paracetamol first-line OTC choices. MUST DIFFERENTIATE SHIN SPLINTS FROM TIBIAL STRESS FRACTURE (stress fracture has focal point tenderness <2 cm)
Home_Care_Advice: Rest from running and high-impact activities; Switch to cross-training (swimming/cycling); Apply ice pack for 15 mins 3 times daily; Use proper shock-absorbing running shoes with arch support; Replace worn running shoes
Lab_Investigations: X-ray Shin/Tibia (AP and Lateral views - usually normal in early shin splints, excludes fracture); MRI Tibia / Bone Scan (differentiates severe MTSS from stress fracture)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Focal pinpoint severe bone tenderness <2 cm on tibia (Tibial Stress Fracture risk); Tense swollen shin with severe numbness or weakness (Exertional Compartment Syndrome)

Common_Names_Hindi: Stress Fracture; Haddi me hairline crack
Primary_Symptoms: Severe localized PINPOINT bone pain (tibia, metatarsals, navicular) worsened by weight-bearing/running and relieved ONLY by complete rest
Secondary_Symptoms: Focal point tenderness <2 cm directly over bone; Localized bony edema; Pain progressing from post-activity to pain during walking
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Running/activity ke baad haddi par EK HI CHHOTE POINT par severe dard hai?; 2. Wazan daalne par tez dard hota hai?; 3. Training intensity achanak badhayi thi?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Paracetamol OR Acetaminophen + Strict Bone Offloading
Supportive_Medicines: Calcium Carbonate 500 mg + Vitamin D3 600 IU daily; Rigid walking boot / cast immobilizer; Crutches for non-weight bearing
Precautions_Contraindications: STRICT OFF-LOADING / IMMOBILIZATION IS MANDATORY. Avoid oral NSAIDs (Ibuprofen/Aceclofenac) if possible, as NSAIDs inhibit prostaglandin-mediated osteoblast bone healing. Paracetamol is preferred analgesic
Home_Care_Advice: Strictly avoid running, jumping, and weight-bearing on affected bone; Use a rigid pneumatic walking boot or crutches as advised; Apply ice packs for 15 mins twice daily; Ensure adequate Calcium and Vitamin D intake
Lab_Investigations: Plain X-rays (may be negative for first 2-3 weeks until periosteal reaction appears); MRI Bone (Gold standard - detects early bone marrow edema); Bone Scan
Emergency_Red_Flags: Severe unremitting pain at rest; Complete fracture displacement with visible deformity; Loss of sensation in foot

Common_Names_Hindi: Raat ko pairo me aedan; Leg Cramps
Primary_Symptoms: Sudden, involuntary, painful contraction of calf, foot, or hamstring muscles occurring at night during sleep or rest, lasting seconds to minutes
Secondary_Symptoms: Visible muscle knotting/hardness; Persistent residual muscle soreness next day; Sleep disruption; Normal neurological exam
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Raat ko sote me achanak pindali (calf) ya panje me tez dard-bhari aedan aati hai?; 2. Aedan ke waqt manspeshi kadi ho jati hai?; 3. Paani kam peete hain ya BP ki paani wali dawai chal rahi hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Stretching First-Line + Hydration & Electrolytes (QUININE IS NOT RECOMMENDED FOR ROUTINE USE)
Supportive_Medicines: Magnesium Glycinate 250 mg at bedtime; Vitamin E 400 IU; Calcium + Vitamin D3 supplementation
Precautions_Contraindications: QUININE IS STRICTLY NOT RECOMMENDED FOR ROUTINE LEG CRAMPS DUE TO FATAL HEMATOLOGIC TOXICITY AND ARRHYTHMIAS. Check serum electrolytes, renal function, and medications (diuretics cause cramps). Stretching and hydration are primary first-line
Home_Care_Advice: When cramp occurs, immediately perform passive stretch of calf (pull toes upward toward shin) and walk on heels; Perform calf stretching exercises for 5 mins before bedtime; Maintain high fluid intake during day; Take warm foot bath before sleep
Lab_Investigations: Serum Electrolytes (Sodium, Potassium, Calcium, Magnesium); Serum Creatinine; Fasting Blood Glucose; Thyroid Profile (TSH)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Rapidly progressive muscle weakness; Dark tea-colored urine (Rhabdomyolysis suspicion); Asymmetric persistent leg swelling (DVT rule out)

Primary_Symptoms: Acute lateral ankle pain, rapid swelling, bruising, and tenderness following an inversion injury (twisting foot inward)
Secondary_Symptoms: Tenderness over anterior talofibular (ATFL) and calcaneofibular (CFL) ligaments; Mild-to-moderate ecchymosis; Antalgic gait
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Pair ka takhna (ankle) andar ki taraf muda tha?; 2. Ankle ke bahar ki taraf soojan aur neela-pan aaya hai?; 3. Kya aap 4 kadam chal pa rahe hain?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Paracetamol OR Aceclofenac / Ibuprofen + RICE Protocol
Supportive_Medicines: Topical Diclofenac gel; Semi-rigid ankle brace / Aircast; Crepe bandage wrap
Precautions_Contraindications: First-line for sprain: RICE protocol (Rest, Ice, Compression, Elevation) and early protected movement as pain permits; avoid heat and massage in first 48 hours. Apply Ottawa Ankle Rules: X-ray mandatory if unable to bear weight immediately and in ER for 4 steps, or bone tenderness over malleoli
Home_Care_Advice: Follow RICE protocol: Rest with brace, Ice pack wrapped in cloth for 15 mins 3-4 times daily for 48h, Compression elastic wrap, Elevate ankle above heart level; Avoid heat/massage for 48h; Gentle active ankle range of motion as pain permits
Lab_Investigations: X-ray Ankle AP, Lateral, and Mortise views (Mandatory if Ottawa Ankle Rules positive - rules out malleolar fracture); Ultrasound Ankle / MRI (if persistent instability)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Ottawa Ankle Rules positive: Inability to bear weight for 4 steps, or severe bone tenderness at posterior tip of malleoli / 5th metatarsal base (Fracture risk); Cold pale foot

Primary_Symptoms: Recurrent feeling of ankle 'giving way' or collapsing during walking/sports on uneven surfaces, secondary to prior unhealed sprains
Secondary_Symptoms: Recurrent minor ankle sprains; Chronic lateral ankle aching; Feeling of apprehension on uneven ground; Positive anterior drawer test of ankle
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Takhna baar-baar mudta (give way karta) hai?; 2. Purani ankle sprain chot ki history hai?; 3. Uneven road par chalne me darr lagta hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Paracetamol OR Aceclofenac (Short course during acute tweaks) + Proprioceptive Rehab
Supportive_Medicines: Semi-rigid functional ankle brace; Peroneal muscle strengthening & wobble board proprioceptive rehab; Anatomical ligament reconstruction (under specialist)
Precautions_Contraindications: Oral NSAIDs short course after food for acute tweaks. Primary cure is proprioceptive rehab and peroneal muscle strengthening. Reconstructive surgery (Broström procedure) Rx under orthopedic specialist for failed rehab
Home_Care_Advice: Perform single-leg balance exercises and wobble board training daily to rebuild proprioception; Wear a supportive semi-rigid ankle brace during sports or walking on rough terrain; Strengthen peroneal muscles
Lab_Investigations: Stress X-rays Ankle (Anterior drawer and Talar tilt stress views); MRI Ankle (evaluates ATFL/CFL chronic tear and osteochondral lesions of talus)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Inability to bear weight; Gross ankle joint deformity; Persistent mechanical locking of ankle joint

Common_Names_Hindi: Achilles Tendon ka dard; Heel Cord Pain
Primary_Symptoms: Pain and stiffness along Achilles tendon (back of heel/lower calf), worst in morning or with first steps after rest
Secondary_Symptoms: Tendon thickening or localized nodule 2-6 cm proximal to insertion (Midportion) or at calcaneal insertion (Insertional); Morning stiffness; Crepitus
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Pair ke piche aedi ke upar ki nass (Achilles tendon) me dard hai?; 2. Subah pehle kadam rakhne par ya running ke baad badhta hai?; 3. Nass moti lagti hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Paracetamol OR Aceclofenac / Naproxen + Eccentric Rehab
Supportive_Medicines: Topical Diclofenac gel; Silicone heel cups/lifts (0.5-1 cm); Eccentric calf loading exercises (Alfredson protocol)
Precautions_Contraindications: Oral NSAIDs short course after food. Contraindicated in peptic ulcer, CKD, heart failure, HTN, 3rd trimester pregnancy. STEROID INJECTIONS INTO OR AROUND ACHILLES TENDON ARE STRICTLY CONTRAINDICATED DUE TO HIGH RISK OF TENDON RUPTURE
Home_Care_Advice: Perform eccentric calf drop exercises (Alfredson protocol) twice daily; Use silicone heel cups in shoes to reduce tendon strain; Apply ice packs for 15 mins post activity; Avoid flat barefoot walking
Lab_Investigations: Ultrasound Achilles Tendon (evaluates tendon thickness, neovascularization, and intratendinous tears); MRI Ankle; X-ray Calcaneus (for insertional spurs)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Sudden loud 'pop' or 'snap' at back of ankle followed by immediate inability to push off foot (Achilles Tendon Rupture emergency); Severe warmth and redness

Primary_Symptoms: Sudden catastrophic 'pop' or feeling of being kicked in back of ankle during pushing-off, followed by immediate inability to plantarflex foot or walk
Secondary_Symptoms: Positive Thompson Squeeze Test (absence of foot plantarflexion when squeezing calf muscle); Palpable gap in tendon 2-6 cm above calcaneus; Marked limping
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Pair ke piche aedi ke upar jhatke ke sath 'pop' ki awaaz aayi thi?; 2. Panje par khade hone me bilkul kamzori hai?; 3. Calf squeeze karne par panja hilti nahi hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: None - emergency hospital referral
Popular_Indian_Brands: Injection Tramadol / Oral Analgesics for transport pain
Dosage_Frequency: Immediate Equinus rigid splinting + Orthopedic Surgery / Functional Rehabilitation evaluation
Supportive_Medicines: Immediate ER / Orthopedic Referral; Rigid Equinus Splint (foot in full plantarflexion); Surgical Tendon Repair or Functional Equinus Cast Protocol
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Life-threatening orthopedic emergency. DO NOT ALLOW PATIENT TO BEAR WEIGHT ON AFFECTED FOOT. DO NOT MASSAGE OR FORCE FOOT UPWARD. Immediate orthopedic evaluation required
Home_Care_Advice: Immobilize ankle immediately in a plantarflexed (pointed toes downward) position using a splint or rigid support; Avoid all weight-bearing; Transfer patient to emergency room
Lab_Investigations: Emergency Ultrasound Achilles Tendon; MRI Ankle/Achilles (confirms full-thickness tear gap size); Clinical Thompson Test
Emergency_Red_Flags: Emergency Red Flags: Complete loss of plantarflexion power; Visible gap in tendon; Cold pale foot; Inability to bear any weight

Primary_Symptoms: STABBING PAIN AT BOTTOM OF HEEL WITH FIRST STEPS IN THE MORNING or after prolonged sitting; Pain eases with initial walking then worsens late in day
Secondary_Symptoms: Point tenderness localized strictly over medial calcaneal tuberosity; Pain worsened by passive dorsiflexion of toes (Windlass mechanism); Tight calf muscles
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Subah zameen par pehla kadam rakhne par aedi me tez sui-jaisa dard hota hai?; 2. Kuch kadam chalne ke baad dard thoda kam hota hai?; 3. Barefoot chalne par badhta hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Paracetamol OR Aceclofenac / Naproxen + Plantar Stretching
Supportive_Medicines: Topical Diclofenac gel; Silicone heel cushions / Orthotic arch supports; Night splint; Plantar fascia local steroid / PRP injection (specialist-administered)
Precautions_Contraindications: Oral NSAIDs short course (3-5 days) after food. Contraindicated in peptic ulcer, CKD, heart failure, HTN, 3rd trimester pregnancy. Local steroid injections Rx and doctor-administered (use sparingly as repeated injections cause plantar fat pad atrophy / fascia rupture)
Home_Care_Advice: Roll arch of foot over a frozen water bottle for 10 mins twice daily; Perform plantar fascia and calf stretches before getting out of bed; Wear cushioned footwear with good arch support indoors; Never walk barefoot on hard floors
Lab_Investigations: X-ray Calcaneus Lateral view (may show calcaneal spur, but spur is not primary cause); Ultrasound Plantar Fascia (shows fascia thickening >4 mm)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Sudden severe tearing sensation in arch of foot with ecchymosis (Plantar Fascia Rupture); High fever with heel redness and warmth (Calcaneal Osteomyelitis)

Common_Names_Hindi: Aedi ki haddi badhna; Calcaneal Spur
Primary_Symptoms: Exostosis (bony growth) on underside of calcaneus; Symptoms closely overlap with Plantar Fasciitis: heel pain on weight-bearing
Secondary_Symptoms: Localized tenderness on deep palpation of inferior calcaneus; Pain on standing after rest; Associated with chronic plantar fascia traction
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Aedi ke niche haddi badhne (calcaneal spur) X-ray me aayi hai?; 2. Khade hone ya chalne par aedi me dard hota hai?; 3. Plantar fasciitis ke lakshan hain?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Paracetamol OR Aceclofenac + Soft Heel Footwear
Supportive_Medicines: Topical Diclofenac gel; Silicone heel pad / MCR (Microcellular Rubber) footwear; Plantar stretching exercises
Precautions_Contraindications: Bony spur itself is usually asymptomatic; pain is due to associated plantar fasciitis inflammatory traction. Oral NSAIDs short course after food. Surgery for spur removal is extremely rare and handled by orthopedic specialists
Home_Care_Advice: Use MCR (Microcellular Rubber) soft-soled slippers indoors; Use silicone heel cups in shoes; Avoid hard-soled footwear and barefoot walking; Perform daily calf and plantar stretches
Lab_Investigations: X-ray Calcaneus Lateral view (confirms inferior calcaneal spur exostosis); Ultrasound Foot
Emergency_Red_Flags: Severe resting pain; Localized swelling, warmth, and redness over calcaneus; Numbness in heel/sole

Common_Names_Hindi: Chapta pair ka dard; Pes Planus
Primary_Symptoms: Aching foot and ankle pain, postural fatigue, and arch strain due to collapse of medial longitudinal arch of foot
Secondary_Symptoms: Valgus heel alignment; Eversion of foot; Wear on medial side of shoe soles; Pain along posterior tibial tendon; Calf fatigue
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Pair ka arch (gaddha) bilkul flat hai?; 2. Lambe samay tak khade rehne ya chalne par pair aur aedi me thakan/dard hota hai?; 3. Joote andar ki taraf se ghisate hain?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Paracetamol OR Aceclofenac (Short course for flares) + Medial Arch Support
Supportive_Medicines: Custom medial arch support orthotics; Motion-control supportive shoes; Posterior tibial muscle strengthening exercises
Precautions_Contraindications: Oral NSAIDs short course after food for acute overuse pain. Primary long-term management is conservative with custom arch support orthotics and calf/foot intrinsic muscle strengthening. Reconstructive surgery Rx under orthopedic specialist
Home_Care_Advice: Use custom-molded medial arch support insoles in all footwear; Wear supportive athletic shoes with firm heel counters; Perform intrinsic foot muscle exercises (towel scrunches, marble picking with toes) and calf stretches
Lab_Investigations: X-ray Both Feet Weight-bearing (AP and Lateral views - measures calcaneal pitch and talonavicular angles); Clinical Wet Footprint Test
Emergency_Red_Flags: Sudden rigid painful flatfoot deformity (Tarsal Coalition risk); Inability to perform single-leg heel raise (Posterior Tibial Tendon Dysfunction Stage 2)

Common_Names_Hindi: Aangoothe ki hadi phoolna; Bunion Pain
Primary_Symptoms: Painful bony prominence (bunion) at 1st metatarsophalangeal (MTP) joint with lateral deviation of big toe toward second toe
Secondary_Symptoms: Erythema, swelling, and tenderness over 1st MTP prominence; Overlapping 2nd toe; Callus formation under 2nd metatarsal head; Difficulty fitting narrow shoes
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Pair ke bade angoothe ke jod par bahar ki taraf painful bony gummda (bunion) bana hai?; 2. Angootha doosri ungli ki taraf tedha ho raha hai?; 3. Narrow joote pehenne par badhta hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Paracetamol OR Aceclofenac (Short course) + Bunion Pad/Splint
Supportive_Medicines: Topical Diclofenac gel; Silicone bunion shield / Toe separator; Wide toe-box footwear; Bunionectomy surgery (specialist evaluation)
Precautions_Contraindications: Oral NSAIDs short course after food for bursal inflammation. Primary management is conservative with wide toe-box shoes and bunion pads. Surgical correction (bunionectomy) Rx under orthopedic specialist for severe painful deformities
Home_Care_Advice: Switch strictly to wide toe-box shoes with soft uppers; Avoid high heels and narrow pointed shoes; Use silicone toe separators and gel bunion protector pads; Apply ice pack for 15 mins post activity
Lab_Investigations: Weight-bearing X-ray Foot (AP and Lateral views - measures Hallux Valgus Angle and Intermetatarsal Angle)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Severe local skin breakdown, ulceration, or purulent infection over bunion prominence (especially in diabetic patients); Severe unremitting pain

Primary_Symptoms: Burning pain, numbness, and paresthesias in 3rd intermetatarsal space (between 3rd and 4th toes); 'Feels like standing on a folded sock or pebble'
Secondary_Symptoms: Positive Mulder's sign (painful click produced by squeezing metatarsal heads together); Symptoms exacerbated by narrow tight shoes and high heels
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Pair ke tale me 3rd aur 4th ungliyo ke beech meetha burning dard aur sunn-pan hai?; 2. Lagta hai jaise joote me kankar (pebble) ya jurab mudi hui hai?; 3. Narrow joote nikalne par aaram milta hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Pregabalin OR Aceclofenac / Paracetamol + Metatarsal Pad
Supportive_Medicines: Metatarsal orthotic pad (placed proximal to metatarsal heads); Wide toe-box shoes; Intermetatarsal local corticosteroid / anesthetic injection (specialist-administered)
Precautions_Contraindications: Pregabalin is Rx only; drowsiness caution. Oral NSAIDs short course after food. Local corticosteroid injection Rx and doctor-administered only. Surgical neurectomy Rx under orthopedic specialist for refractory cases
Home_Care_Advice: Wear wide toe-box shoes with soft cushioned soles; Avoid high heels and narrow tight footwear; Place a teardrop-shaped metatarsal pad just behind painful intermetatarsal space; Apply ice pack for 15 mins twice daily
Lab_Investigations: Ultrasound Foot (visualizes intermetatarsal neuroma hypoechoic mass >5 mm); MRI Foot (Gold standard); Clinical Mulder's click test
Emergency_Red_Flags: Progressive spreading numbness across sole; Severe resting pain preventing sleep; Local skin ulceration

Common_Names_Hindi: Panje ke niche ka dard; Metatarsalgia
Primary_Symptoms: Aching pain and tenderness localized under metatarsal heads ('ball of foot'); Worsened by standing, walking barefoot, or high-impact jumping
Secondary_Symptoms: Callus formation under 2nd or 3rd metatarsal head; Pain worsened by passive toe dorsiflexion; Feeling of walking on stones
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Pair ke tale me samne ki taraf (ball of foot/ungliyo ke niche) dard hota hai?; 2. Nange pair chalne ya khade hone par badhta hai?; 3. Tale par kadi chamdi (callus) bani hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Paracetamol OR Aceclofenac + Metatarsal Bar/Pad
Supportive_Medicines: Topical Diclofenac gel; Metatarsal orthotic bar/pad insoles; Soft cushioned footwear; Callus shaving (podiatrist-administered)
Precautions_Contraindications: Oral NSAIDs short course after food. Contraindicated in peptic ulcer, CKD, heart failure, HTN, 3rd trimester pregnancy. Primary management is conservative biomechanical offloading using metatarsal pads/bars
Home_Care_Advice: Wear well-cushioned shoes with thick soft soles; Place metatarsal insoles/pads in shoes to offload metatarsal heads; Avoid barefoot walking on hard tiles; Apply ice pack wrapped in cloth for 15 mins post activity
Lab_Investigations: X-ray Foot (AP, Lateral, and Sesamoid views - rules out stress fracture or Freiberg's infraction); Plantar pressure pedobarography
Emergency_Red_Flags: Severe focal bone tenderness over metatarsal neck (Metatarsal Stress Fracture risk); Deep bleeding callus ulcer (especially in diabetics); High fever

Primary_Symptoms: Burning pain, numbness, and paresthesias in sole of foot and toes due to posterior tibial nerve compression under flexor retinaculum at medial malleolus
Secondary_Symptoms: Positive Tinel's sign posterior to medial malleolus; Pain worsened by prolonged standing or walking; Night pain in sole; Preserved dorsal sensation
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Pair ke tale (sole) aur ungliyo me burning dard, sunn-pan aur chiintiya kat ti hain?; 2. Takhne ke andar ki haddi ke piche choone par electric jhatka lagta hai?; 3. Baithne par aaram milta hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Pregabalin OR Gabapentin + Orthotic Arch Support
Supportive_Medicines: Methylcobalamin 1500 mcg OD; Medial arch orthotic insole (corrects pronation); Tarsal tunnel steroid injection / Surgical decompression (specialist-administered)
Precautions_Contraindications: Pregabalin and Gabapentin are Rx only; cause drowsiness, dizziness, and dependence caution; never stop abruptly. Avoid forced foot eversion. Local steroid injection or surgical release Rx under specialist guidance
Home_Care_Advice: Wear custom orthotic arch supports to correct foot pronation; Avoid prolonged standing or walking on hard surfaces; Wear supportive well-fitted shoes; Apply ice packs for 15 mins to medial ankle
Lab_Investigations: Nerve Conduction Studies (NCS) and Electromyography (EMG - confirms posterior tibial neuropathy); Ultrasound Tarsal Tunnel (rules out ganglion or varicose vein compression); MRI Ankle
Emergency_Red_Flags: Progressive wasting (atrophy) of intrinsic plantar foot muscles; Complete loss of sensation on sole leading to neuropathic ulceration; Severe motor weakness

Primary_Symptoms: Irresistible urge to move legs, usually accompanied by uncomfortable paresthesias/sensations deep within legs; WORST AT REST/EVENING, RELIEVED BY MOVEMENT
Secondary_Symptoms: Urge triggered by inactivity/lying down; Periodic Limb Movements of Sleep (PLMS) association; Sleep-onset insomnia; Fatigue
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Shaam ko ya sote me pairo me aisi bechaini hoti hai ki pairo ko hilana hi padta hai?; 2. Pairo ko ghumane ya chalne par aaram milta hai?; 3. Serum Ferritin / Iron test hua hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: CHECK IRON/FERRITIN FIRST + Pramipexole OR Ropinirole / Pregabalin
Supportive_Medicines: Ferrous Ascorbate 100 mg elemental iron OD (MANDATORY IF SERUM FERRITIN <50 mcg/L); Magnesium supplements; Sleep hygiene
Precautions_Contraindications: CHECK SERUM FERRITIN / IRON STORES FIRST BEFORE ANY DRUG THERAPY. Oral Iron supplementation is first-line if Ferritin <50 mcg/L. Pramipexole/Ropinirole (Dopamine Agonists) and Pregabalin are Rx only; risk of augmentation (worsening of symptoms earlier in day) with long-term dopamine agonists
Home_Care_Advice: Maintain regular sleep schedule; Perform light leg stretching and warm bath before bedtime; Avoid caffeine, alcohol, nicotine, and diphenhydramine-containing cold medicines (they worsen RLS); Massage legs gently
Lab_Investigations: Serum Ferritin, Iron, and TIBC (MANDATORY - target Ferritin >50 mcg/L); Serum Creatinine; HbA1c; Fasting Blood Glucose (rule out diabetic neuropathy)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Severe sudden onset daytime sleepiness while driving (Dopamine agonist side effect); Impulse control disorders (pathological gambling/hypersexuality on dopamine agonists); Severe insomnia

Primary_Symptoms: Systemic skeletal disease with low bone mineral density (DEXA T-score ≤-2.5); Usually asymptomatic until a low-trauma fragility fracture occurs
Secondary_Symptoms: Fragility fractures (vertebral compression, distal radius / Colles fracture, hip fracture); Loss of height; Kyphosis ('dowager's hump'); Chronic back pain
Clarifying_Questions: 1. DEXA scan me T-score -2.5 se kam aaya hai?; 2. Chhoti chot par haddi tootne (fragility fracture) ki history hai?; 3. Umar 50+ ya menopause ho chuka hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Calcium + Vitamin D3 First-Line + Alendronate OR Zoledronic Acid / Teriparatide
Adult_Strength_Mg: 500 Elemental Calcium / 2500 IU Vitamin D3 / 70 mg (Alendronate)
Meal_Timing: Empty Stomach (Alendronate: first thing in morning with full glass of plain water)
Duration_Days: ONCE A WEEK for Alendronate (3 to 5 years duration under specialist)
Supportive_Medicines: Calcitriol 0.25 mcg OD; Teriparatide 20 mcg SC daily (for severe osteoporosis); Denosumab 60 mg SC 6-monthly
Precautions_Contraindications: Bisphosphonates (Alendronate) are Rx only. **ALENDRONATE MUST BE TAKEN ON AN EMPTY STOMACH FIRST THING IN MORNING WITH FULL GLASS OF PLAIN WATER, REMAINING STRICTLY UPRIGHT (SITTING/STANDING) FOR AT LEAST 30 MINUTES BEFORE ANY FOOD/DRINK** to prevent severe erosive esophagitis. Contraindicated in esophagitis/stricture, inability to sit upright for 30 mins, severe CKD (eGFR <35), and hypocalcemia. Regular DEXA monitoring required
Home_Care_Advice: Take Calcium and Vitamin D3 daily; Perform regular weight-bearing exercises (brisk walking, resistance training); Maintain fall-prevention measures at home (good lighting, anti-skid bathroom mats, remove throw rugs); Avoid smoking and excess alcohol
Lab_Investigations: Dual-Energy X-ray Absorptiometry (DEXA Scan - Gold standard T-score ≤-2.5); Serum Calcium, Phosphate, Alkaline Phosphatase; Serum 25(OH)D; Serum Creatinine
Emergency_Red_Flags: Low-trauma hip, spine, or wrist fracture; Severe difficulty swallowing or retrosternal chest pain after Alendronate (Esophagitis emergency); Thigh/groin pain (atypical femur fracture risk)

Primary_Symptoms: Mildly reduced bone mineral density (DEXA T-score between -1.0 and -2.5); Asymptomatic; Precursor state to Osteoporosis
Secondary_Symptoms: Absence of fragility fractures; General bone tiredness; Postmenopausal status; Risk of progression
Clarifying_Questions: 1. DEXA scan report me T-score -1.0 se -2.5 ke beech hai?; 2. Menopause ho gaya hai ya umar 50+ hai?; 3. Calcium/Vitamin D report kaisa hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Calcium Carbonate 500 mg + Vitamin D3 2000 IU Daily
Supportive_Medicines: Weight-bearing exercise program; Dietary Calcium optimization
Precautions_Contraindications: Calcium and Vitamin D3 supplementation as per daily requirement. Avoid high-dose self-supplementation for prolonged unmonitored periods (risk of hypercalcemia, hypercalciuria, and renal stones). Routine bisphosphonates NOT indicated for simple Osteopenia unless FRAX high risk
Home_Care_Advice: Engage in regular weight-bearing exercises (brisk walking 30 mins 5 days/week); Eat Calcium-rich foods (milk, curd, paneer, leafy greens, ragi); Get 15-20 mins daily morning sunlight exposure; Stop smoking
Lab_Investigations: DEXA Scan (T-score between -1.0 and -2.5; calculate FRAX 10-year fracture risk score); Serum 25(OH)D; Serum Calcium & Creatinine
Emergency_Red_Flags: Fracture from a simple fall from standing height; T-score declining below -2.5 on follow-up DEXA scan

Primary_Symptoms: Defective bone mineralization in adults due to severe Vitamin D deficiency; Generalized dull aching BONE PAIN and muscle weakness
Secondary_Symptoms: Proximal muscle weakness (difficulty rising from chair or climbing stairs - 'waddling gait'); Bone tenderness over sternum/tibia; Pathological microfractures
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Poore sharir ki haddiya me andar tak meetha dard rehta hai?; 2. Kurse se uthne me thagho me kamzori (waddling walk) hai?; 3. Vitamin D level kitna kam aaya hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Cholecalciferol (Vitamin D3) 60,000 IU Weekly + Calcium Carbonate 500 mg BD
Dosage_Frequency: ONCE A WEEK ONLY for 8 weeks (Cholecalciferol) / BD (Calcium)
Meal_Timing: After Food (With fat-containing meal for Vitamin D)
Duration_Days: 8 weeks loading, then 1000-2000 IU daily maintenance
Supportive_Medicines: Magnesium 250 mg OD; Sun exposure
Precautions_Contraindications: Vitamin D3 60,000 IU is taken ONCE A WEEK for 8 weeks, individualized by serum 25(OH)D levels. CAUTION AGAINST HIGH-DOSE DAILY SELF-SUPPLEMENTATION FOR LONG PERIODS (causes Vitamin D toxicity, severe hypercalcemia, and renal failure)
Home_Care_Advice: Take Vitamin D3 60,000 IU strictly ONCE A WEEK with milk or fat-containing meal; Take Calcium tablets daily after food; Get 20 mins morning sunlight on face and arms; Perform gentle low-impact walking
Lab_Investigations: Serum 25-Hydroxy Vitamin D [25(OH)D - <12-20 ng/mL diagnostic]; Serum Calcium, Phosphate (low), and Alkaline Phosphatase (markedly elevated); Serum PTH (secondary hyperparathyroidism); Plain X-rays (Looser's zones / pseudofractures)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Severe muscle tetany or spasms (Severe Hypocalcemia); Nausea, vomiting, confusion, and polyuria (Vitamin D toxicity / Hypercalcemia); Pathological bone fracture

Common_Names_Hindi: Vitamin D ki kami ka dard
Primary_Symptoms: Symptomatic Vitamin D deficiency [25(OH)D <20 ng/mL]: Diffuse non-specific body aches, deep bone pain, and proximal muscle heaviness/fatigue
Secondary_Symptoms: Difficulty climbing stairs or standing from low seating; Persistent lower back and shin aching; Fatigue; Frequent muscle twitches
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Blood test me Vitamin D level 20 ng/mL se kam aaya hai?; 2. Poore sharir aur pairo me thakan aur bone pain rehta hai?; 3. Sunlight exposure kam hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Cholecalciferol (Vitamin D3) 60,000 IU Weekly
Dosage_Frequency: ONCE A WEEK ONLY for 8 weeks
Meal_Timing: After Food (With milk or fatty meal)
Duration_Days: 8 weeks loading, followed by monthly maintenance
Supportive_Medicines: Calcium Carbonate 500 mg OD; Sunlight exposure
Precautions_Contraindications: Cholecalciferol 60,000 IU is taken ONCE A WEEK for 8 weeks, dose individualized by baseline serum 25(OH)D. Avoid taking 60,000 IU daily (risk of hypercalcemia, confusion, and kidney damage). Regular serum 25(OH)D recheck
Home_Care_Advice: Take 60,000 IU capsule ONCE A WEEK with milk; Expose face, arms, and legs to direct morning sunlight for 15-20 mins daily without sunscreen; Eat egg yolks, fatty fish, and fortified dairy
Lab_Investigations: Serum 25-Hydroxy Vitamin D [25(OH)D level]; Serum Calcium & Phosphate; Serum Creatinine & Alkaline Phosphatase
Emergency_Red_Flags: Signs of Vitamin D Toxicity: intractable vomiting, confusion, severe constipation, polyuria, and extreme thirst; Severe muscle tetany

Primary_Symptoms: Disorganized bone remodeling with excessive osteoclastic resorption and faulty bone formation; Deep aching bone pain, worst at rest
Secondary_Symptoms: Bony enlargement and bowing deformities (tibia/femur); Increased local skin warmth over bone; Hearing loss (skull involvement); Pathological fractures
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Ek hi haddi (tibia/femur/skull) me gehra dard aur aakar badalna (bowing) hua hai?; 2. Skull bada hone se hat size ya hearing me kami aayi hai?; 3. Alkaline Phosphatase elevated hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Rx - specialist supervision required (Intravenous Zoledronic Acid 5 mg single infusion / Oral Risedronate)
Dosage_Frequency: Single IV Infusion over 15-30 mins under Specialist
Supportive_Medicines: Calcium Carbonate 500 mg + Vitamin D3 1000 IU daily; Analgesics for bone pain; Orthopedic surgical deformity correction
Max_Safe_Limit_24h: Single 5 mg IV dose per year or as indicated
Precautions_Contraindications: Rx - specialist supervision required. Intravenous Zoledronic Acid requires adequate hydration and pre-infusion serum calcium/creatinine check. Hypocalcemia must be corrected prior to infusion. Monitor for acute phase reaction (fever, flu-like symptoms)
Home_Care_Advice: Ensure adequate hydration before and after IV infusion; Take daily Calcium and Vitamin D3 supplements; Avoid high-impact loading on bowed bones; Regular follow-up with endocrinologist
Lab_Investigations: Serum Total Alkaline Phosphatase (markedly elevated diagnostic marker); Serum Calcium & Phosphate; Plain X-rays (shows osteolytic/sclerotic cotton-wool appearance); Radionuclide Bone Scan
Emergency_Red_Flags: Sudden onset bone fracture from minor movement; High-output heart failure (due to hypervascular bone lesions); Rapidly expanding bone mass with severe pain (Osteosarcoma transformation risk)

Common_Names_Hindi: Plaster ke baad ki jakdan; Post-Fracture Stiffness
Primary_Symptoms: Joint stiffness and markedly restricted range of motion in a joint following prolonged cast immobilization or fracture fixation surgery
Secondary_Symptoms: Periarticular soft tissue tightness; Muscle atrophy; Residual mild aching pain on passive stretch; Joint capsule contracture
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Fracture/Plaster khulne ke baad jod (joint) jam aur kada ho gaya hai?; 2. Jod poora modne ya seedha karne me takleef hoti hai?; 3. Pain severity kitni hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Paracetamol OR Aceclofenac + Intensive Active Physical Therapy
Supportive_Medicines: Topical Diclofenac gel; Warm hydrotherapy / paraffin wax bath; Active and passive physical therapy exercises
Precautions_Contraindications: Oral NSAIDs short course after food prior to physical therapy sessions. Primary management is structured active mobilization and physical therapy. DO NOT ALLOW AGGRESSIVE FORCED MANUAL BONE MANIPULATION BY UNQUALIFIED PERSONS
Home_Care_Advice: Perform active range-of-motion exercises 4-5 times daily; Apply warm compresses for 15 mins before exercise to relax soft tissues; Perform hydrotherapy (movement in warm water); Avoid violent forceful passive stretching
Lab_Investigations: Follow-up X-rays of fracture site (confirms complete bony union before aggressive rehabilitation); Joint ROM measurement
Emergency_Red_Flags: Reflex Sympathetic Dystrophy / Complex Regional Pain Syndrome (CRPS): severe burning pain, hypersensitivity to light touch, shiny skin, and diffuse swelling; Fracture non-union or re-fracture

Primary_Symptoms: FIRST AID ONLY: Severe acute localized bone pain, swelling, ecchymosis, bony crepitus, and complete inability to bear weight/use limb post trauma
Secondary_Symptoms: Bony deformity; Angulation or rotation of limb; Point bone tenderness; False movement at non-joint site
Typical_Duration: Acute emergency (requires immediate hospital transfer & X-ray)
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Chot/girne ke baad haddi par severe local dard, soojan aur tedha-pan hai?; 2. Limb bilkul use nahi ho raha?; 3. Chamdi phati hui hai (open fracture)?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: FIRST AID ONLY: Paracetamol (for transport pain) -> GO TO HOSPITAL FOR X-RAY IMMEDIATELY
Supportive_Medicines: Immobilization splint; Sterile dressing (if open wound); Ice wrapped in cloth
Precautions_Contraindications: FIRST AID ONLY. IMMOBILIZE THE LIMB IMMEDIATELY. ICE WRAPPED IN CLOTH. DO NOT ATTEMPT TO STRAIGHTEN OR ALIGN BENT BONE AT HOME. KEEP PATIENT NPO (NOTHING BY MOUTH) AS EMERGENCY SURGERY OR SEDATION IS LIKELY. NO DRUG DOSE BEYOND PARACETAMOL
Home_Care_Advice: First Aid Protocol: 1. Immobilize injured limb using splint/cardboard; 2. Apply Ice pack wrapped in cloth over swelling; 3. Do NOT straighten bent bone; 4. Keep NPO (no food/water) in case surgery needed; 5. Transport immediately to hospital for X-ray
Lab_Investigations: Emergency Plain X-rays (AP and Lateral views of injured bone including joint above and below); CT Scan (for intra-articular fractures)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Emergency Red Flags: Open Fracture (bone protruding through skin breakdown - emergency infection risk); Absent distal pulse / cold pale limb (Vascular compromise); Loss of distal sensation; Compartment Syndrome

Primary_Symptoms: Localized muscle pain, swelling, and ecchymosis (bluish-purple discoloration) following direct blunt impact/trauma to muscle belly
Secondary_Symptoms: Tenderness directly over impact zone; Restricted muscle contraction and stretch due to hematoma; Local tightness
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Seedhi chot/maar lagne ke baad manspeshi par soojan aur neela dhabba (bruise) bana hai?; 2. Choone par dard hota hai?; 3. Ghutna/haath modne me takleef hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Paracetamol OR Aceclofenac + RICE Protocol
Supportive_Medicines: Topical Heparinoid / Hirudoid cream (for hematoma resolution); Compression wrap; RICE protocol
Precautions_Contraindications: First-line: RICE protocol (Rest, Ice, Compression, Elevation) and early gentle movement as pain allows; avoid heat and vigorous massage in first 48-72 hours (prevents Myositis Ossificans formation). Oral NSAIDs short course after food
Home_Care_Advice: Follow RICE protocol: Rest, Ice pack wrapped in towel for 15 mins 3-4 times daily for first 48h, Compression bandage, Elevate limb; STRICTLY AVOID DEEP HEAT AND VIGOROUS MASSAGE FOR 72 HOURS (prevents intramuscular calcification)
Lab_Investigations: Ultrasound Muscle (evaluates intramuscular hematoma volume); Plain X-ray (rules out underlying bone fracture or late Myositis Ossificans)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Rapidly expanding intramuscular hematoma; Severe unremitting pain with compartment tightness (Compartment Syndrome risk); High fever with local fluctuation

Common_Names_Hindi: Exercise ke baad ka dard; DOMS
Primary_Symptoms: Diffuse muscle soreness, stiffness, and tenderness developing 24-48 hours after unaccustomed or strenuous eccentric exercise
Secondary_Symptoms: Temporary reduction in muscle strength; Mild localized edema; Peak soreness at 48 hours, resolving spontaneously by 72-96 hours
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Nayi workout ya heavy physical kaam karne ke 1-2 din baad manspeshiyo me dard shuru hua hai?; 2. 2-3 din me apne aap kam ho raha hai?; 3. Urine ka color normal hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Paracetamol OR Topical Diclofenac Gel + Active Recovery
Dosage_Frequency: TDS SOS (Paracetamol) / Local application 3-4 times daily
Supportive_Medicines: Warm hydrotherapy bath; Gentle foam rolling; Light active recovery exercise; Hydration
Precautions_Contraindications: Topical diclofenac gel and paracetamol are first-line OTC choices. Stop and see doctor if pain lasts beyond 7 days. Avoid overuse of systemic NSAIDs as they may blunt long-term muscle adaptation. MUST RULE OUT RHABDOMYOLYSIS IF URINE IS DARK TEA-COLORED
Home_Care_Advice: Perform light active recovery (gentle walking, cycling); Apply warm bath compresses after 48h; Perform gentle muscle stretching and foam rolling; Ensure adequate fluid hydration and protein intake
Lab_Investigations: Clinical evaluation; Serum Creatine Kinase (CK) & Urine Myoglobin (ONLY IF RHABDOMYOLYSIS SUSPECTED due to dark urine and extreme pain)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Dark tea-colored or cola-colored urine (Rhabdomyolysis emergency); Severe muscle swelling with inability to move limb; Symptoms persisting >7 days

Primary_Symptoms: Triad: Severe acute muscle pain/weakness + Muscle swelling + DARK TEA-COLORED / COLA-COLORED URINE following extreme exertion, trauma, or statins
Secondary_Symptoms: Profound fatigue; Nausea; Vomiting; Oliguria/Anuria; Confusion; Cardiac arrhythmias secondary to hyperkalemia; Acute Kidney Injury
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Severe workout, chot, ya statin dawai ke baad urine ka color TEA/COLA JAISA KAALA/BHOORA aaya hai?; 2. Manspeshiyo me bhayankar dard aur kamzori hai?; 3. Peshab kam ho raha hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: None - emergency hospital referral
Popular_Indian_Brands: Injection Normal Saline 0.9% IV Infusion + IV Sodium Bicarbonate
Dosage_Frequency: Immediate emergency aggressive IV fluid hydration + Forced Diuresis / Hemodialysis
Supportive_Medicines: Immediate ER / ICU Admission; Aggressive IV Normal Saline Hydration (200-500 mL/hr); Urine Alkalinization; Treatment of Hyperkalemia; Emergency Hemodialysis if AKI refractory
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Life-threatening emergency with high risk of acute renal failure and fatal cardiac arrest. STOP ALL STATINS AND OFFENDING DRUGS IMMEDIATELY. Do NOT delay seeking emergency hospital care
Home_Care_Advice: Immediate emergency transfer to hospital ICU; Stop all statin medications and strenuous exercise immediately; Drink water if conscious and awaiting transport, but IV fluids in ER are mandatory
Lab_Investigations: Serum Creatine Kinase (CK - markedly elevated >5,000-100,000 U/L); Urine Myoglobin; Serum Electrolytes (Potassium monitoring); Serum Creatinine & Blood Urea; ABG
Emergency_Red_Flags: Emergency Red Flags: Dark tea-colored / cola-colored urine; Severe muscle swelling and weakness; Anuria/Oliguria; Cardiac arrhythmias (Hyperkalemia); Confusion

Primary_Symptoms: 5 Ps: PAIN OUT OF PROPORTION to injury, Pain on PASSIVE STRETCH, Paresthesia, Pallor, Paralysis, Pulselessness (late); Tense wooden muscle compartment
Secondary_Symptoms: Excruciating unremitting limb pain non-responsive to opioids; Hypoesthesia in distal nerve distribution; Tense, hard, swollen muscle compartment
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Chot, fracture, ya tight plaster ke baad limb me UNBEARABLE PAIN HO RAHA HAI JO PAINKILLER SE BHI TEEK NAHI HOTA?; 2. Limb kada/wooden sooja hai?; 3. Ungliyo me sunn-pan hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: None - emergency hospital referral
Popular_Indian_Brands: Injection Morphine IV / Injection Tramadol IV (for transport)
Dosage_Frequency: Immediate emergency Surgical Fasciotomy (within 6 hours to prevent permanent muscle necrosis/amputation)
Supportive_Medicines: Immediate ER Transfer; Emergency Surgical Fasciotomy (complete release of fascia compartments); Removal of all tight casts/dressings; Oxygen; IV Hydration
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Life-threatening surgical emergency. DO NOT ELEVATE LIMB ABOVE HEART LEVEL (elevation reduces capillary perfusion pressure). DO NOT APPLY COMPRESSION. REMOVE ALL CIRCULAR CASTS/BANDAGES IMMEDIATELY
Home_Care_Advice: Remove any tight bandages, dressings, or circular casts immediately; Keep limb at heart level (DO NOT ELEVATE); Transport patient immediately to emergency surgery department
Lab_Investigations: Intracompartmental Pressure Measurement (Gold standard - delta pressure <30 mmHg diagnostic); Serum CK; Plain X-rays; Doppler Ultrasound
Emergency_Red_Flags: Emergency Red Flags: Severe excruciating pain out of proportion; Tense, wooden, rock-hard swollen limb compartment; Severe pain on passive digit stretching; Distal numbness/paralysis

Primary_Symptoms: Acute or chronic infection of bone (Staph aureus); Severe localized bone pain, local warmth, swelling, erythema, and inability to bear weight
Secondary_Symptoms: High fever with chills/rigors; Purulent sinus tract drainage (in chronic osteomyelitis); Systemic toxicity; Local bone tenderness
Typical_Duration: Weeks to months (requires prolonged IV/oral antibiotics)
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Haddi me andar tak severe dard, soojan, aur lalapan ke sath tez bukhar hai?; 2. Chamdi se mawaad (pus) nikalne waala chhed (sinus) bana hai?; 3. Diabetes ya purani chot ki history hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Rx - specialist supervision required (Parenteral IV Bactericidal Antibiotics - Cefazolin / Ceftriaxone / Vancomycin + Surgical Debridement)
Duration_Days: Rx - specialist supervision required (4 to 6 weeks course)
Supportive_Medicines: Surgical bone debridement / Sequestrectomy; Immobilization splint; Inflammatory marker monitoring
Precautions_Contraindications: Rx - specialist supervision required. Long-term parenteral/oral antibiotic therapy required (4-6 weeks minimum). Surgical removal of necrotic bone (sequestrum) often mandatory in chronic cases. Regular CBC, ESR, CRP monitoring
Home_Care_Advice: Rest and immobilize affected bone; Keep purulent sinus wounds dressed with sterile dressings; Eat high-protein diet; Strictly complete full 4-6 week antibiotic course without defaulting
Lab_Investigations: Plain X-rays (shows periosteal reaction, lytic lesions, sequestrum); MRI Bone (Gold standard for early acute osteomyelitis); ESR and CRP (markedly elevated); Blood and Bone/Pus Cultures
Emergency_Red_Flags: High fever with septic shock signs; Pathological fracture through infected bone; Spreading cellulitis and tissue necrosis

Primary_Symptoms: Progressive deep groin pain radiating to anterior thigh or knee, worsened by weight-bearing and relieved by rest; Limping gait
Secondary_Symptoms: Marked restriction of hip internal rotation and abduction; Pain at rest and night (advanced stage); Microcollapse of femoral head
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Kulhe/groin me andar tak dard hai jo chalne par badhta hai?; 2. Steroid dawai, alcohol, ya purani chot ki history hai?; 3. Hip MRI report hua hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Paracetamol OR Aceclofenac / Naproxen + Non-Weight Bearing (Early) / Total Hip Arthroplasty (Advanced)
Supportive_Medicines: Bisphosphonates (Alendronate short-term); Core Decompression surgery (Stage 1-2); Total Hip Arthroplasty (THA - Stage 3-4 under specialist)
Precautions_Contraindications: Oral NSAIDs short course after food for acute pain flares. Primary management depends on Ficat stage: early stages require bone offloading/core decompression, advanced femoral head collapse requires Total Hip Replacement surgery
Home_Care_Advice: Strictly avoid weight-bearing on affected hip (use crutches/walker); Avoid high-impact sports, running, and heavy lifting; Stop alcohol completely; Avoid unnecessary steroid use
Lab_Investigations: MRI Both Hips (Gold standard - shows 'double line sign' and femoral head osteonecrosis); X-ray Pelvis with Hips AP and Frog-leg Lateral views (Ficat staging)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Sudden collapse of femoral head with severe acute inability to walk; Severe unremitting rest pain; High fever with joint swelling

Primary_Symptoms: Generalized joint laxity with widespread joint/muscle pain, fatigue, and frequent joint subluxations/sprains; Beighton score ≥5/9
Secondary_Symptoms: Joint popping and clicking; Soft hyperextensible skin; Easy bruising; Postural orthostatic tachycardia (POTS) association; Recurrent ankle sprains
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Jod zaroorat se zyada aage-piche mudte (flexible) hain?; 2. Ungliya ya kohni piche tak aasaani se mud jati hain?; 3. Baar-baar sprains ya jod nikalte hain?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Paracetamol OR Topical Diclofenac Gel + Proprioceptive Physical Therapy
Dosage_Frequency: TDS SOS (Paracetamol) / Local application 3-4 times daily
Supportive_Medicines: Topical NSAID gel; Supportive joint braces/taping; Proprioceptive joint strengthening exercises
Precautions_Contraindications: Topical NSAIDs and paracetamol first-line OTC choices for joint pain flares. Avoid heavy high-impact contact sports that cause joint dislocation. Do NOT perform forced extreme joint stretching tricks
Home_Care_Advice: Perform low-impact joint stabilization exercises (swimming, pilates, isometric strengthening); Avoid high-impact contact sports and extreme joint hyperextension tricks; Wear supportive braces during sports
Lab_Investigations: Clinical Beighton Hypermobility Score (≥5/9 diagnostic); Echocardiogram (rule out aortic root dilation if Marfan/Ehlers-Danlos suspected); Genetic testing
Emergency_Red_Flags: Recurrent major joint dislocations (e.g., shoulder/patella dislocation); Chest pain or aortic root dilation signs; Severe orthostatic dizziness/syncope

Primary_Symptoms: Multisystem autoimmune disease: Malar 'butterfly' facial rash sparing nasolabial folds, photosensitivity, non-erosive polyarthritis, and fatigue
Secondary_Symptoms: Oral ulcers; Alopecia (hair loss); Serositis (pleurisy/pericarditis); Lupus nephritis (frothy urine/edema); Raynaud's phenomenon; Cytopenias
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Chehre par naak aur gaalo par butterfly jaisa lal rash hai jo dhoop me badhta hai?; 2. Jodon me dard, hair fall, aur muuh me chhale hain?; 3. ANA test positive aaya hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Rx - rheumatologist supervision required (Hydroxychloroquine + Systemic Corticosteroids / Immunosuppressants under Rheumatologist)
Supportive_Medicines: Sunscreen SPF 50+ (mandatory); Mycophenolate Mofetil / Azathioprine (for Lupus Nephritis under specialist); Calcium + Vitamin D3
Precautions_Contraindications: Rx - rheumatologist supervision required. Hydroxychloroquine requires baseline and annual Ophthalmic Retinal Screening. Corticosteroids require sugar, BP, and bone monitoring. Mandatory Sunscreen SPF 50+ application. Do not provide self-treatment plan
Home_Care_Advice: STRICT SUN PROTECTION MANDATORY: Apply broad-spectrum Sunscreen SPF 50+ daily every 3 hours outdoors; Wear full-sleeved protective clothing and wide-brimmed hats; Rest during flares; Avoid sun exposure
Lab_Investigations: ANA (Antinuclear Antibodies by IFA - Screening test); Anti-dsDNA and Anti-Sm Antibodies (Specific); Serum Complement C3/C4 levels; Urine Routine & Microalbumin (Lupus Nephritis screen); CBC
Emergency_Red_Flags: Lupus Nephritis flare (frothy urine, leg edema, acute hypertension, rising creatinine); Severe chest pain/breathlessness (Pericarditis/Pleurisy); CNS Lupus (seizures, psychosis, stroke)

Primary_Symptoms: Symmetrical muscle aching, stiffness, tenderness, or heaviness affecting large proximal muscle groups (thighs, buttocks, calves) post statin initiation
Secondary_Symptoms: Absence of joint swelling; Mild muscle fatigue; Onset usually within weeks to months of starting or increasing statin dose; Serum CK normal or elevated
Typical_Duration: Resolves within 2 to 4 weeks after statin pause
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Cholesterol/Statin dawai (Atorvastatin/Rosuvastatin) shuru karne ke baad pairo/thighs me dard shuru hua hai?; 2. Urine ka color normal hai ya kaala/tea-like hai?; 3. CK test hua hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: ADVISE NOT STOPPING STATIN ON YOUR OWN -> CONSULT DOCTOR FOR CK TEST AND STATIN DOSE ADJUSTMENT
Supportive_Medicines: Serum Creatine Kinase (CK) test; Coenzyme Q10 100 mg OD (under doctor guidance); Switch to alternate statin (e.g., Rosuvastatin 5 mg alternate day or Ezetimibe)
Precautions_Contraindications: ADVISE PATIENT NOT TO STOP OR ALTER STATIN DOSE ON THEIR OWN. SEE DOCTOR FOR CREATINE KINASE (CK) TEST. Statin can be paused, dose-reduced, or switched ONLY BY A DOCTOR. Rule out hypothyroidism and Vitamin D deficiency (which increase statin myopathy risk)
Home_Care_Advice: Do not stop statin on your own without consulting prescribing doctor; Drink plenty of fluids; Report any change in urine color immediately; Avoid unaccustomed strenuous exercise
Lab_Investigations: Serum Creatine Kinase (CK level - evaluates muscle inflammation/rhabdomyolysis); LFT; Serum 25(OH)D and TSH; Serum Creatinine
Emergency_Red_Flags: Dark tea-colored or cola-colored urine with severe muscle breakdown (Rhabdomyolysis emergency - stop statin and go to ER immediately); Severe muscle weakness preventing walking

Disease_Name: Bone Pain with Red Flags (Suspected Malignancy)
Common_Names_Hindi: Haddi ka dard Red Flags; Suspected Malignancy
Primary_Symptoms: NEEDS URGENT IN-PERSON EVALUATION AND IMAGING: Unexplained deep aching bone pain that IS WORST AT NIGHT AND AWAKENS PATIENT FROM SLEEP
Secondary_Symptoms: Unexplained weight loss; Persistent fever; Night sweats; Pathological fracture from minor trauma; Palpable bone mass; Localized bone tenderness
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Haddi me gehra dard hai jo RAAT KO SOTE ME SEVERE BADHTA HAI aur neend todta hai?; 2. Weight kam ho raha hai ya bukhar rehta hai?; 3. Bina badi chot ke haddi me fracture hua hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: NEEDS URGENT IN-PERSON EVALUATION AND IMAGING (NO HOME TREATMENT OR DRUGS TO BE PRESCRIBED)
Duration_Days: Urgent Referral to Oncologist / Orthopedic Oncologist
Supportive_Medicines: Urgent Imaging (X-rays, MRI, PET-CT Scan); Bone Biopsy; Serum Protein Electrophoresis
Precautions_Contraindications: NO HOME DRUG TREATMENT OR NSAIDS TO BE PRESCRIBED. WRITE 'NEEDS URGENT IN-PERSON EVALUATION AND IMAGING'. Unexplained nocturnal bone pain is a primary red flag for Primary Bone Tumors (Osteosarcoma, Ewing's) or Metastatic Bone Disease (from breast, prostate, lung, kidney, thyroid) or Multiple Myeloma
Home_Care_Advice: Do NOT self-medicate with painkillers. Seek immediate urgent in-person medical evaluation with an oncologist or orthopedic specialist; Avoid heavy weight-bearing on painful bone until evaluated to prevent pathological fracture
Lab_Investigations: Urgent Plain X-rays of affected bone (shows lytic/sclerotic lesion, periosteal sunburst reaction, cortical destruction); MRI Affected Region; Serum Protein Electrophoresis & Serum Free Light Chains (Multiple Myeloma screen); PET-CT Scan; Bone Biopsy
Emergency_Red_Flags: Urgent Oncological Emergency Red Flags: Severe unremitting nocturnal bone pain; Pathological fracture; Spinal cord compression signs (leg paralysis, bowel/bladder loss); Hypercalcemia (confusion, severe vomiting)

Primary_Symptoms: Unilateral throbbing or pulsating headache preceded by visual aura (flashing lights, zigzag lines, blind spots) or sensory paresthesias
Secondary_Symptoms: Photophobia; Phonophobia; Nausea; Vomiting; Transient numbness/tingling in hand or face
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Sirdard se pehle aakhon ke aage roshni ke dhabbe, chamak, ya sunn-pan aata hai?; 2. Sirdard sar ke ek hi taraf hota hai?; 3. Sirdard mahine me kitni baar hota hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Paracetamol OR Naproxen (Acute attack) / Sumatriptan (Rx under doctor)
Dosage_Frequency: TDS SOS (Paracetamol) / BD SOS (Naproxen) / Single dose at onset (Sumatriptan)
Supportive_Medicines: Domperidone 10 mg (for nausea); Propranolol / Amitriptyline (for prophylaxis if >2-4 attacks/month under neurologist)
Max_Safe_Limit_24h: 3250 mg Paracetamol / 1000 mg Naproxen / 100 mg Sumatriptan
Precautions_Contraindications: Simple analgesics (Paracetamol/Naproxen) first-line for acute attacks. Triptans are Rx only; contraindicated in ischemic heart disease, uncontrolled hypertension, history of stroke/TIA, and peripheral vascular disease. Avoid simple or combination analgesic use on more than 10-15 days per month to prevent Medication Overuse Headache. Ergotamine is Rx only and strictly contraindicated in pregnancy. Never stop or change preventive medication doses on your own
Home_Care_Advice: Rest in a quiet, dark, sound-proof room during an attack; Apply cold ice compress to forehead or temples; Maintain a consistent sleep schedule and hydration; Identify and avoid personal triggers (bright lights, missed meals, specific foods, stress)
Lab_Investigations: Clinical evaluation; MRI Brain (if atypical aura, persistent focal neurological deficits, or first episode after age 50)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Sudden worst headache of life ('Thunderclap'); Aura symptoms lasting >60 minutes; Persistent weakness or speech difficulty after headache resolves; Fever with stiff neck

Primary_Symptoms: Headache occurring on 15 or more days per month for >3 months, with at least 8 days per month meeting criteria for migraine headache
Secondary_Symptoms: Moderate to severe throbbing pain; Photophobia; Phonophobia; Nausea; Scalp allodynia; Daily functional impairment
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Mahine me 15 din se zyada sirdard rehta hai?; 2. Painkillers kitne din lete hain?; 3. Sirdard ke sath ulti ya roshni se takleef hoti hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Rx - neurologist supervision required (Propranolol / Amitriptyline / Topiramate / Flunarizine / Botulinum Toxin)
Duration_Days: Rx - neurologist supervision required (3 to 6 months continuous prophylaxis)
Supportive_Medicines: Pantoprazole 40 mg OD; Acute attack rescue medication (Sumatriptan SOS under strict limit)
Precautions_Contraindications: Rx - neurologist supervision required. Never stop or change preventive doses on your own; sudden withdrawal can trigger severe rebound status migrainosus. Beta-blockers (Propranolol) contraindicated in asthma, sinus bradycardia, and heart block. Topiramate contraindicated in pregnancy (teratogenic) and acute glaucoma. Triptans contraindicated in coronary artery disease and uncontrolled HTN. Limit acute analgesic intake to <10 days/month to avoid Medication Overuse Headache
Home_Care_Advice: Maintain a strict daily headache diary tracking frequency, intensity, and medication use; Practice regular sleep-wake hygiene; Manage stress with relaxation techniques; Avoid acute painkiller overuse
Lab_Investigations: MRI Brain (rule out secondary structural causes); Complete Blood Count; Thyroid Profile (TSH)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Sudden explosive onset of severe unremitting headache; New neurological deficits (facial droop, arm weakness); Fever with neck stiffness; Progressive headache in cancer history

Common_Names_Hindi: Dawai ke zyada use se sirdard; Rebound Headache
Primary_Symptoms: Daily or near-daily headache present upon awakening, caused by regular overuse of acute headache medications for >3 months
Secondary_Symptoms: Dull, diffuse, pressing or migraine-like headache; Irritability; Nausea; Sleep disturbance; Dependence on daily painkillers
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Aap mahine me 10-15 din se zyada painkillers (Paracetamol/NSAIDs/Triptans) lete hain?; 2. Dawai ka asar khatam hote hi sirdard fir shuru ho jata hai?; 3. Subah uthte hi sirdard rehta hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Abrupt Discontinuation / Structured Taper of Overused Medication under Doctor + Prophylaxis
Supportive_Medicines: Antiemetics (Metoclopramide SOS during withdrawal phase); Non-pharmacological bridge therapy; Hydration
Precautions_Contraindications: Never stop or change medications on your own without medical guidance. Taper or abruptly stop the overused acute analgesic strictly under doctor supervision. Expect withdrawal rebound headache lasting 2-10 days after stopping overused pain medicine. Prevent re-starting frequent acute analgesics; limit all acute pain medicine to <8-10 days per month. Avoid combination analgesics containing caffeine or opioids
Home_Care_Advice: Understand that overused pain medicine is the cause, not the solution, for the daily headache; Drink plenty of fluids (2-3 liters daily); Rest during the initial withdrawal phase; Use non-drug relief (ice packs, dark room, gentle neck stretching)
Lab_Investigations: Clinical evaluation; MRI Brain (rule out underlying structural intracranial pathology)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Sudden severe 'thunderclap' headache; Persistent vomiting with dehydration; Confusion, seizures, or focal neurological deficits

Common_Names_Hindi: Trigeminal Neuralgia; Chehre ki nass ka tez dard
Primary_Symptoms: Sudden, severe, electric shock-like, stabbing paroxysmal facial pain along V1, V2, or V3 distribution of trigeminal nerve (usually unilateral)
Secondary_Symptoms: Pain triggered by light touch, chewing, washing face, brushing teeth, smiling, or cold wind; Pain-free refractory periods between spasms
Typical_Duration: Seconds to 2 minutes per spasm (recurrent episodes over weeks/months)
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Chehre par (gaal, jabde, ya aakh ke paas) achanak bijli ke jhatke jaisa tez stabbing dard hota hai?; 2. Khana chabane, brush karne, ya chehre ko choone par dard shuru hota hai?; 3. Dard kitni der rehta hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Carbamazepine OR Oxcarbazepine
Dosage_Frequency: BD initial, titrated slowly up to TDS by doctor
Supportive_Medicines: Pregabalin 75 mg OD at bedtime; Baclofen 10 mg BD (under specialist supervision)
Precautions_Contraindications: Rx - neurologist supervision required. Carbamazepine is an antiepileptic drug; NEVER STOP OR CHANGE DOSE ON YOUR OWN (risk of severe rebound pain and seizures). HLA-B*1502 genetic testing recommended prior to starting carbamazepine in patients of Asian/Indian origin due to risk of fatal Stevens-Johnson Syndrome (SJS) / Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis (TEN). Monitor Complete Blood Count (risk of aplastic anemia/leukopenia) and Serum Sodium (risk of hyponatremia). Causes drowsiness, dizziness, and ataxia
Home_Care_Advice: Avoid known facial trigger zones during acute flares; Wash face with lukewarm water using soft gentle dabs; Eat soft foods and chew on unaffected side; Avoid cold wind drafts directly on face
Lab_Investigations: MRI Brain with thin-slice trigeminal nerve sequences (3D CISS/FIESTA - rules out neurovascular compression or Multiple Sclerosis); Complete Blood Count; Serum Electrolytes (Sodium); HLA-B*1502 screening
Emergency_Red_Flags: Severe generalized skin rash, fever, or mucosal ulcers (SJS/TEN reaction - STOP DRUG IMMEDIATELY AND GO TO ER); Progressive facial numbness or motor weakness; Unremitting agony preventing hydration

Common_Names_Hindi: Gardan se uthne waala sirdard; Cervicogenic Headache
Primary_Symptoms: Unilateral non-throbbing headache originating from neck/occipital region and radiating forward to forehead, temple, or retro-orbital area
Secondary_Symptoms: Neck pain and stiffness; Restricted cervical range of motion; Pain triggered by specific neck movements or sustained posture; Ipsilateral shoulder pain
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Sirdard gardan ke piche se shuru hokar aage aakh ya patti tak jata hai?; 2. Gardan modne ya lambe samay tak jhuk kar baithne par badhta hai?; 3. Gardan me aedan hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Paracetamol OR Aceclofenac + Physical Therapy
Supportive_Medicines: Thiocolchicoside 4 mg BD (if severe paraspinal muscle spasm present under doctor); Topical NSAID gel; Cervical posture exercises
Precautions_Contraindications: Oral NSAIDs short course (3-5 days) after food. Contraindicated in peptic ulcer, CKD, severe heart failure, uncontrolled HTN, asthma, and 3rd trimester pregnancy. Simple analgesics/topical NSAIDs first-line OTC choices. Muscle relaxants Rx only (drowsiness caution, contraindicated in pregnancy/lactation). Diagnostic/therapeutic cervical facet or greater occipital nerve blocks Rx under specialist
Home_Care_Advice: Maintain ergonomic posture during desk/computer work; Perform gentle cervical isometric exercises and chin tucks; Apply warm compresses to back of neck; Avoid prolonged forward head posture ('text neck')
Lab_Investigations: X-ray Cervical Spine (AP, Lateral, and Flexion-Extension views); MRI Cervical Spine (rule out C2-C3 disc prolapse or spinal cord compression)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Onset of arm weakness, numbness, or loss of hand dexterity; Sudden severe trauma prior to headache; Fever with neck stiffness; Loss of bowel/bladder control

Common_Names_Hindi: Chot ke baad ka sirdard; Post-Concussion Headache
Primary_Symptoms: Persistent headache developing within 7 days following a head injury or concussion, resembling tension-type or migraine headache
Secondary_Symptoms: Dizziness; Fatigue; Concentration difficulties; Irritability; Insomnia; Light and sound sensitivity
Typical_Duration: Weeks to months (usually resolves within 3-6 months)
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Head injury ya girne ke kitne din baad sirdard shuru hua?; 2. Dizziness, thakan, ya dhundla dikhna to nahi hai?; 3. Vomiting ya behoshi hui thi?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Paracetamol OR Amitriptyline (if chronic persistent post-traumatic headache under doctor)
Supportive_Medicines: Pantoprazole 40 mg OD; Rest protocol; Cognitive rest
Precautions_Contraindications: Avoid Aspirin and NSAIDs immediately post-injury until intracranial hemorrhage is ruled out. Never stop or change prescribed psychotropic/neurological medications on your own. Paracetamol is the safer initial choice for mild pain. If headache persists beyond 2 weeks, specialist neurological evaluation is mandatory
Home_Care_Advice: Enforce strict physical and cognitive rest in initial days post-injury; Limit screen time (mobile, TV, computer); Avoid sports, driving, and strenuous physical activity until cleared by a doctor; Maintain adequate hydration
Lab_Investigations: Non-Contrast CT Scan Brain (MANDATORY initially to rule out epidural/subdural hematoma or skull fracture); MRI Brain (if symptoms persist >2-4 weeks)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Emergency Red Flags: Sudden worst headache; Repeated vomiting; Progressive drowsiness or inability to awaken; One-sided arm/leg weakness; Fluid/blood discharge from nose or ears; Seizures; Asymmetric pupils

Common_Names_Hindi: Thunderclap Headache (Emergency); Dimag ki nass phatna
Primary_Symptoms: Sudden, explosive headache that reaches MAXIMUM SEVERE INTENSITY WITHIN 60 SECONDS ('worst headache of life'); High suspicion for ruptured cerebral aneurysm
Secondary_Symptoms: Neck stiffness; Repeated projectile vomiting; Altered mental status; Seizures; Loss of consciousness; Photophobia; Focal neurological deficits
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Sirdard achanak ek minute ke andar life ka sabse severe headache ban gaya?; 2. Ulti, gardan me aedan, ya behoshi aayi hai?; 3. Aankho ke samne dhundla-pan hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: None - emergency hospital referral
Popular_Indian_Brands: Injection Nimodipine IV / Oral Nimodipine (in ICU post-scan)
Dosage_Frequency: Immediate emergency transfer to tertiary neurosurgical ICU
Supportive_Medicines: Immediate ER Transfer; Emergency Non-Contrast CT Brain; Lumbar Puncture (if CT negative); Cerebral Angiography (DSA/CTA); Emergency Neurosurgical / Endovascular Coiling or Clipping
Precautions_Contraindications: Doctor prescription required; do not self-medicate; Life-threatening emergency. DO NOT GIVE ASPIRIN, NSAIDS, OR PAINKILLERS AT HOME (can worsen intracranial bleeding). Do NOT delay seeking emergency transport. Keep patient flat and calm
Home_Care_Advice: Immediate emergency hospital referral to a tertiary care center with neurosurgical facilities; Keep patient lying flat in a dark quiet environment; Do NOT give anything by mouth (NPO) as emergency surgery/procedure may be required
Lab_Investigations: Emergency Non-Contrast CT Brain (within 6 hours of onset); Lumbar Puncture (for xanthochromia if CT is normal); CT Angiogram (CTA) / Digital Subtraction Angiography (DSA)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Emergency Red Flags: Explosive onset worst headache within 60 seconds; Loss of consciousness; Neck stiffness with fever; Pupil dilation; Hemiparesis; Seizures

Primary_Symptoms: Severe new-onset unilateral temporal or occipital headache in patients >50 years, associated with TEMPORAL ARTERY TENDERNESS and JAW CLAUDICATION
Secondary_Symptoms: Jaw pain/cramping while chewing; Scalp tenderness (pain on combing hair); Amaurosis fugax (transient monocular vision loss); Polymyalgia rheumatica symptoms
Typical_Duration: Requires high-dose steroids for months to years
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Umar 50 se zyada hai aur kankhi (temple) me naya severe sirdard hai?; 2. Baal kankhi karne par scalp me dard hota hai ya khana chabate waqt jabde me dard hota hai?; 3. Aakhon ke samne andhera aata hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Rx - specialist supervision required (High-dose Systemic Corticosteroids - Prednisolone / IV Methylprednisolone under Specialist)
Duration_Days: Rx - specialist supervision required (Months with slow taper)
Supportive_Medicines: Calcium Carbonate 500 mg + Vitamin D3 1000 IU daily; Bisphosphonates (osteoporosis prophylaxis); PPI cover (Pantoprazole 40 mg OD)
Precautions_Contraindications: Rx - specialist supervision required. HIGH RISK OF PERMANENT BLINDNESS IF STEROID THERAPY IS DELAYED. Steroids must be initiated immediately upon clinical suspicion even before temporal artery biopsy results. Never stop steroids suddenly. Monitor blood glucose, BP, and bone density
Home_Care_Advice: Take oral steroids strictly as prescribed every morning with food; Report any visual changes immediately to doctor; Maintain calcium and vitamin D intake; Do not stop steroids abruptly
Lab_Investigations: ESR (>50 mm/hr, often >100) and CRP (markedly elevated - key diagnostic markers); Temporal Artery Ultrasound / Biopsy (Gold standard); Complete Blood Count
Emergency_Red_Flags: SUDDEN MONOCULAR OR BINOCULAR VISION LOSS / BLINDNESS (OPHTHALMIC EMERGENCY); Double vision (diplopia); Stroke-like symptoms (hemiparesis, dysarthria)

Primary_Symptoms: Progressive daily headache worse in morning and with coughing/straining, blurred vision, transient visual obscurations, and PULSATILE TINNITUS
Secondary_Symptoms: Papilledema on fundoscopy; Diplopia (horizontal 6th nerve palsy); Nausea; Neck stiffness; Associated with obesity or rapid weight gain in young females
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Sirdard ke sath aakhon ke samne achanak kuch seconds ke liye andhera (visual obscuration) aata hai?; 2. Kaan me dil ki dhadkan jaisi aawaaz (pulsatile tinnitus) sunai deti hai?; 3. Aakhon ke doctor ne piche sujan (papilledema) batayi hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Rx - specialist supervision required (Acetazolamide / Furosemide + Weight Loss)
Supportive_Medicines: Potassium supplements (Syp Potklor SOS as acetazolamide causes hypokalemia); Weight management program; Lumbar puncture (therapeutic)
Precautions_Contraindications: Rx - specialist supervision required. Acetazolamide is a carbonic anhydrase inhibitor; NEVER STOP OR CHANGE DOSE ON YOUR OWN. Contraindicated in severe renal/hepatic impairment, hyperchloremic acidosis, and sulfa allergy. Requires regular monitoring of serum electrolytes (risk of hypokalemia and metabolic acidosis) and visual fields
Home_Care_Advice: Engage in a structured weight-loss program if overweight (5-10% weight loss significantly reduces intracranial pressure); Avoid Vitamin A supplements, tetracyclines, and oral contraceptives (known triggers); Regular visual field testing
Lab_Investigations: Fundoscopy / Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT - checks papilledema); MRI Brain with MR Venogram (MRV - excludes cerebral venous sinus thrombosis); Lumbar Puncture (opening pressure >25 cm H2O)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Sudden rapid deterioration of vision or peripheral visual field loss (RISK OF PERMANENT BLINDNESS); Severe unremitting headache with persistent vomiting

Primary_Symptoms: Sudden acute unilateral facial weakness or paralysis developing over 24-48 hours, INVOLVING FOREHEAD FROWNING (inability to wrinkle forehead)
Secondary_Symptoms: Inability to close eye; Drooping of mouth corner; Drooling; Hyperacusis (sensitivity to loud sounds); Loss of taste on anterior 2/3 of tongue; Dry eye
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Chehre ke ek taraf ki manspeshiya achanak dhili/paralyzed ho gayi hain?; 2. Aakh poori band nahi ho rahi aur forehead par silvat (wrinkles) nahi ban rahi?; 3. Haath ya pair me kamzori to nahi hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Rx - doctor guidance required (Oral Corticosteroids - Prednisolone started within 72 hours) + Eye Protection
Adult_Strength_Mg: 50 to 60 mg Prednisolone daily total initial
Supportive_Medicines: Lubricating Eye Drops (Carboxymethylcellulose 0.5% q2h); Eye Ointment + Eye Taping at night; Oral Antivirals (Valacyclovir 1g TDS for 7 days under doctor in severe cases)
Precautions_Contraindications: Rx - doctor supervision required. Oral steroids must be initiated by a doctor strictly within 72 hours of onset to maximize recovery. Stroke must be ruled out: Bell's palsy involves FOREHEAD wrinkling loss, whereas stroke SPARES forehead and often has limb weakness. Protect affected eye from corneal drying/ulceration
Home_Care_Advice: Apply lubricating eye drops every 2 hours during day; Tape eye closed securely at night after applying eye ointment; Wear protective sunglasses outdoors to shield eye from dust and wind; Perform gentle facial muscle massage and exercises once pain subsides
Lab_Investigations: Clinical evaluation; MRI Brain (if atypical features, recurrent episodes, or no recovery after 6 weeks); HbA1c; Fasting Blood Glucose
Emergency_Red_Flags: Forehead SPARING with lower facial droop AND arm/leg weakness or speech difficulty (STROKE EMERGENCY - call 112); Severe eye pain, redness, or blurred vision (Corneal Ulceration emergency)

Primary_Symptoms: Involuntary, painless, tonic-clonic contractions of muscles on one side of face, starting around orbicularis oculi (eye twitching) and spreading to lower face
Secondary_Symptoms: Involuntary eye closure during spasms; Mouth twitching; Worse with stress, fatigue, or anxiety; Persistent clicking noise in ear
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Chehre ke ek taraf ki aakh aur gaal ke paas achanak apne aap phadkan/khichav hota hai?; 2. Thakan ya stress me badhta hai?; 3. Sirdard ya numbness to nahi hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Rx - specialist supervision required (Botulinum Toxin Injections / Carbamazepine / Baclofen / Microvascular Decompression Surgery)
Popular_Indian_Brands: Tegretol 100; Lioresal 10; Botulinum Toxin Type A
Supportive_Medicines: Local Botulinum Toxin Type A injections into affected facial muscles (Gold standard treatment, repeated every 3-4 months under neurologist)
Precautions_Contraindications: Rx - specialist supervision required. Oral medications (Carbamazepine, Baclofen) have limited efficacy and cause drowsiness/dizziness. Never stop prescribed neurological medications abruptly. Botulinum toxin injections must be administered strictly by a trained neurologist
Home_Care_Advice: Manage psychological stress through relaxation techniques; Ensure adequate sleep hygiene; Avoid excessive caffeine intake; Reassure patient regarding benign non-life-threatening nature
Lab_Investigations: MRI Brain with high-resolution CISS/FIESTA sequences (evaluates ectopic neurovascular compression of facial nerve at brainstem exit zone)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Progressive facial weakness or numbness; Hearing loss on affected side; Onset of double vision or balance instability

Primary_Symptoms: Postural and action tremor predominantly affecting both hands/forearms during voluntary movements (holding a cup, writing, using a spoon)
Secondary_Symptoms: Head tremor ('yes-yes' or 'no-no' motion); Voice tremor; Tremor IMPROVES WITH SMALL AMOUNTS OF ALCOHOL and rest; Absence of parkinsonian rigidity or bradykinesia
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Haath me kampan (shaking) tab hota hai jab aap koi kaam karte hain (jaise chai peena, likhna)?; 2. Aaram se haath god me rakhne par kampan ruk jata hai?; 3. Parivar me kisi ko ye problem hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Rx - doctor guidance required (Propranolol OR Primidone)
Supportive_Medicines: Topiramate / Gabapentin (second-line under neurologist); Adaptive heavy-handled eating utensils
Precautions_Contraindications: Rx - doctor supervision required. Never stop or change medication doses on your own. Propranolol (beta-blocker) is contraindicated in bronchial asthma, sinus bradycardia, heart block, and uncompensated heart failure. Monitor pulse rate and blood pressure regularly
Home_Care_Advice: Use weighted eating utensils, heavy mugs, and thick pens to damp hand tremors; Avoid caffeine, energy drinks, and stress triggers; Use two hands to hold cups/glasses; Maintain adequate sleep
Lab_Investigations: Thyroid Profile (TSH - rule out hyperthyroidism); Serum Electrolytes; Liver Function Tests; Clinical Neurological Examination
Emergency_Red_Flags: Resting tremor associated with slow movements and shuffling gait (Parkinson's Disease suspicion); Sudden dramatic onset or rapid asymmetric progression

Primary_Symptoms: Asymmetric RESTING TREMOR ('pill-rolling'), BRADYKINESIA (slowness of movement), RIGIDITY ('cogwheel'), and POSTURAL INSTABILITY
Secondary_Symptoms: Shuffling gait with reduced arm swing; Micrographia (small handwriting); Mask-like facial expression; Monotone quiet voice; Constipation; REM sleep behavior disorder
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Haath me kampan tab hota hai jab haath bilkul aaram se god me rakha ho?; 2. Chalne me dheema-pan, pairo ka ghaseatna, ya bina vajah chhote akshar me likhna shuru hua hai?; 3. Balance me kami hai?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Rx - specialist supervision required (Levodopa + Carbidopa / Dopamine Agonists - Pramipexole / MAO-B Inhibitors - Rasagiline)
Dosage_Frequency: TDS (Taken strictly 30 mins before meals or 1 hour after meals)
Meal_Timing: Empty Stomach (Protein meals impair Levodopa absorption)
Supportive_Medicines: Trihexyphenidyl 2 mg BD (for prominent tremor in young under specialist); Domperidone 10 mg (for nausea); Stool softeners for constipation
Precautions_Contraindications: Rx - specialist supervision required. Levodopa/Carbidopa is an antiparkinson drug; NEVER STOP OR CHANGE DOSE ON YOUR OWN (risk of Neuroleptic Malignant-like syndrome / severe hyperpyrexia). Take Levodopa strictly 30-60 mins before protein-containing meals to prevent competitive amino acid absorption blockade. Monitor for levodopa-induced dyskinesias, orthostatic hypotension, and impulse control disorders
Home_Care_Advice: Take Levodopa strictly on time as scheduled by neurologist; Avoid taking levodopa with high-protein meals (milk, paneer, eggs); Maintain daily walking and balance exercises; Install grab bars in bathrooms and remove home tripping hazards
Lab_Investigations: MRI Brain (rule out vascular parkinsonism or progressive supranuclear palsy); Thyroid Profile; Serum Ceruloplasmin (if onset <40 years to rule out Wilson's disease)
Emergency_Red_Flags: Sudden severe fever, extreme muscle rigidity, and confusion following missed levodopa doses (Emergency Hyperpyrexia Syndrome); Frequent unexplained backward falls; Hallucinations

Primary_Symptoms: Recurrent unprovoked seizures (tonic-clonic convulsions, focal impaired awareness, or absence seizures) due to abnormal hypersynchronous neuronal discharge
Secondary_Symptoms: Post-ictal confusion and drowsiness; Tongue biting; Urinary incontinence; Todd's paresis; Aura prior to seizure
Typical_Duration: Chronic condition requiring long-term anti-seizure medication
Clarifying_Questions: 1. Seizures/doure kis tarah ke aate hain (convulsions, behoshi, ya staring spells)?; 2. Abhi kaunsi antiepileptic dawai chal rahi hai?; 3. Dawai ki koi dose miss to nahi hui?
First_Line_Generic_Drug: Rx - neurologist supervision required (Levetiracetam / Sodium Valproate / Carbamazepine / Lamotrigine / Phenytoin)
Duration_Days: Rx - neurologist supervision required (Minimum 2-5 years seizure-free)
